docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL

Open-source autonomy stack for the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super: GPU perception, state estimation and model-predictive control in ROS 2, STM32N6 flight firmware, simulation and deployment.

Every control path derived, closed-loop and verified in simulation before hardware

Get Started Documentation GitHub

docs.title: Verified in simulation
docs.text:
0.07–0.16 m Waypoint miss, full-stack SIL with unknown wind and +10 % mass 171 / 171 Hexacopter loop checks meeting GM ≥ 6 dB and PM ≥ 45° (current loops ≥ 30°) over ±20 % parameters 0.030 m LiDAR SLAM keyframe ATE on a 52 m loop (SIL) 1–1.5 % Stereo depth error on a ray-traced scene

These figures come from analysis, unit tests and software-in-the-loop runs committed with the code. Hardware-in-the-loop and vehicle evidence is in progress; the stack is not yet flight-ready. See Performance and Verification.

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
🧠 GPU Perception

YOLOv5 (TensorRT), SSD-MobileNet (Triton) and NanoOWL open-vocabulary detection; CenterPoint, PointPillars and BEVFusion on LiDAR; VPI stereo depth with its 1σ uncertainty.

🛩️ Closed-loop UAV Control

15-state error-state Kalman filter, offset-free MPC with MPPI on CUDA near obstacles, flight-mode state machine and mission planner — every loop with its derivation and margins.

🗺️ LiDAR SLAM

LD19 and LPB40B drivers written from their datasheets, PL-ICP scan matching, EKF, pose graph with loop closure and occupancy grid.

🔌 Firmware & micro-ROS

STM32N6 flight control (MPC, PID + ESO, DShot) and camera MCU as native ROS 2 nodes over Ethernet, plus a full-duplex LoRa RC link.

🌙 Thermal Detection

Radiometric MI48 camera, CA-CFAR hot-target detector and multi-target Kalman tracker with thresholds derived from a chosen false-alarm probability.

🚀 Simulation to Deployment

Gazebo hexacopter with a virtual MCU, MAVLink ground-station link and TLS relay, Docker, Kubernetes, Helm and A/B OTA updates.

docs.title: System architecture
docs.text: The stack spans two Jetson boards and the vehicle's microcontrollers on one Ethernet segment; see Architecture for the layers and the closed-loop signal chain.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Simulation (PC)Native (Jetson)Docker Compose (one Jetson)k3s + Helm (two Jetsons) 
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/TNG-Blue/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL.git
cd Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL
sudo apt install ros-humble-ros-gzharmonic libeigen3-dev libyaml-cpp-dev
ROS/build.sh --rosdep -u ros2_hexacopter_gazebo -u ros2_jetowl_bridge
source install/setup.bash
ros2 launch ros2_hexacopter_gazebo hexacopter_sim.launch.py

git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/TNG-Blue/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL.git
cd Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL
ROS/install.sh --distro humble --variant ros-base -y
ROS/build.sh --rosdep
source install/setup.bash
ros2 launch ros2_mission_planner autonomous_mission.launch.py

cd Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL/Docker/compose
docker compose --profile base build ros2_base ros2_base_gpu && docker compose build
docker compose up -d

sudo Kubernetes/cluster/install-master.sh                  # master
sudo Kubernetes/cluster/install-worker.sh --token <token>  # worker
Docker/scripts/build_all.sh --push --tag v0.3.0
Helm/scripts/deploy.sh --set global.imageTag=v0.3.0
make -C Helm test

docs.title: Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL Documentation 2.5.0 October 9, 2026
docs.text: The whole site is now in English and every hand-written page states only what the repository implements or has measured.

docs.title: What's New
docs.text:
• Tutorials rewritten as runnable procedures with measurable checks, each built from the README or design record of the package it uses:
    • Fly Your First Mission — mission files, full-stack SIL with unknown wind and +10 % mass, keep-out detours, in-flight re-tasking (ros2_mission_planner)
    • Calibrate the Stereo Camera — acceptance criteria (row error ≤ 0.5 px), measurement of σ_d, NIS test of the per-pixel Kalman filter (ros2_stereo)
    • Connect the Flight Controller and Sensors — vehicle network, micro-ROS agent, sensor-stream health, Gazebo virtual MCU (ros2_jetowl_bridge)
    • Deploy a Custom Detection Model — ONNX, TensorRT on sm_87, decoder geometry, Kalman tracker (isaac_ros_objectdetection, DeepLearning/)
    • Configure and Validate 2-D LiDAR SLAM — bench calibration and consistency checks (ros2_lidar_slam)
    • Connect a Ground Control Station (replaces Multi-Robot, which described no existing code) — MAVLink budget, acknowledged commands, datalink-loss failsafe, TLS relay (ros2_network_bridge)
    • Deploy the Stack on a Two-Jetson Cluster, Update MCU Firmware Over the Air, Monitor a Running Robot (Docker/, Kubernetes/, Helm/, Server_OTA/, ros2_monitoring)
  • Rewritten from the code: home page, Getting Started, Architecture, Hardware, Development, API Reference, Deployment overview, OTA Updates, Community (support, FAQ, roadmap, contributors) and About (project, license)
  • Roadmap built from the Known limitations of every component, ordered by the verification sequence model → SIL → HIL → bench → vehicle
  • Community → Changelog renders .github/CHANGELOG.md; About → Acknowledgments renders NOTICE.md; CUDA Library pages render CUDA/README.md and its docs/
  • ROS 2 API page lists every .msg, .srv and .action file of the workspace (interfaces: front matter)
  • System overview diagram (home page, Architecture) redrawn from the repositories, with the Remote UAV handset, the Android console and the closed control loop
  • Hardware pages, architecture and diagrams name the STM32N6 as the hexacopter sensor MCU in place of the Arduino Portenta H7, which the project no longer uses
  • Translated to English: Remote UAV README and design records, the ROS 2 node flowchart, the OpenMV API audit, and the submodule documents snapshotted from JetOwl_FlightControl and JetOwl_Vision

docs.title: Bug Fixes
docs.text:
• Removed figures that were never measured (35+ FPS, < 20 ms, 98.5 % accuracy, 10–15 W, 95 % navigation success) and features that do not exist (YOLOv8 pipeline, Firebase, Prometheus and Grafana, multi-robot coordination, a public Helm repository); the home page now shows SIL results with their conditions
  • Removed contact channels that do not exist (Discord, Twitter, YouTube, @tngblue.com addresses) and placeholder team and contact pages; support goes through GitHub and the maintainer address of SECURITY.md and NOTICE.md
  • Removed the Cloud Integration page, which described no code in the repository; App Engine deployment of the OTA server is on Server OTA → Deployment
  • CUDA pages described an unbuilt VPI module as available and quoted unmeasured speed-ups
  • Root README.md: build from the repository root with ROS/build.sh, documentation URL, package table with all 13 packages; Server_OTA/README.md rewritten without the invented load-test and fleet statistics, and with its missing authentication stated

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text: • Snapshot pages of the submodules are refreshed by hand after a submodule bump

docs.title: Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL Documentation 2.4.0 October 9, 2026
docs.text: The site now covers every component in the repository and is rendered from the code's own documentation, so it cannot drift from it.

docs.title: What's New
docs.text:
• Pages rendered from the code: a page whose front matter names source: <path> renders that file at build time (hook Scripts/mkdocs_hooks/source_pages.py). 39 pages now come from the package READMEs and design records, with their node graphs, topic contracts and control-design records:
    • ROS 2 modules: Control System, Flight Controller, Mission Planner, JetOwl Bridge, Network Bridge, RF Spectrum, Object Detection, LiDAR AI Perception (+ installation and Isaac ROS integration), LiDAR SLAM, Stereo Vision, Night Vision, Qt Dashboard, Monitoring
    • System Node Graph: every ROS 2 node of the three repositories on one diagram
    • Simulation (new): Gazebo overview, hexacopter plugin, control core, description, MCU emulator
    • Firmware (new): Microcontroller overview, Remote UAV ground controller with its link design, signal chain, UI and wiring
    • Deep Learning (new): overview, architecture, mathematics, installation
    • MATLAB & Simulink (new), MAVLink Relay Server, Examples, DFRobot I2C multiplexer
    • Development: Control Design Standard (.claude/rules/control-systems.md), Repository Tests
  • Submodule snapshots: 14 pages for JetOwl Flight Control (README, control design, architecture, micro-ROS, LoRa RC link, OTA), JetOwl Vision (README, camera control loop, micro-ROS) and the JetbotNanoOWL Android app (README, estimation design, MAVLink link, Isaac ROS integration, 3-D UAV console), generated by Scripts/mkdocs_hooks/snapshot_submodules.py because the docs workflow does not check the submodules out
  • New hand-written pages: Sensor Fusion & Estimation (where each estimator lives and what it fuses) and Model Training & Notebooks (Train_Pytorch/, Notebooks/)
  • ROS2 Modules index, Documentation index and home page list the 13 real packages in Source/; the index has a UAV signal-chain diagram built from the packages' topic contracts
  • Site features (Material 9.7): navigation.instant.prefetch, navigation.instant.preview, content.footnote.tooltips, grid cards, and a glossary (Docs/includes/abbreviations.md) that turns ESKF, MPC, NIS, CFAR, … into tooltips on every page
  • Navigation: Documentation tab grouped into UAV Stack, Perception, Operator Tools, Simulation, Firmware, Deep Learning, MATLAB & Simulink, Mobile App, Examples & Utilities

docs.title: Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL Documentation 2.3.0 September 25, 2026
docs.text: Display fixes for the published site, a rewritten Features page, and a build that now fails on the problems it used to publish.

docs.title: What's New
docs.text:
• Features page (Docs/home/features.md):
    • Rewritten around the actual subsystems (perception, estimation and control, firmware, simulation, deployment), each card linking to its documentation page
    • Removed the pricing-style Comparison Table, the placeholder buttons (href="#") and the invented statistics
    • Added the sensor → filter → estimator → controller → actuator chain with its equations, a Recent updates timeline taken from merged PRs, and a guide to the site's own features
  • Site features:
    • Tag index page (Docs/tags.md); 69 pages tagged by subsystem
    • Colour scheme follows the operating system (auto / light / dark toggle)
    • Image lightbox (glightbox), code-line selection, pruned navigation, right-hand table of contents
    • Keyboard shortcuts: ? help, d colour scheme, h home, g Getting Started - now correct under the site's sub-path
    • MathJax is loaded only on pages that contain maths

docs.title: Bug Fixes
docs.text:
• site_url pointed at …/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL/, but the site is served from …/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL-Docs/: the 404 page loaded no CSS or JS and canonical URLs, sitemap and social cards were wrong
  • Removed polyfill.io (domain taken over in 2024; returned 403)
  • Removed the placeholder Google Analytics property, whose cookie-consent overlay covered every first visit; its Manage settings button rendered blank
  • Layout: component CSS used rem as if 1 rem = 16 px, while Material uses 20-24 px, so headline numbers broke mid-value (98. / 5%) and cards overflowed; all component sizes are now em-based and numbers never wrap
  • Inline-code styling also applied to code blocks and shifted them against the line numbers; line numbers are now opt-in so copied commands never contain them
  • JavaScript:
    • Two scripts animated the same counters at once and garbled values such as 10-15W; one idempotent counter remains and restores the original text
    • Handlers re-ran on every instant navigation and duplicated labels and toasts
    • pwa.js threw Failed to construct 'URL' on every page; the broken, cache-first service worker, the manifest (10 missing icons) and the floating button that duplicated back to top were removed, and old service-worker copies are unregistered
    • Custom handlers overrode Material's own colour-scheme persistence, TOC highlighting and back-to-top button
    • MathJax.typesetPromise is not a function race on first load
  • Mermaid: switched from the mermaid2 plugin to Material's built-in renderer (re-renders after instant navigation, follows the colour scheme); fixed parse errors in architecture/network.md and architecture/overview.md
  • Links: 191 broken internal links fixed - raw-HTML hrefs written relative to the .md file instead of the page URL, *.md hrefs in raw HTML, links to tutorials that do not exist yet (now point to the page that covers the topic or are marked Planned), and links outside Docs/ (now GitHub URLs)
  • Contributor image from contrib.rocks returned 404 for the private repository
  • Logo and favicon were a 467 KB, 628×412 PNG loaded on every page; now 30 KB / 7 KB

docs.title: Build and CI (.github/workflows/docs_deploy.yaml)
docs.text:
• mkdocs build --strict | tee always succeeded because the pipe hid the exit code ("Aborted with 175 warnings in strict mode!" was followed by "✓ … strict mode"); the build now runs with pipefail and fails on any warning
  • Social-card dependencies (mkdocs-material[imaging]) were never installed; all build dependencies now come from Docs/requirements.txt
  • Filtering moved from copying Docs/ into build_temp/ to exclude_docs in mkdocs.yml, so page revision dates come from real git history
  • New Scripts/check_docs_links.py checks every internal link and asset in the built site the way a browser resolves it, and fails the build on a broken one
  • OTA preview links in the job summary pointed at the wrong host path

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
• Material requests api.github.com/repos/…/releases/latest for the repository badge; the source repository is private, so the request returns 404 and the badge shows no version. It is harmless and cached per session.
  • /ota-preview/ exists only after the deploy job merges the OTA build; it is ignored by the link check and 404s under mkdocs serve.

docs.title: Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL Documentation 2.2.0 September 20, 2026
docs.text: The documentation site is now a dual build: the MkDocs site and the Server_OTA web interface are built separately and published together, so the OTA dashboard can be viewed from the documentation.

docs.title: What's New
docs.text:
Updates including:

  • Documentation deployment (.github/workflows/docs_deploy.yaml):

    • New build-ota-preview job builds a static copy of the OTA Server dashboard in parallel with the MkDocs build
    • deploy-to-public-repo merges both artifacts and publishes the OTA UI at /ota-preview/ of Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL-Docs
    • Deployment fails instead of publishing a partial site if either half is missing
    • Workflow now also triggers on changes to Server_OTA/web/** and Server_OTA/scripts/build_preview.sh

  • New page Docs/documentation/deployment/ota-web-ui.md:

    • Added to the navigation under Documentation → Deployment → OTA Web Interface
    • Embeds the live dashboard and links to a full-screen view
    • Documents the simulated API contract, the dual-build pipeline and how to reproduce both halves locally
    • Deployment index gained a matching card

  • New top-level section Server OTA (Docs/server-ota/):

    • Added as a navigation tab between Documentation and Tutorials
    • index.md — service overview, runtime limits table, fleet update flow, repository layout and quick start
    • architecture.md — packages, request pipeline, the 5-slot concurrency semaphore, runtime/timeout budget, firmware metadata derivation rules and the current implementation gaps
    • api.md — every route with exact payloads, status codes and a device-side polling example
    • deployment.md — local binary, Docker image, App Engine Standard/Flexible, Cloud Build and the OTA CI pipeline
    • The OTA Web Interface page is reachable from this section as well

  • Fixed card links on Docs/documentation/deployment/index.md:

    • Buttons inside the raw-HTML cards pointed at *.md targets, which MkDocs does not rewrite; with use_directory_urls they 404 on the published site
    • Now use directory URLs (docker/, kubernetes/, helm/, ota/, cloud/)

  • New builder Server_OTA/scripts/build_preview.sh:

    • Rewrites the server's absolute /static/... asset paths for static hosting
    • Injects Server_OTA/web/static/js/preview-demo.js, which answers /api/stats, /api/health and /api/firmware/list with demo payloads that follow the Go handler contracts (models.APIResponse, models.FirmwareInfo, models.HealthStatus)
    • --serve [PORT] serves the result locally; the build self-verifies and exits non-zero on a missing asset, flag or shim

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
• The published preview is read-only: upload, download and delete need a running Go server and are replaced by an explanatory notification.
  • mkdocs serve alone does not produce the preview; run build_preview.sh --output site/ota-preview to assemble the full site locally.

docs.title: Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL Documentation 2.1.0 September 15, 2026
docs.text: Documentation now targets a single compute platform: the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super.

docs.title: What's New
docs.text:
Updates including:

  • Platform documentation:

    • Declared the Jetson Orin Nano Super (8GB) the project's only supported board
    • Added a compute-platform specification table to the root README.md (1024-core Ampere GPU, sm_87, 6-core Cortex-A78AE @ 1.7 GHz, 8GB LPDDR5 @ 102 GB/s, 67 INT8 TOPS in MAXN SUPER, 7/15/25 W modes)
    • Documented that MAXN SUPER requires JetPack 6.2 or newer; on JetPack 6.1 the same board runs at 40 TOPS / 68 GB/s

  • Toolchain versions across all guides:

    • JetPack 5.1.2 / 4.6.x → JetPack 6.2+
    • Ubuntu 20.04 → Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (L4T 36.4.3+)
    • CUDA 11.4 / 11.8 / 12.2 → CUDA 12.6, build target sm_87
    • TensorRT 8.⅝.6 → TensorRT 10.3+; cuDNN 8.x → cuDNN 9.3+
    • Python 3.8 → Python 3.10

  • Corrections to Docs/documentation/hardware/jetson.md:

    • CPU was listed as 8 cores @ 2.0 GHz; the Orin Nano Super has 6 cores @ 1.7 GHz
    • Power-mode IDs were documented as 0 = MAXN; on this board under JetPack 6.2 they are 0 = 15W, 1 = 7W, 2 = MAXN SUPER
    • Storage was listed as 128GB UFS 3.1; the developer kit provides microSD plus an M.2 Key M NVMe slot

  • Issue and security templates:

    • .github/SECURITY.md and SECURITY.template.md list JetPack 6.2+ as fully supported, 6.0/6.1 as security-only, and 5.x and older as unsupported
    • Bug report, question and installation templates collect JetPack 6.2, CUDA 12.6, and the active nvpmodel power mode

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text:
• Platform support: the original Jetson Nano, Xavier NX and AGX Xavier are documented as unsupported.
    • Old: Jetson Nano (JetPack 4.6.x) listed as "security only"
    • New: not supported — JetPack 4.x cannot run ROS2 Humble natively and the CUDA kernels here target sm_87 (Jetson Nano is Maxwell sm_53)
    • Migration: move to a Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit and flash JetPack 6.2 or newer

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
• Benchmark tables in Utilities/SenXor_Jetson/README.md and Source/ROS2_Lidar_AI_Solution/CUDA-Utilities/README.md were originally measured on the Jetson Nano. They are annotated as legacy figures and kept as a conservative upper bound until the suites are re-run on sm_87; no Orin Nano Super numbers have been invented in their place.
  • Per-package CHANGELOG.md files retain their original Jetson Nano references, since published release history is not rewritten.
  • Jetson AGX Orin and Orin NX share the same Ampere sm_87 architecture, so builds are expected to work, but they remain untested and undocumented here.

docs.title: Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL Documentation 2.0.0 February 4, 2026
docs.text: Comprehensive documentation suite for Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL platform with complete API reference, tutorials, and deployment guides.

docs.title: What's New
docs.text:
This release introduces a complete professional documentation suite replacing ad-hoc guides with enterprise-grade, well-structured documentation covering all aspects of the platform:

  • API Reference Documentation:

    • Complete C++ API with motor control, camera interface, IMU sensor, object detection
    • Pythonic API for rapid development with Jupyter notebook support
    • ROS2 Interfaces with 15+ message types, 10+ service definitions, action types
    • REST API with 20+ endpoints and multi-language client examples (Python, JavaScript, cURL)
    • 40+ working code examples across all APIs
    • ~54KB comprehensive documentation with implementation details

  • Tutorial Series - Learning Paths:

    • Basic Tutorials (9 total): First Mission, Camera Calibration, Sensor Setup - covering beginner operations
    • Advanced Tutorials (3 total): Custom Models, SLAM Configuration, Multi-Robot Setup - intermediate to advanced
    • Deployment Tutorials (3 total): Production Setup, OTA Integration, Monitoring & Maintenance - professional deployment
    • 2,000+ lines of tutorial documentation with 75+ code examples
    • Estimated learning time: 10.5 hours total for complete path
    • Step-by-step instructions with verification checklists

  • Deployment Documentation:

    • Docker Deployment: Multi-stage Dockerfiles, docker-compose with 8 services, GPU integration, registry management
    • Kubernetes Deployment: Cluster setup, manifests (deployments, services, StatefulSet), kustomization, RBAC, monitoring
    • Helm Charts: Parameterized charts with 3 environment profiles (dev/prod/edge), dependency management, templating
    • OTA Updates: Update server infrastructure, staged rollout strategies, automatic rollback, fleet management
    • Cloud Integration: AWS (EC2, RDS, S3, CloudFormation), Google Cloud (Compute Engine, Firestore, Pub/Sub), Azure (VMs, Cosmos DB)
    • ~61KB documentation with 45+ code examples for 5 deployment methods
    • Covers 3 major cloud platforms with complete CLI commands and infrastructure templates

  • ROS2 Modules Documentation (11 modules):

    • Object Detection with YOLOv8 integration and real-time performance metrics
    • SLAM & Navigation with visual-inertial fusion and loop closure detection
    • Control System with PID tuning and motor feedback
    • Sensor Fusion using Extended Kalman Filter
    • Night Vision with thermal imaging and RGB-thermal fusion
    • Network Bridge supporting WiFi 5GHz, LoRa, 4G/LTE
    • Monitoring with real-time system health tracking
    • RF Spectrum Analysis with interference detection
    • Stereo Vision for 3D perception with point cloud generation
    • Microcontroller Integration with ARM Cortex-M7 real-time scheduling
    • ~4,870 lines of documentation with 75+ code examples and 20+ diagrams
    • Performance benchmarks and configuration parameters

  • CUDA Vision Documentation:

    • Complete CUDA acceleration library documentation
    • GPU kernel implementations for real-time vision processing
    • Performance optimization guide with benchmarks
    • Integration examples with ROS2 pipeline
    • 450+ lines of comprehensive API documentation

  • Doxygen Configuration Documentation:

    • Doxyfile.in template with CMake substitution explained
    • DoxygenLayout.xml configuration for HTML generation
    • Complete explanation of Doxygen purpose and workflow
    • Practical guide with step-by-step instructions
    • Code comment examples for C++ and Python
    • ~4,000 lines of Doxygen education and practical guide

docs.title: Documentation Statistics
docs.text:
This release provides comprehensive coverage with measurable improvements:

  • Total Documentation: 6 main sections covering API, tutorials, and deployment
  • File Count: 30+ markdown files organized by function
  • Total Content: 150+ KB of high-quality documentation
  • Code Examples: 200+ working examples in C++, Python, JavaScript, Bash, YAML
  • Diagrams: 20+ architectural diagrams and flowcharts
  • Configuration Templates: 50+ ready-to-use configuration files
  • Coverage: All major features and use cases documented

docs.title: Quality Improvements
docs.text:
• Structured Learning Paths: Three progressive paths (beginner → advanced → professional)
  • Cross-Referenced Documentation: All sections linked with "Next Steps" navigation
  • Production-Ready Examples: All code examples tested and executable
  • Search Optimized: Well-formatted markdown with clear headings for easy navigation
  • Consistency: Enterprise-grade formatting and terminology throughout
  • Completeness: No missing sections - all APIs and features documented

docs.title: Performance Improvements
docs.text:
Documentation generation and delivery:

  • Fast Navigation: Cross-referenced links enable jumping between related topics
  • Searchable Content: ~150KB of indexed documentation
  • Offline Capable: HTML can be hosted locally or offline
  • Quick Reference: Tabulated APIs for rapid lookup
  • Code-First Approach: Examples first, theory second for faster learning

docs.title: Platform Support
docs.text:
This documentation supports and documents:

  • Development Environments:

    • Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (primary)
    • Windows with WSL2
    • macOS
    • Jetson Orin Nano (target device)

  • Deployment Targets:

    • Single robot (Docker)
    • Multi-robot (Kubernetes)
    • Cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure)
    • Edge deployments (Helm)
    • Fleet management (OTA)

  • Languages & Frameworks:

    • C++ (native API)
    • Python (high-level API)
    • ROS2 Humble (middleware)
    • REST HTTP (language-agnostic)
    • Docker (containerization)
    • Kubernetes (orchestration)

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
This release has the following known limitations:

  • Documentation assumes basic knowledge of robotics and Linux
  • MATLAB documentation section not yet completed (planned for v2.1.0)
  • Some advanced cloud integration patterns documented but not fully tested
  • GPU-specific documentation focused on NVIDIA Jetson architecture
  • REST API examples primarily focus on curl and Python (other languages will be added)

docs.title: Version Format
docs.text:
Follow semantic versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH

  • MAJOR: Major documentation restructuring, complete section rewrites, significant coverage additions
  • MINOR: New documentation sections, new tutorials, new API coverage, new deployment guides
  • PATCH: Documentation corrections, typo fixes, example updates, clarification improvements

docs.title: Release Entry Format
docs.text:
## Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL Documentation X.Y.Z Month Day, Year

Brief overview of documentation changes in this release.

### What's New

Documentation updates including:

* **Section Name**:
    * Feature or update description
    * Key improvements with metrics
    * User-facing benefits

### Quality Improvements

* Specific improvements to documentation quality
* Better examples or explanations
* Enhanced organization

### Platform Support

Platforms and features covered in documentation

### Limitations

Known limitations in current documentation

### Issues Addressed

Documentation improvements addressing user feedback

docs.title: Writing Guidelines
docs.text:
When to Update: - Addition of new APIs or modules - New tutorial series or guides - New deployment strategies or platforms - Major documentation reorganization - Significant content improvements or corrections - Performance documentation updates - Security improvements to documentation

What to Include: - Clear description of documentation additions - Technical accuracy and completeness - Code examples demonstrating features - Cross-references to related documentation - Performance metrics and benchmarks - Platform requirements and support - Known limitations and workarounds

What to Exclude: - Minor typo fixes or formatting - Internal documentation reorganization without content changes - Temporary or staging documentation - Outdated reference materials

Structure Your Entries: - Group documentation by functional area or topic - Lead with most significant additions - Include specific metrics (number of examples, lines of documentation) - Reference specific files or sections - Use clear technical terminology - Mention target audience (beginner, advanced, professional)

Language and Tone: - Use clear, professional technical language - Focus on completeness and accuracy - Be specific with numbers and metrics - Mention compatibility and platform support - Use active voice for improvements - Highlight practical benefits for users

docs.title: Breaking Changes Documentation
docs.text:
When significant documentation structure changes occur:

### Documentation Structure Changes

* **API Reference Reorganization**:
    * Old: Combined C++ and Python APIs
    * New: Separate sections with dedicated examples
    * Migration: See API reference index for new structure
    * Reason: Improved clarity for language-specific users

* **Tutorial Path Restructuring**:
    * Old: Linear progression without clear difficulty levels
    * New: Three progressive paths (beginner/advanced/professional)
    * Migration: See tutorials/index.md for new organization
    * Benefit: Faster learning for appropriate skill levels

Maintained by: Isaac ROS Jetbot NanoOWL Documentation Team Project Repository: GitHub Documentation Home: Main Index Issue Tracker: GitHub Issues

For questions about documentation or to report issues, please open an issue on GitHub or contact the documentation team through the project channels.

docs.title: About the Project
docs.text: Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL is an open-source autonomy stack for small robots and a coaxial X12 hexacopter built around the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super. It combines GPU-accelerated perception (Isaac ROS, NanoOWL, stereo, LiDAR), state estimation and model-predictive control in ROS 2 Humble, embedded flight-control firmware on STM32N6 microcontrollers, simulation in Gazebo Harmonic, and the tooling to deploy, update and monitor it all.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
Every control path is derived, not tuned. From sensor to actuator, each stage — filter, estimator, controller, actuator interface — carries its model, units, sample rate and stability argument, and the loop is closed wherever a sensor exists. The Control Design Standard makes this a review requirement.

Claims come with evidence. Performance figures in this documentation come from tests and simulations committed with the code, with their conditions. What has not been measured is said to be unmeasured; see Performance and Verification.

The documentation is the code's own. Component pages are rendered at build time from the README and design record next to the code, so they cannot drift from it.

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text: Repository Content Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL ROS 2 packages, CUDA and deep-learning libraries, simulation, MATLAB/Simulink, ground-controller firmware, deployment, OTA server, MAVLink relay, this site JetOwl_FlightControl flight-control firmware for the STM32N657 (TrustZone, FreeRTOS, micro-ROS, OTA) JetOwl_Vision camera firmware for the STM32N655 with an IMX335 sensor JetbotNanoOWL Android operator console

docs.title: Status
docs.text: The stack is under active development and is not certified for flight. Components are verified by unit tests and software-in-the-loop simulation; hardware-in-the-loop, bench and vehicle evidence is in progress (see the Roadmap). It is intended for development and research. Operating it on a vehicle requires your own safety validation and compliance with the aviation rules of your jurisdiction.

docs.title: HOW TO READ THIS FILE
docs.text:
The Project spans several subsystems, each with its own dependency set: ROS 2 packages, CUDA and TensorRT libraries, MATLAB/Simulink models, microcontroller firmware, an Android client, a Go OTA server, Kubernetes/Helm deployment assets and an MkDocs documentation site. Components are grouped by subsystem below.

  • Bundled — source is vendored in this repository (including Git submodules) and is redistributed with it.
  • Linked — resolved at build time from the platform (JetPack, rosdep, apt, pip) and linked into Project binaries; not redistributed here.
  • Runtime / tooling — invoked as a separate process, driver or service, or used only to build the documentation; not linked into Project binaries and not redistributed here.

License identifiers reflect each upstream project's stated license at the time of writing. Before redistributing a build, verify them against the LICENSE file in the version you actually ship — particularly for submodules, which track upstream branches.

docs.title: Server_OTA (HTTP)
docs.text:
The OTA server stores firmware packages, serves them to the MCUs with resumable downloads and records what each MCU reports.

Method Path Purpose GET /api/ota/manifest?device=<id> newest valid release for jetowl_fc or jetowl_vision, as key=value text GET /download?file=<file> firmware download; Range: bytes=n- → 206 + Content-Range POST /upload store a package; .fw files are checked (header, SHA-256, name) and never overwritten POST /api/ota/report?device=&version=&state=&detail= MCU state report GET /api/ota/devices last report of every MCU GET /api/firmware/list, /api/firmware/info?file= catalogue and metadata GET /api/stats, /api/health counters and liveness

Full reference with payloads and status codes: Server OTA API. The MCU-side client and the A/B boot logic are described in the firmware OTA document.

docs.title: MAVLink relay (TLS)
docs.text:
1. TLS 1.2+ to the relay (default port 5790).

  2. One line, ≤ 512 bytes, within 5 s:

    MAVRELAY/1 <vehicle|observer> <robot-id> <token>

  3. The relay answers OK , or ERR auth / ERR malformed / ERR full and closes.

  4. Then raw MAVLink v1/v2 frames flow both ways; the relay forwards whole frames only.

An observer can only send a HEARTBEAT to the vehicle — never a command. Details, security model and deployment: MAVLink Relay Server.

docs.title: MAVLink ground-station link
docs.text: ros2_network_bridge speaks MAVLink v2 over UDP, TCP, serial or the relay. Supported commands, telemetry streams, rates and the link-loss policy are listed in Network Bridge.

docs.title: MCU sensor link (UDP)
docs.text: CRC-32 framed, little-endian datagrams from the sensor MCU (or the Gazebo virtual MCU) to the Jetson on port 9870, with time synchronisation on 9871. Header: magic 0x4254, version, type, payload length, device id, flags, sequence number, MCU measurement time [µs]; frame types IMU, GNSS, ENCODER, ATTITUDE, HEARTBEAT, IMU_INFO, TIME_SYNC_REQUEST/RESPONSE. Full wire format: JetOwl Bridge — Wire format.

docs.title: RC link (LoRa)
docs.text: Frame layout, authentication (AES-128-CMAC) and replay protection of the Remote UAV ↔ FC link: Link Design §6.

docs.text: Conventions (frames, QoS, acknowledgement) are described in ROS 2 Integration; the complete wiring of all nodes is the System Node Graph.

# Lidar 3D track augmented with an open-vocabulary semantic label obtained by

#
# label_probabilities is the posterior p(c | z_1:k) maintained by a recursive
# Bayesian estimator with fading memory; see docs/isaac_ros_integration.md.
std_msgs/Header header

uint32 track_id                    # Track ID inherited from object_tracker_node
uint8 track_state                  # 0=TENTATIVE, 1=CONFIRMED, 2=LOST

string label                       # MAP label, "unknown" when below min_probability
float64 label_probability          # Posterior probability of the MAP label [0-1]
float64[] label_probabilities      # Full posterior, indexed as the vocabulary
float64 entropy                    # Shannon entropy of the posterior (nats)
uint32 observation_count           # Number of 2D observations fused so far

# Camera association evidence for the current cycle
bool matched                       # true when fused with a 2D detection this cycle
float64 match_iou                  # IoU between projected and detected 2D boxes

docs.title: Ground rules
docs.text:
• Participation is governed by the Code of Conduct.
  • First-time contributors sign the CLA by commenting I have read and agree to the CLA on their first pull request.
  • Changes to control, estimation or firmware code carry their derivation, units, sample rate and stability argument; see the Control Design Standard.

docs.title: CHANGELOG
docs.text:
Source

This page is rendered from .github/CHANGELOG.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in .github/.

All notable changes to Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL will be documented in this file.

docs.title: What's New
docs.text:
• k3s and load-balancing detail in the overview: control plane on the master (why one server), the kube-scheduler score and the chart's spread / GPU anti-affinity / co-location terms, the resource budget (requests against allocatable per board), the failover timeline (20 + 5 + 10 s) with preemption by PriorityClass, DDS on the host network, the 1 GbE link budget and MetalLB; every ROS 2 pod carries its PriorityClass and CPU / memory requests from the Helm values.
  • Docs/images/Jetson_ROS2_Cluster.svg redrawn from the repositories, generated by Scripts/diagrams/system_overview.py: operators (JetbotNanoOWL Android console, QGroundControl, operator laptop), the Remote UAV handset and its full-duplex LoRa link, off-board services (Server_Relay, build machine, GNSS), the two-Jetson k3s cluster with every ROS 2 node, the STM32N6 flight controller and camera, the sensors, and the closed control loop highlighted.

docs.title: Bug Fixes
docs.text: • The previous diagram showed components that do not exist (Portenta H7, publisher/subscriber autoscaling, Prometheus/Grafana, ArgoCD, SX1276 radios, cert-manager) and wrong addresses.

docs.title: STM32N6 replaces the Portenta H7 October 9, 2026
What's New
docs.text:
• The hexacopter sensor MCU is an STM32N6 (Cortex-M55, lwIP) instead of the Arduino Portenta H7. The UDP sensor link is unchanged: protocol.h/protocol.c are plain C99 and the STM32N6 CRC unit computes the same CRC-32/ISO-HDLC (DEFAULT_CRC32_POLY, input bit reversal by byte, output reversal, init and final XOR 0xFFFFFFFF).
  • ros2_jetowl_bridge config/sensor_link.yaml: the clock-sync Allan deviation is now stated for an STM32N6 timer clocked from the HSE crystal (still an assumption to measure); the MCU address 192.168.1.103 is unchanged.
  • Documentation, diagrams, issue and pull-request templates, and the Gazebo virtual-MCU comments name the STM32N6. The Portenta H7 and breakout schematics are removed from Docs/datasheet/.
  • Claude Code configuration: the microcontroller agent and the stm32-cube-setup skill target the STM32N6 (four CubeMX contexts, RIF, pins and clocks of the JetOwl flight controller); the dual-core-sync skill (Portenta M7/M4) is replaced by stm32n6-trustzone.

docs.title: What's New
docs.text:
• Documentation site 2.5.0: every page in English; tutorials rewritten as runnable procedures with measurable checks (missions in SIL, stereo calibration, sensor bring-up, custom models, SLAM, ground station, two-Jetson cluster, OTA, monitoring); Community and About rebuilt from the repository's own records. Details: Docs/CHANGELOG.md.
  • Remote UAV firmware documents, the ROS 2 node flowchart and the OpenMV API audit translated to English.

docs.title: Bug Fixes
docs.text:
• Unmeasured performance figures, non-existent features and contact channels removed from the site, README.md and Server_OTA/README.md.
  • README.md quick start builds from the repository root with ROS/build.sh and links the published documentation.

docs.title: Documentation site rendered from the code October 9, 2026
What's New
docs.text:
• The MkDocs site covers every component: 39 pages are rendered at build time from the package READMEs and design records (source: front matter, hook Scripts/mkdocs_hooks/source_pages.py) and 14 pages are snapshots of the firmware and Android submodules (Scripts/mkdocs_hooks/snapshot_submodules.py). New sections: Simulation, Firmware, Deep Learning, MATLAB & Simulink, Mobile App, Examples & Utilities, MAVLink Relay Server, Control Design Standard. Details: Docs/CHANGELOG.md.
  • Material 9.7 features: link prefetch, instant previews, footnote tooltips, glossary tooltips.

docs.title: Bug Fixes
docs.text:
• ROS 2 module pages described packages that do not exist; they now render the real packages.
  • Broken links in MATLAB/README.md and Utilities/DFRobot_I2C_Multiplexer/README.md.

docs.title: UAV 3-D map for the JetbotNanoOWL console October 9, 2026
What's New
docs.text:
• ros2_network_bridge 0.5.0 sends the planar LD19 scan as MAVLink OBSTACLE_DISTANCE (#330):

    • 360 one-degree sectors in BODY_FRD, in five messages per scan;
    • mount yaw and offset applied;
    • de-skewed to the scan stamp with the body twist;
    • decimated to fit the link budget, n = ⌈B_scan / (u_max C − B_streams)⌉.

    The console places each fan with the 6-DoF pose at its own timestamp and stacks the fans into a 3-D voxel map, so the UAV is mapped in 3-D rather than as a floor plan. * jetbot_console.launch.py gains three arguments: scan_topic, scan_mount_yaw_deg, and link_loss_action (default none; set rth for a UAV also flown from a GCS). * Tests: OBSTACLE_DISTANCE byte-exact against pymavlink, sector geometry, mount and no-return handling, de-skew, and budget decimation. The package now has 42 gtest cases.

docs.title: MAVLink relay: robot and console on different networks October 9, 2026
What's New
docs.text:
• Server_Relay/ (new; Go 1.21, standard library only) joins a robot and its consoles when they do not share a network. Both ends dial out over TLS, so any NAT is crossed, the carrier's CGNAT included:

    • per-robot, per-role tokens, stored only as SHA-256 hashes and compared in constant time;
    • frame-level forwarding;
    • observers can send nothing but a verified HEARTBEAT, so an observer credential can never command the robot.

    Tests cover TLS, the policy, back-pressure and timeouts (go test -race). Deployment: Dockerfile and README. CI: relay-server-ci.yml. * ros2_network_bridge 0.4.0: transport: relay (OpenSSL, CA or SPKI pin, token from a file, exponential back-off), with launch arguments in jetbot_console.launch.py. * JetbotNanoOWL connects as an observer through the same relay. It measures each fix's delay from its timestamp and carries the fix to the present before fusing it.

docs.title: ROS2 Network Bridge: ODOMETRY with covariances for the JetbotNanoOWL console October 9, 2026
What's New
docs.text:
• ros2_network_bridge 0.3.0 sends MAVLink ODOMETRY (#331): pose in LOCAL_NED and twist in BODY_FRD, with both 6×6 covariances mapped from the ROS conventions. The pose covariance goes through J = blockdiag(T, E⁻¹T); this is checked against central differences. An all-zero or non-finite covariance is sent as unknown, never as a perfect measurement.
  • jetbot_console.launch.py connects the Jetbot graph (/odometry) to the JetbotNanoOWL Android console. The console fuses ODOMETRY in its EKF and sends only a MAV_TYPE_LOG heartbeat, so it never acts as the GCS.
  • Details and the bandwidth budget: Source/ROS2_Network_Bridge/CHANGELOG.md.

docs.title: ROS2 Lidar AI Solution: NVIDIA code as submodules October 9, 2026
What's New
docs.text:
• Source/ROS2_Lidar_AI_Solution no longer carries copies of NVIDIA's code. NVIDIA-AI-IOT/ Lidar_AI_Solution is a git submodule at Lidar_AI_Solution/, next to CUDA-LidarAI/ (its nested CUDA-PointPillars is checked out at the upstream tip with --remote), built unmodified by the new standalone CMake project CUDA-LidarAI (lidar_ai_core, targets lidar_ai::*); the ROS 2 nodes link those targets. The libraries can be built and installed separately and the package built against them (-DUSE_INSTALLED_LIDAR_AI_CORE=ON).
  • The removed copy was stale and partly broken (empty source files, Git LFS pointers instead of libspconv, a missing upstream bounds check).
  • cuda_utilities: the duplicated ComputeCentroid is replaced by the GPU implementation, renamed ComputeCentroidDevice (device result, stream-ordered) plus ComputeCentroidHost, with intensity weighting and NaN/Inf rejection; pointcloud_preprocessor_node, isaac_ros_semantic_overlay_node and the CUDA-Utilities tests link again.
  • ros2_lidar_ai_solution 0.6.0; see Source/ROS2_Lidar_AI_Solution/CHANGELOG.md for the migration and the platform support of each component.

docs.title: Shell scripts: consistent interface and fixes October 9, 2026
What's New
docs.text:
Every repository shell script now has a usage header (purpose, options, environment, exit status), --help, strict mode (set -euo pipefail), quoted expansions, argument validation and a clean ShellCheck run; executable scripts carry the executable bit.

  • Scripts/shell/common.sh: no longer changes the caller's shell options or IFS, can be sourced twice, adds die and require_command; warnings go to stderr; honours NO_COLOR.
  • CMakePreBuild.sh: configures CUDA/CMakeLists.txt (it pointed at the repository root, which has none); build and install in CUDA/build, CUDA/install.
  • jetbot-nanoowl: a failing build-all step now stops the build instead of being reported as an unknown command; setup prints source commands (eval "$(jetbot-nanoowl setup)"); --config without a path and add-to-path without ~/.bashrc no longer crash.
  • ROS/: tag.sh selects the distribution non-interactively (--distro, $ROS_DISTRO, or the only one installed); install.sh installs ROS 2 Humble/Jazzy from the official ros2-apt-source with Ubuntu-release checks; build.sh builds the repository workspace (-p, -u, --rosdep, --test); run.sh lists workspace nodes and forwards Ctrl-C to nodes started in parallel.
  • Docker/scripts/docker_manager.sh 3.0.0 drives Docker/compose/docker-compose.yml (build, up, logs, exec, ...); the Dockerfiles it referenced no longer exist. ros2_build.sh builds any src/ workspace; its --symlink-install and --parallel-workers were passed to CMake because they came after --cmake-args.
  • Configs/run-setup.sh implements its steps (NVMe mount, nvidia default runtime, Docker data-root, swap, GUI, docker group, nvpmodel, ROS 2, NetworkManager) with --dry-run, --yes and --only. It parses .env instead of sourcing it: KEY=value# comment lines were executed as commands. .env comments moved to their own lines.
  • Scripts/install-firebase-sdk.sh 2.0.0: honours --jobs/BUILD_JOBS; no prompt in unattended runs (--reconfigure); deletes a /usr/local Abseil only with --remove-system-abseil.
  • Source/ROS2_Qt/configure_firebase.sh: validates input, hides the API key while typing, writes .env with mode 600; Source/ROS2_Qt/.env is git-ignored.
  • Server_OTA/scripts/build.sh builds static linux/amd64, linux/arm64 (Jetson) and linux/arm/7 binaries; run.sh starts the binary for the host or falls back to go run.
  • Scripts/dependencies/install_vpi3_x86_64.sh adds NVIDIA's signing key and picks the repository and Python binding matching the Ubuntu release.

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text:
• Docker/scripts/docker_manager.sh: services are the compose service names (docker_manager.sh list), e.g. ros2_stereo instead of stereo.
  • ROS/build.sh: ROS 1 (catkin) is no longer handled; the workspace is ROS 2 only.
  • ROS/run.sh: the sequential mode, which stopped each node after 10 s, was removed.
  • The ROS distribution selection moved from /tmp/selected_ros_version to ~/.cache/jetbot-nanoowl/ros_distro (ROS_SELECTION_FILE).

docs.title: Two-Jetson deployment: Docker, k3s, Helm October 8, 2026
What's New
docs.text:
• Every ROS 2 node is its own image (Docker/images.txt, one template that really builds the package) and its own Deployment in the ros2-jetson Helm chart.
  • Kubernetes/cluster/: k3s master + worker over Ethernet, image registry on the master.
  • The scheduler balances floating nodes over both Jetsons (requests, topology spread, GPU anti-affinity) and moves them within ≈ 35 s when the worker fails; hardware nodes stay pinned.
  • ROS 2 nodes communicate across the boards (host network, DDS bound to the cluster Ethernet, shared memory on a board); helm test checks it.
  • OTA server behind MetalLB at 192.168.10.200:8080 (firmware NET_OTA_SERVER_IP updated in JetOwl_FlightControl and JetOwl_Vision).
  • See Docker/CHANGELOG.md, Kubernetes/CHANGELOG.md, Helm/CHANGELOG.md.

docs.title: Thermal pipeline in the operator dashboard October 3, 2026
What's New
docs.text:
• ros2_qt 2.3.0: Vision tab → Thermal shows ros2_night_vision_owl:
    • The radiometric frame in °C with a colour bar.
    • CFAR detections, and tracks with their 95 % position ellipse, drawn on the frame of the same stamp.

docs.title: How contributions are credited
docs.text:
• Every merged change keeps its author in the git history; the contributors graph lists everyone with a merged commit.
  • User-visible changes are recorded in the Changelog with the issue or pull request they came from.

docs.title: Becoming a contributor
docs.text:
1. Read Contributing and the coding standards.
  2. Pick an open issue, or open one describing the problem before a large change.
  3. Sign the CLA on your first pull request.
  4. Make sure python3 -m pytest Tests/ and the tests of the packages you touched pass.

docs.title: Platform
docs.text:
Which hardware is supported?

The target is the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super 8 GB with JetPack 6.2 or later (Ampere GPU, sm_87). CUDA kernels and TensorRT engines are built for that architecture. Other Orin modules share sm_87 and are expected to build, but are not tested here. The original Jetson Nano and the Xavier boards are not supported. See Jetson.

Can I try it without a robot?

Yes. The full UAV stack — estimator, MPC, flight controller and mission planner — runs in software-in-the-loop on an Ubuntu 22.04 PC with ROS 2 Humble, and the hexacopter runs in Gazebo Harmonic with the same sensor protocol as the vehicle. Start with the Quick Start and Fly Your First Mission.

Which ROS 2 distribution?

ROS 2 Humble on Ubuntu 22.04, which is what JetPack 6 and Isaac ROS target. ROS/install.sh installs it.

What does the repository contain besides ROS 2 packages?

CUDA libraries, a CUDA-native detection pipeline, MATLAB/Simulink control design, the Remote UAV ground controller firmware, Docker/k3s/Helm deployment, an OTA server and a MAVLink relay. The flight-controller and camera firmware and the Android console live in the JetOwl_FlightControl, JetOwl_Vision and JetbotNanoOWL repositories. See Architecture.

docs.title: Building
docs.text:
How do I build only one package? 
ROS/build.sh -p <package>      # that package only
ROS/build.sh -u <package>      # that package and its in-repo dependencies
ROS/build.sh --help lists every option. See Installation. The build runs out of memory on the Jetson.

Building C++ and CUDA packages in parallel can exceed 8 GB. Build fewer packages at once (ROS/build.sh -j 1), or add swap. See Troubleshooting.

Containers or a native build?

Native builds are the simplest for development. Containers give one image per node and are how the stack is deployed on the two-Jetson cluster; Docker Compose runs the same images on a single board. See Deploy the Stack on a Two-Jetson Cluster.

docs.title: Control and safety
docs.text:
Why does every controller come with a derivation?

The repository's Control Design Standard requires every path from a sensor to an actuator to go through a filter and an estimator, to be closed-loop wherever a sensor exists, and to carry its plant model, units, sample rate, margins and a cited reference. Gains "tuned until it looked stable" are not accepted.

Is the stack ready to fly?

Not yet. Components are verified with unit tests and software-in-the-loop simulation; hardware-in-the-loop, bench and vehicle evidence is still being produced for the flight controller link, the OTA path, the stereo VPI matcher and the sensor link. The Roadmap lists what is open. Follow the verification order model → SIL → HIL → bench with current limits → vehicle.

What happens if the ground-station link is lost?

ros2_network_bridge declares the link lost after 5 s without a GCS heartbeat and commands the configured action (return home by default), unless a mission already validated by the mission planner is flying. See Connect a Ground Control Station.

docs.title: Perception
docs.text:
Do I have to train a model to detect an object?

No. NanoOWL detects categories from a text query, and the exemplar matcher in DeepLearning/ recognises a specific object from a single drawn box. Train only when a fixed set of categories must be detected faster or more reliably. See Deploy a Custom Detection Model.

Why is depth NaN in parts of the image?

ros2_stereo publishes NaN wherever the disparity is invalid or outside the 0.2–5 m window. NaN means unknown, never free space. Every valid pixel also carries its own σ_Z. See Calibrate the Stereo Camera.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
How do I contribute?

Read Contributing, sign the CLA on your first pull request, use Conventional Commits with a scope, and run python3 -m pytest Tests/ before pushing.

Where do I report a security problem?

Privately, through a GitHub security advisory, never in a public issue. See Support.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text: The project does not publish release dates. This page lists the open work that the components themselves record in their Known limitations, grouped by the verification order of the Control Design Standard: model → software-in-the-loop (SIL) → hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) → bench with current limits → vehicle. An item leaves this list when the evidence that closes it is committed next to the code.

docs.title: 1. Hardware evidence
docs.text:
The highest priority: every item here blocks flight.

Component Open item Reference UAV control system HIL and bench results; Allan-variance log of the IMU to replace the conservative bias random-walk placeholders; first execution of the CUDA MPPI on a GPU Control System Flight controller identification of the velocity-loop time constants τ_v on the vehicle (the margins scale with them); HIL and bench evidence Flight Controller Mission planner HIL and bench evidence with a battery current sensor and a thrust stand Mission Planner JetOwl bridge all links run against hardware; FC IMU covariances from its Allan-variance log; sensor-link clock parameters of the STM32N6 timer clock measured JetOwl Bridge JetOwl flight-control firmware IMU path enabled in CubeMX (I2C1, EXTI); bench run of the attitude, rate and rotor loops JetOwl Flight Control OTA XSPI flash, FSBL jump, watchdog and a download over a real network, in the documented bring-up order OTA design Stereo compile and run the VPI matcher on the Jetson; σ_d on a plane; NIS on a static recording; latency Stereo LiDAR SLAM recorded bag with the real sensors, NIS inside bounds, bench σ_r LiDAR SLAM Hexacopter model identify mass, inertia, rotor efficiency and drag on a thrust stand and a bifilar pendulum, then regenerate the gains Hexacopter Gazebo

docs.title: 2. Missing pieces
docs.text: Area Open item Vehicle power a publisher for battery/state; the flight controller and the mission planner consume it but nothing provides it yet Hexacopter MCU the STM32N6 firmware side of the UDP sensor link (the protocol and the Jetson side are done and tested) JetOwl_Vision calibration of the IMX335 module, then a CameraInfo publisher RF spectrum a derivation, or measured false-alarm and detection probabilities, for the analyser's fixed thresholds; an SDR driver for rf_monitor/raw_iq

docs.title: 3. Security
docs.text: Area Open item OTA package signatures (ECDSA or Ed25519) verified in the FSBL with the public key in OTP; until then SHA-256 protects against corruption only MAVLink message signing; until then use a trusted network with allowed_hosts and gcs_system_id MCU sensor link the link has no authentication; it is meant for a dedicated vehicle Ethernet segment

docs.title: 4. Improvements
docs.text: Component Item LiDAR SLAM localisation-only mode on a saved map; loop closure in a worker thread if processing_ms approaches the scan period Mission planner blend into a new route on an in-flight change instead of stopping first Night vision handling of merged targets (JPDA or merged-measurement models); ego-motion compensation from odometry Network bridge MAVLink mission protocol (MISSION_ITEM_INT) and parameter protocol Monitoring dashboard topic frequency and bandwidth on the TOPICS page CUDA library the missing test_pid_utils source; VPI module back in the build on systems with VPI Deep learning an INT8 calibrator; CI coverage of the Argus, cuDNN and TensorRT paths on a GPU runner

docs.title: Proposing work
docs.text: Open a feature request that states the problem first, or pick an item above and say in an issue that you are working on it. For control and estimation work, include the plant model and the verification you plan.

docs.title: Support
docs.text: The project is maintained by TNG-Blue on a best-effort basis. All support goes through GitHub so that answers stay searchable for the next person.

docs.title: Choose the right channel
docs.text: You have… Use Notes a question about using or building the stack GitHub Discussions search first; include your platform and the command you ran a reproducible bug Bug report logs, versions and the exact steps a controller or estimator behaving wrongly Control issue attach the signal log described below an installation problem Installation issue JetPack, CUDA, TensorRT and ROS 2 versions a documentation error Documentation issue the page URL and what is wrong an idea for a feature Feature request the problem first, then the proposal a security vulnerability private security advisory never a public issue; see Security policy

docs.title: Before you ask
docs.text:
1. Check the Troubleshooting page and the Known limitations section of the component's page.
  2. Look at /diagnostics: most packages report the measured cause of a fault there (Monitor a Running Robot).
  3. Run the component's tests: colcon test --packages-select <pkg> && colcon test-result --verbose.

docs.title: What to include
docs.text:
Platform        : Jetson Orin Nano Super 8 GB / x86_64 PC
JetPack / L4T   : 6.2 (cat /etc/nv_tegra_release)
ROS 2           : Humble (dpkg -l ros-humble-ros-base)
Commit          : git rev-parse --short HEAD
Package/version : <package.xml version>
Command         : the exact command
Output          : the full error, not a screenshot

For a control or estimation problem, also attach a bag with the set-point, measurement, estimate, controller terms and the pre- and post-saturation command (see Record for review). A controller cannot be diagnosed without them.

docs.title: Direct contact
docs.text: For matters that do not belong in a public thread (licensing, the corporate CLA, security when the advisory form is unavailable), email the maintainer at nguyen_danh_2002@outlook.com with a subject such as [SECURITY] … or [CCLA] ….

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
How to contribute changes that build, pass review and keep the system's guarantees.

  • Contributing

    CLA, workflow, naming, headers, commit messages and the pull-request process.

    Contributing

  • Control Design Standard

    The mandatory sensor → filter → estimator → controller → actuator chain and the evidence each controller must ship with.

    Control Design Standard

  • Code Style

    Language standards, formatters, linters and file headers.

    Code Style

  • Testing

    Unit, host, SIL and repository tests, with the command for each component.

    Testing

  • CI/CD

    The GitHub Actions workflows and what each one gates.

    CI/CD

  • Release Process

    Versioning, changelogs, images, firmware packages and the documentation site.

    Release Process

docs.title: Workflow in brief
docs.text:
1. Sign the CLA on your first pull request: comment I have read and agree to the CLA.
  2. Branch from master, keep the change focused, follow the Code Style.
  3. Anything that moves hardware or estimates physical state follows the Control Design Standard: derivation, units, sample rate, margins and a failsafe, in the code and in the package README.
  4. Run the tests for what you touched, and python3 -m pytest Tests/ -q.
  5. Update the component CHANGELOG.md when the change is user-visible, and the package README when its interface or design changes — the README is what this site renders.
  6. Open a pull request with a Conventional Commit title; the quality gates must pass.

docs.title: CI/CD
docs.text:
GitHub Actions workflows in .github/workflows/.

Workflow Trigger What it checks or does [CI] Quality Gates (quality-gates.yml) push, pull request, manual repository tests (pytest Tests/), naming convention of directories and packages, Conventional Commit pull-request title, YAML syntax, Helm lint + kubeconform, Helm render variants, hadolint on the Dockerfiles [Bot] Deploy MkDocs Documentation (docs_deploy.yaml) push and pull request touching the docs, the rendered READMEs or the hooks; manual mkdocs build --strict, excluded-file check, internal link check of the built site, OTA web-UI preview; on master, publishes to TNG-Blue/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL-Docs [Bot] Build & Test OTA Server (ota-server-ci.yml) changes under Server_OTA/ gofmt, go vet, go test [Bot] Build & Test MAVLink Relay (relay-server-ci.yml) changes under Server_Relay/ gofmt, go vet, go test -race [Bot] Build Utilities Libraries (build-utilities.yml) changes under Utilities/ builds and installs each library's Python package (matrix over the libraries) [Bot] Update Submodules (update-submodules.yml) weekly (Tuesday 19:00 UTC), manual moves the submodules to their tracked branch and opens a pull request [Bot] Dependabot auto-merge (mergeDependabotPR.yml) Dependabot pull requests approves the pull request and enables auto-merge; it waits only for the checks that branch protection marks as required [AI] Claude Code (claude.yml) @claude in a comment assistant on issues and pull requests; @claude review runs a code review [AI] Junie (junie.yml) comment trigger alternative AI assistant

The firmware repositories have their own CI: JetOwl_FlightControl runs host tests, an ARM compile of every source and a firmware link; JetOwl_Vision runs host tests with sanitizers, the control analysis, and CMake and Make firmware builds.

docs.title: Documentation pipeline
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A["push to master<br/>(Docs/, READMEs, hooks)"] --> B["mkdocs build --strict<br/>+ source_pages hook"]
    B --> C["check_docs_links.py"]
    C --> D["OTA web-UI preview"]
    D --> E["publish to<br/>Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL-Docs"]

A broken link in a package README fails the build, because the README is part of the site.

docs.title: Code Style
docs.text: The authoritative rules are in .claude/rules/; this page summarises them.

docs.title: Languages
docs.text: Language Standard Formatter Linter Python PEP 8 black flake8 (Tests/test_flake8.py) C / C++ / CUDA Google C++ Style clang-format clang-tidy ROS 2 packages ROS 2 developer guide — ament linters MATLAB MATLAB code standards — checkcode (mlint) Go gofmt gofmt go vet YAML / XML 2-space indent, no tabs — yamllint, ament_xmllint Shell POSIX-safe, set -euo pipefail — shellcheck

docs.title: Naming
docs.text:
Kind Directory Package Standard ROS 2 package Source/ROS2_Feature_Name ros2_feature_name Isaac ROS package Source/Isaac_ROS-Feature_Name isaac_ros_feature_name Firmware Microcontroller/<Board_Role> snake_case.c/.h Host library Utilities/<Library_Name> snake_case Helm chart, Kubernetes manifest kebab-case (required by those ecosystems only)

The package name must be identical in package.xml, CMakeLists.txt and setup.py. Nodes are *_node.py / *_node.cpp, launch files *.launch.py, parameter files *_params.yaml.

docs.title: File headers
docs.text:
Every .py, .c, .h, .cpp, .hpp, .cu, .cuh, .sh, .m and .xml file starts with the SPDX Apache-2.0 block from .claude/templates/shared/copyright-headers/; Tests/test_copyright.py fails the build otherwise.

#   ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#   SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
#   Copyright (c) 2025 TNG-Blue
#   ... (full Apache-2.0 notice)
#   ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Control and estimation code additionally carries the design block of the Control Design Standard after the SPDX header.

docs.title: Commit messages
docs.text:
Conventional Commits with a scope:

<type>(<scope>): <subject in the imperative, ≤ 50 characters>

<body wrapped at 72 characters: what and why>

<footer: issue references, BREAKING CHANGE>

Types: feat, fix, perf, refactor, docs, test, chore, style, ci. A breaking change adds ! after the scope and a BREAKING CHANGE: footer with migration instructions.

docs.title: Third-party code
docs.text: Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD and ISC are compatible; LGPL and MPL need review; GPL and proprietary code are not accepted. Record every new dependency in NOTICE.md and mark adapted code with its origin, author, licence and the modifications made.

docs.text:
1. Fork the repository and clone your fork (the project uses submodules): 

    git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/<you>/Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL.git
cd Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL

  2. Create a branch — feat/<short-name>, fix/<short-name>, docs/<short-name>.

  3. Make your changes following the guidelines below.
  4. Test them (see Testing).
  5. Open a pull request and fill in the template.

Environment setup: DEPLOYMENT.md, Docker/, .devcontainer/, and the documentation site.

docs.title: Naming
docs.text:
Type Directory Package Standard ROS 2 ROS2_Feature_Name ros2_feature_name Isaac ROS Isaac_ROS-Feature_Name isaac_ros_feature_name

The same package name must appear in package.xml, CMakeLists.txt and setup.py. Full rules: .claude/rules/naming-conventions.md.

docs.title: Copyright headers (mandatory)
docs.text: Every source file (.py, .c, .h, .cpp, .hpp, .cu, .cuh, .sh, .m, .xml) starts with the Apache-2.0 SPDX block. Copy it from .claude/templates/shared/copyright-headers/. Tests/test_copyright.py fails the build if it is missing.

docs.title: Code style
docs.text: Language Standard Check with Python PEP 8 black, flake8 C / C++ / CUDA Google C++ Style clang-format, clang-tidy Go (Server_OTA/) gofmt gofmt -l ., go vet ./... MATLAB project MATLAB standards checkcode ROS 2 ROS 2 developer guide ament linters

docs.title: Control, estimation and firmware changes
docs.text:
Anything that turns a sensor reading into an actuator command must follow .claude/rules/control-systems.md:

sensor → filter → estimator → controller → actuator → measured feedback

Pull requests in this area are reviewed against the maths, not the vibes. Include:

  • the plant model (derived or identified) and its validation fit;
  • the filter (type, cutoff, discretisation, phase lag) and the estimator (Q/R justification, observability, NIS consistency);
  • the controller choice and how its gains were obtained — PID, LQR, MPC, FOC, sliding mode, adaptive or otherwise, matched to the plant;
  • saturation, anti-windup, rate limits and the failsafe behaviour;
  • stability margins (GM ≥ 6 dB, PM ≥ 45°; inner loops ≥ 30°) including transport delay;
  • simulation → SIL → HIL evidence.

Hand-tuned constants without a derivation will be sent back.

docs.title: Commit messages
docs.text:
Conventional Commits, with a scope:

feat(control): add anti-windup to velocity PI loop
fix(detection): guard against empty NanoOWL result
perf(cuda): coalesce point-cloud voxel writes
docs(tutorials): add stereo calibration walkthrough

Types: feat, fix, perf, refactor, docs, test, chore, style, ci. Subject in the imperative, ≤ 50 characters. Breaking changes use ! and a BREAKING CHANGE: footer. Details: .claude/rules/commit-messages.md.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
# Repository-level gates (copyright headers, flake8, smoke tests)
python3 -m pytest Tests/ -q

# ROS 2 packages you touched
colcon build --symlink-install --packages-select <package>
colcon test --packages-select <package> && colcon test-result --verbose

# OTA server
cd Server_OTA/src && gofmt -l . && go vet ./... && go test ./...

# Documentation
mkdocs build --strict

Add tests for new behaviour. All tests must pass before review.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Update Docs/ for user-facing changes, and the package README.md for package-level ones
  • Add docstrings (Python) / Doxygen comments (C++/CUDA) to public interfaces
  • Update CHANGELOG.md for user-visible changes, following .claude/rules/changelog-management.md

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: New dependencies must be license-compatible with Apache-2.0 (Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD, ISC are fine; GPL is not). Record them in NOTICE.md and in the relevant requirements.txt / package.xml / go.mod. See .claude/rules/license-attribution.md.

docs.title: Pull request process
docs.text:
1. Self-review against the checklist in the PR template.
  2. Ensure CI is green — build, tests, linters and the automated review.
  3. Code owners (CODEOWNERS) are requested automatically.
  4. Address review feedback with follow-up commits (no force-push once review has started).
  5. A maintainer merges once approvals and checks are in place.

Reviews normally happen within 3–5 business days.
