docs.text: Defect Consequence Fix configENABLE_TRUSTZONE = 1 but AppliSecure lacked FreeRTOS's secure port NS did not link (SecureContext_*) added the 4 secure/*.c files of FreeRTOS-Kernel V11.2.0 (same version as NS) + AppliSecure/FreeRTOS_Secure/FreeRTOSConfig.h heap_5.c without USE_FreeRTOS_HEAP_5 the first osThreadNew hit configASSERT macro defined in the Makefile and in AppliNonSecure/CMakeLists.txt arm-compile-check.sh passed -DHAL_TIM_MODULE_ENABLED while hal_conf.h already enables it every Interface file failed with "redefined" under -Werror removed the redundant -D Old CubeMX Makefile (from before FreeRTOS/RIF) missing hal_rif.c, FreeRTOS, timebase rewritten from mx-generated.cmake

docs.title: 9. Not yet verified / open items
docs.text:
• Not yet run on hardware. In order: ping 192.168.10.2 → the agent sees the session → ros2 topic list → bench without propellers → HIL (control-systems §4).
  • The IMU read path exists (imu_acq.c, CONTROL_DESIGN.md §1.4–1.5) but runs only once CubeMX has enabled I2C1 + EXTI PE0 and BOARD_CUBEMX_PERIPHERALS_READY = 1. Until then the firmware refuses to arm and does not publish /imu/data. The mounting frame q_SB is an assumption — the static check of §1.4 must be performed.
  • BOARD_CUBEMX_PERIPHERALS_READY = 0: the TIM6 tick is not running ⇒ arming is refused (control loop timer not running).
  • Pre-existing conflict: CubeMX currently uses TIM1 as the NS HAL timebase, while board_config.h reserves TIM1 for DShot. The timebase must move to another timer before DShot is enabled.
  • The Jetson MPC's thrust_min_n estimate (5 N, X12 airframe) must be below 20 % of the JetOwl airframe's maximum thrust, otherwise arming is refused (thrust command too high).
  • The Imu covariances are 0 ("unknown") until an Allan-variance log of the IMU is available.

docs.title: OTA: over-the-network firmware updates for JetOwl_FlightControl and JetOwl_Vision
docs.text:
Source

Snapshot of docs/OTA.md from TNG-Blue/JetOwl_FlightControl at commit 23b5ac3 (submodule Microcontroller/JetOwl_FlightControl). Regenerate with Scripts/mkdocs_hooks/snapshot_submodules.py after updating the submodule.

This document describes what has been written, compiled, linked and tested on the host in the repository, and separates out what is not yet verified on hardware (section 9). Read section 9 before flashing a board. The OTA layer (Application/Ota/, FSBL/Boot/, tools/ota_pack.py, tests/host/test_ota.c) is identical in JetOwl_Vision (Appli/Ota/); only ota_board.h differs.

docs.title: 1. Architecture
docs.text:
Server_OTA (Go, Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL)        STM32N6 (FC or Vision)
 192.168.1.101:8080                               ┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 ┌──────────────────────────────┐   HTTP/TCP      │ "ota" task (ota_service.c, low priority)   │
 │ GET /api/ota/manifest?device │◀──────────────── │   ota_client: manifest → download → SHA-256│
 │ GET /download?file= (Range)  │◀──────────────── │   → flash read-back → header check → READY │
 │ POST /api/ota/report         │◀──────────────── │   ota/apply: set pending, persist, reset   │
 │ POST /upload  (.fw validated) │                 │   trial image healthy 30 s → confirm; IWDG │
 └──────────────────────────────┘                  │ micro-ROS: /jetowl/ota/start, /ota/apply   │
          ▲ make ota-upload                        ├────────────────────────────────────────────┤
          │                                        │ FSBL (fsbl_boot.c): read boot record →     │
   tools/ota_pack.py → <device>_v<M.m.p>.fw        │ choose slot → SHA-256 → copy to RAM → IWDG │
                                                   │ (if trial) → jump                          │
                                                   ├────────────────────────────────────────────┤
                                                   │ NOR XSPI2 (64 MB): FSBL | bootctl×2 | A | B │
                                                   └────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Principles: OTA never overwrites the running image (A/B); a new image becomes the primary image only after it has proven itself healthy; every failure (power loss, network loss, corrupted image, hanging image) leads back to a bootable state.

docs.title: 2. Flash map (Ota/Inc/ota_layout.h)
docs.text:
Offset Size Content 0x0000_0000 1 MB FSBL (signed with STM32_SigningTool, loaded by the Boot ROM) 0x0010_0000 4 KB boot control record, copy 0 0x0010_1000 4 KB boot control record, copy 1 0x0020_0000 4 MB slot A (.fw package) 0x0060_0000 4 MB slot B

Bus (memory-mapped) address = 0x7000_0000 + offset. [BOARD] MX25UM51245G NOR on XSPI2 (NUCLEO-N657X0-Q, STM32N6570-DK): 4 KB sector, 64 KB block, 256 B page.

docs.title: 3. The .fw package (JOWL v1, Ota/Inc/ota_image.h)
docs.text:
A 256 B little-endian header followed by contiguous segments: magic JOWL, device (jetowl_fc / jetowl_vision), version M.m.p, total_size, entry (vector table), ≤ 4 segments {load_addr, offset, size}, SHA-256 of the payload, CRC-32 of the header.

Device Segments Permitted RAM windows (ota_board.h) jetowl_fc AppliSecure.bin @ 0x34000400, AppliNonSecure.bin @ 0x34100400 (secure alias of 0x24100400) [0x34000400, 0x34064000), [0x34100400, 0x34180000) jetowl_vision JetOwl_Vision_Appli.bin @ 0x34000400 [0x34000400, 0x34080000)

The FSBL runs at 0x34180400… (AXISRAM2), outside every window: a corrupted or malicious package cannot overwrite the running FSBL. Invariants checked (C: ota_image_parse, Go: ParsePackageHeader, Python: ota_pack.py parse): contiguous segments, total = 256 + Σ size, each segment inside one window, no overlap, entry = load_addr[0] aligned to 128 B (ARMv8-M VTOR), reserved fields = 0.

Integrity: CRC-32/ISO-HDLC has a Hamming distance ≥ 2 at every length, so every single-bit error in the header is detected (the test flips every one of the 2048 bits: none slips through, in both C and Go). The content is protected by SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) — checked four times: (1) downloaded file == the manifest's sha256, (2) full read-back of the slot from flash == manifest (catches silent flash write errors), (3) payload == header (ota_slot_verify), (4) the FSBL hashes the copy in RAM — exactly what will run — before jumping. SHA-256 protects against corruption, not against forgery (section 9).

docs.title: 4. Server (Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL/Server_OTA)
docs.text:
Endpoint Meaning GET /api/ota/manifest?device=<id> latest valid release for the device, key=value text (device, version, file, size, sha256); 404 if none GET /download?file=<file> download; supports Range: bytes=n- → 206 + Content-Range (used to resume) POST /upload (multipart firmware) stores a package; a .fw must pass the header + SHA-256 check and be named <device>_v<M.m.p>.fw; never overwrites (409) POST /api/ota/report?device=&version=&state=&detail= the MCU reports its state (running, trial, downloaded, staged, confirmed, error…) GET /api/ota/devices last state of each MCU (JSON)

Versions are compared numerically (1.10.0 > 1.9.99). A package with the newest name but a corrupted content is skipped (an MCU is never invited to download it).

docs.title: 5. A/B boot state machine (Ota/Inc/ota_bootctl.h)
docs.text:
application: download + verify slot S ≠ running ── ota/apply ──▶ pending = S, trials = 0, PERSIST, reset
 FSBL, pending ≠ NONE:
     trials < 3 and S valid ─▶ trials++, PERSIST, boot S in trial mode (IWDG 8 s)
     otherwise              ─▶ pending = NONE (rollback), PERSIST, boot active
 FSBL, active corrupted ─▶ the other slot if valid (fallback)
 application in trial + continuously healthy for 30 s ─▶ confirm: active = S, pending = NONE, PERSIST

Atomic update, proven: two copies in two sectors; the new copy (seq = seq_max + 1) is always written to the sector not holding the newest copy; reading selects the CRC-valid copy with the largest seq under serial-number arithmetic (RFC 1982, correct even when seq wraps at 2³²). A power loss during any operation of one persist leaves the old sector intact ⇒ the state read back is either old or new, never a mixture. test_ota.c cuts power at every operation (half-erased, half-written) from four different histories and checks exactly this property.

No infinite loop: trials is incremented and persisted before jumping into the trial image, so an image that hangs or keeps resetting runs at most OTA_MAX_TRIALS = 3 times (the test simulates 10 boots: a hanging image ⇒ exactly 3 trials, then back to A; a healthy image ⇒ one trial, then confirm). If the FSBL cannot persist the record it does not boot the trial image.

The application knows which slot it runs without anything passed from the FSBL: pending ≠ NONE while the application runs ⇔ the application is the trial image.

IWDG: 32 kHz LSI, prescaler 256, reload 1000 ⇒ T = 1001·256/32000 = 8.008 s. The FSBL enables it only when booting a trial image; the IWDG cannot be stopped until the next reset, so ota_service refreshes it for the whole session. Invariant: the interval between two refreshes is < 8 s. The task refreshes at the start of every cycle (≤ 1 s) and before every blocking operation on the network and flash; each blocking operation is bounded: connect 2 s (non-blocking + select, because lwIP's blocking connect can wait tens of seconds when the server is down), send/recv 5 s, erasing one flash block ≤ 2 s (datasheet); the computation between two operations takes microseconds ⇒ the largest interval is ≈ 5 s < 8 s. A stopped OTA server therefore does not reset or roll back a healthy image. If the ota task is starved for

8 s ⇒ reset ⇒ the FSBL counts one more trial.

docs.title: Confirmation ("healthy")
docs.text:
OTA_SVC_CONFIRM_S = 30 s of continuous health — a policy, not a control constant: much longer than the status period (1–2 Hz), the agent ping (1 Hz) and the time synchronisation (10 s), so an image that only half starts is not confirmed.

Device Healthy when Applied (reset) when FC micro-ROS session alive and the control TIM tick running (when BOARD_CUBEMX_PERIPHERALS_READY = 1) disarmed; arming is refused for the whole trial-boot session (even after confirmation, because the IWDG keeps running) — power-cycle once, then fly Vision micro-ROS session alive and the camera streaming (UROS_OTA_CONFIRM_REQUIRES_CAMERA) always (no actuator)

docs.title: 6. Usage
docs.text:
# 1) Release (on the build machine): package and upload to the server
make ota-upload VERSION=1.2.3              # FC  -> jetowl_fc_v1.2.3.fw
make ota-upload VERSION=1.0.1              # Vision (JetOwl_Vision repository) -> jetowl_vision_v1.0.1.fw
#    (OTA_SERVER=192.168.1.101:8080 by default; package only: make ota VERSION=...)

# 2) On the Jetson (ROS 2): check + download, monitor, apply
ros2 service call /jetowl/ota/start std_srvs/srv/Trigger
ros2 topic echo /jetowl/status        # fw_version, ota_state, ota_progress_pct, ota_available, ota_error
ros2 service call /jetowl/ota/apply std_srvs/srv/Trigger    # the FC must be disarmed
#    Vision: /jetowl_vision/ota/start, /jetowl_vision/ota/apply, /jetowl_vision/status
#    ros2_jetowl_bridge forwards the firmware status to /diagnostics, so ota_* is there too.

# 3) Server: which device runs which version
curl http://192.168.1.101:8080/api/ota/devices

ota_state: idle → checking → up_to_date | downloading → ready → (ota/apply) applying → reset. ota_trial = 1 during the first 30 s of a new image; ota_last_event: staged, confirmed, rollback_trials, rollback_invalid, fallback.

docs.title: First flash (once, with STM32CubeProgrammer and the board's external loader)
docs.text:
1. Signed FSBL (STM32_SigningTool_CLI -bin FSBL.bin -nk -of 0x80000000 -t fsbl -hv 2.3) → offset 0.
  2. .fw package (make ota VERSION=…) → offset 0x00200000 (slot A), i.e. 0x70200000.
  3. No boot record needs to be written: on blank flash the FSBL boots slot A and creates the record itself.

Development with a debugger (loading the application straight into RAM) still works: without a boot record, ota/apply treats the other slot as active and writes into slot A.

docs.title: 7. Network
docs.text:
The MCUs are on 192.168.10.0/24 and the server on 192.168.1.101: packets go through the gateway 192.168.10.1 (the Jetson, net_config.h).

  • Server_OTA runs on the Jetson itself and the Jetson owns 192.168.1.101 on another interface (Wi-Fi/LAN): no extra configuration — Linux accepts packets for every local address on every interface.
  • Server on another machine in 192.168.1.0/24: the Jetson must forward: 
    sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
sudo iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 192.168.10.0/24 -o <LAN interface> -j MASQUERADE
    (or replace NAT with a static route 192.168.10.0/24 via <Jetson LAN IP> on the router/server).

Check: curl http://192.168.1.101:8080/api/ota/manifest?device=jetowl_fc from the Jetson.

docs.title: 8. Verification
docs.text: Level Content Result Host C (tests/host/test_ota.c, gcc + clang + ASan/UBSan, -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion) 504 checks: NIST SHA-256 vectors (empty, abc, 448 bit, 10⁶×a) + random buffer splits; CRC-32 check value 0xCBF43926; every header bit flipped (package + boot record); every package invariant; power cut at every flash operation; boot decisions (fresh, trial, trials exhausted, corrupted pending, fallback); 10-boot life cycle; malformed HTTP/manifest; client against a fake server: odd-sized recv, connection dropped 3 times (resumed with Range), server ignoring Range, trials exhausted, wrong SHA, flash write error, 404, too large, wrong device, wrong version pass Cross-check in 3 languages the same package built by ota_pack.py decodes identically in C (test_ota.c) and Go (ota_test.go), and the Go builder produces it byte for byte pass Go server (go test -race) newest release by number, corrupted/misnamed packages skipped; manifest; upload (409/413/422/400); Range 206 with the correct Content-Range; ../ blocked; report pass ARM (arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.2) FC FSBL (ROM 60.5 KB) and Vision FSBL (36.4 KB) link; FC AppliNonSecure with OTA (ROM 221 KB / 511 KB, RAM 232 KB / 512 KB); Vision Appli with OTA (ROM 215 KB / 511 KB); arm-compile-check.sh (41 files) pass End to end on the host the real Server_OTA (Go) + make ota-upload of a real FC package (236 KB, 2 segments) + the C client (same source as the firmware) over real TCP, with one disconnection mid-way: resumed with Range, slot == file byte for byte, ota_slot_verify passes, the report appears in /api/ota/devices pass Hardware XSPI2, FSBL jump, IWDG, download over a real network not yet

docs.title: 9. Not yet verified / limitations
docs.text:
• Not yet run on hardware. In order: FSBL boots slot A → ota_state other than no_flash (the driver reads the Macronix JEDEC ID) → ota/start against the real server → ota/apply → confirmation → a deliberately corrupted image to observe the rollback.
  • [BOARD] flash and pins: MX25UM51245G on XSPI2/port N, VDDIO3 = 1.8 V (as on the NUCLEO-N657X0-Q). The JetOwl_Vision board must be checked against its schematic. XSPI runs single-line SPI ≤ 50 MHz and does not depend on the HSLV fuse configuration.
  • Boot ROM → FSBL: the FSBL must be signed and placed at offset 0 (ST documentation, RM0486 "Boot"); the driver resets the NOR chip in OPI-DTR, OPI-STR and SPI modes before use, so it does not depend on the mode the Boot ROM leaves behind.
  • No digital signature: SHA-256 only protects against corruption. Anyone who can write to the server (or impersonate it on the network) can install firmware. This network must be a dedicated vehicle segment. ECDSA/Ed25519 signatures verified in the FSBL (public key in OTP) are the next step.
  • FC: AppliSecure assigns XSPI2/XSPIM/IWDG to AppliNonSecure (as for ETH1), so the non-secure side can write the whole flash, FSBL included. Moving flash writes into a secure (CMSE) service that only allows writes to the slots is the next improvement (docs/TRUSTZONE_TRADEOFF.md).
  • The IWDG enabled during a trial-boot session runs until the next reset, even after confirmation. The FC refuses to arm for that whole session (power-cycle after OTA before flight): the IWDG never runs in flight.
  • Server WriteTimeout 30 s: if slow flash erasure (BE64K up to 2 s per block) makes one download exceed 30 s, the client resumes with Range — verified by the dropped-connection test.

docs.title: Full-duplex LoRa control link (Remote_UAV ↔ JetOwl_FlightControl)
docs.text:
Source

Snapshot of docs/RFLINK.md from TNG-Blue/JetOwl_FlightControl at commit 23b5ac3 (submodule Microcontroller/JetOwl_FlightControl). Regenerate with Scripts/mkdocs_hooks/snapshot_submodules.py after updating the submodule.

Design document for Application/RfLink/ (a pure-C library, shared verbatim with Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL/Microcontroller/Remote_UAV/src/rflink/), Application/Control/Src/rc_input.c and Application/Interface/Src/rflink_app.c. Every figure below is either checked by a host test (tests/host/test_rflink.c, test_rc_input.c) or cited.

docs.title: 1. Hardware
docs.text:
Remote_UAV (ground) JetOwl_FlightControl (UAV) MCU Arduino GIGA R1 WiFi (STM32H747) + GIGA Display Shield STM32N657 (NUCLEO-N657X0-Q) UL module (uplink, commands) Core1121-XF #1 — transmit only, SPI1 (D11–D13) Core1121-XF #1 — receive only, SPI5 DL module (downlink, telemetry) Core1121-XF #2 — receive only, SPI (header D89–D91) Core1121-XF #2 — transmit only, SPI5

Chip: Semtech LR1121, 32 MHz TCXO at 3.0 V, RF switch on DIO5/DIO6 (table from the Waveshare BSP). Frequency ranges supported by the chip (Semtech lr1121_common.h): 150–960 MHz, 2000–2100 MHz (S-band), 2400–2500 MHz. The LR1121 has no 1.2 GHz band.

FC pins: Application/Interface/Inc/board_config.h sections 2.4 and 2.8. Remote pins: Remote_UAV/src/app/app_config.h and Remote_UAV/docs/WIRING.md.

docs.title: 2. Why full duplex needs TWO modules at EACH end
docs.text:
A LoRa transceiver is half-duplex: it cannot transmit and receive at the same time. Full duplex here is FDD (frequency-division duplex): each end has two modules, each module handles one direction only, and the two directions use two different bands and run simultaneously:

flowchart LR
    subgraph GND[Remote_UAV – GIGA R1]
        S[Sticks + buttons] --> F[Filtering + calibration] --> TXu[LR1121 UL<br/>TRANSMIT only]
        RXd[LR1121 DL<br/>RECEIVE only] --> UI[Display<br/>MEASURED state]
    end
    subgraph AIR[UAV – STM32N657]
        RXu[LR1121 UL<br/>RECEIVE only] --> RC[rc_input] --> CG[cmd_guard] --> AT[attitude_ctrl → rate_loop → ESC]
        IMU[IMU + ESC RPM] --> AT
        AT --> TLM[telemetry] --> TXd[LR1121 DL<br/>TRANSMIT only]
    end
    TXu -- "2.4 GHz FHSS, 50 Hz" --> RXu
    TXd -- "sub-GHz 921.4 MHz, 10 Hz" --> RXd

Consequences: there is no TX/RX turnaround time, telemetry never blocks commands, and command latency does not depend on traffic in the opposite direction.

docs.title: 2.1 Band choice: why commands use 2.4 GHz and telemetry sub-GHz (default)
docs.text:
Criterion Commands (UL) 2.4 GHz Telemetry (DL) sub-GHz Worldwide regulation ISM 2400–2483.5 MHz; FHSS with ≥ 15 channels is compliant under ETSI EN 300 328 §4.3.1.4 and FCC 15.247(a)(1)(iii) Region-dependent (AS923 / EU868 / US915) Bandwidth → ToA BW 812 kHz ⇒ ToA 5.2 ms ⇒ 50 Hz feasible BW 250 kHz ⇒ ToA 41 ms ⇒ 10 Hz Link budget sufficient for line of sight (section 5) large margin

TX→RX isolation on the same airframe. With a 13 dBm transmit antenna and a receive antenna d ≈ 10 cm apart: FSPL = 20 log₁₀(4πd/λ) ≈ 20 dB at 2.44 GHz ⇒ a blocker of ≈ −7 dBm at the receiver, while the wanted packet arrives near the sensitivity limit (≈ −105 dBm) ⇒ ≈ 98 dB of selectivity is needed. Placing the two directions in two bands ~1.5 GHz apart lets each module's matching network and antenna provide most of that; putting both at 2.4 GHz (RFLINK_PLAN_2G4_DUAL) is usable only with widely separated antennas.

Harmonics. rflink_check_config() rejects a configuration in which the 2nd or 3rd harmonic of the DL falls inside the UL range (a non-linear PA radiates its strongest harmonics at orders 2–3). 921.4 MHz → 1842.8 / 2764.2 MHz: outside 2402–2478 MHz.

S-band 2000–2010 MHz (RFLINK_PLAN_2G4_SBAND) is a mobile-satellite-service (MSS) band and requires a licence.

docs.title: 2.2 Three band plans (rflink_config.h)
docs.text:
RFLINK_PLAN UL DL DL ToA / period 2G4_SUBGHZ (default) 2402–2478 MHz, 20 channels, 4 MHz step 921.4 MHz (AS923, Vietnam) 41.1 ms / 100 ms — RFLINK_REGION_EU868 as above 869.525 MHz (g3, duty ≤ 10 %) 41.1 ms / 500 ms = 8 % — RFLINK_REGION_US915 as above 915 MHz, BW 500 kHz (DTS) 20.5 ms / 100 ms 2G4_SBAND as above 2005 MHz — licence required 25.3 ms / 100 ms 2G4_DUAL 2402–2447 MHz, 16 channels 2478 MHz 25.3 ms / 100 ms

To change the plan or region, add -DRFLINK_PLAN=... / -DRFLINK_REGION=... to both firmwares.

docs.title: 3. Physical layer and timing
docs.text:
Time on air from the Semtech formula (AN1200.13; lr11xx_radio_get_lora_time_on_air_numerator, tested against an independent implementation of the formula):

n_payload = 8 + max(ceil((8PL − 4SF + 28 + 16CRC − 20IH − 8FS) / (4(SF − 2DE))) · (CR + 4), 0)
T = (n_pre + 4.25 + 2FS + n_payload) · 2^SF / BW          FS = 1 when SF ≤ 6 (fine synch)
UL (RC) DL (TLM) SF / BW / CR 6 / 812 kHz / ⅘ 7 / 250 kHz / ⅘ Preamble 12 (SF6 requires ≥ 12) 8 Frame 21 B (9 header + 8 payload + 4 tag) 37 B (9 + 24 + 4) ToA 5.22 ms 41.08 ms Period 20 ms (50 Hz) 100 ms (10 Hz) Output power 13 dBm (HF PA maximum) 14 dBm

Command latency (stick → set-point in cmd_guard), mean: stick filter ≈ 28 ms (group delay of the 2nd-order Butterworth, f_c = 7.93 Hz, see Remote_UAV/src/input/stick_dsp.h) + frame wait T/2 = 10 ms + ToA 5.2 ms + processing < 1 ms + attitude-loop tick ≤ 4 ms ⇒ ≈ 46 ms.

docs.title: 4. Frequency hopping and synchronisation (rflink_fhss.h)
docs.text:
• The channel sequence is a permutation π of {0..19} (Fisher–Yates + xorshift32, seed derived from the master key). Frame number seq is transmitted on channel π[seq mod 20].
  • Lock: frame k received at r_k ⇒ listen immediately on π[k+1] with deadline D = r_k + T + g. Past the deadline ⇒ hop to π[k+2] before frame k+2 starts, with margin T − ToA − g = 20 − 5.22 − 3 = 11.8 ms > 0.
  • Clock drift: 100 ppm in total ⇒ still inside the g = 3 ms window after at most g/(εT) = 1500 consecutive lost frames; the "blind hopping" limit is set to 50 frames (1 s), after which the receiver enters SEARCH.
  • SEARCH: park on π[0]; since π is a permutation the transmitter visits that channel at least once every 20 frames ⇒ re-acquisition ≤ 20 × 20 ms = 0.4 s (no packet loss).

docs.title: 5. Link budget (theoretical, free space)
docs.text:
Sensitivity S = −174 + 10 log₁₀ BW + NF + SNR_min. From the Waveshare figure (−111 dBm at SF7/BW800) ⇒ NF ≈ 11.4 dB ⇒ SF6/BW812: S ≈ −108.5 dBm.

UL: PL_max = 13 + 2 + 2 − (−108.5) = 125.5 dB. Subtracting a 10 dB fading margin (Rayleigh P_out 10 %, section 7) ⇒ FSPL 115.5 dB ⇒ d = 10^((115.5 − 100.2)/20) km ≈ 5.8 km in free space at 2.44 GHz. The sub-GHz DL has far more margin (≈ 100 km in theory) ⇒ the UL limits the range — sufficient for visual-line-of-sight flight. The real range is lower (Fresnel zone, shadowing by the airframe, antennas).

docs.title: 6. Framing, authentication, replay protection (rflink_proto.h)
docs.text:
off size  field
0   1     hdr = (version << 4) | type        type 1 = RC, 2 = TLM
1   4     nonce_tx (current nonce of the transmitter)
5   4     seq      (frame counter of the transmitter)
9   N     payload
9+N 4     tag = AES-CMAC_Kdir(nonce_rx || frame[0..9+N))[0..3]
  • AES-128 (FIPS-197) + CMAC (NIST SP 800-38B), tested against the FIPS-197 C.1 and RFC 4493 vectors.
  • Per-direction keys K_UL, K_DL and the hopping seed are derived with a counter-mode KDF (NIST SP 800-108r1, PRF = CMAC) from a 128-bit master key (rflink_key.h).
  • Replay protection without non-volatile memory: the tag covers the receiver's random nonce (LR1121 GetRandomNumber, generated at boot) ⇒ a frame recorded before that boot carries a wrong tag. Within a session, seq must increase strictly. If the transmitter reboots (seq back to 0) ⇒ 3 frames with a valid tag but stale sequence ⇒ the receiver changes its nonce (rekey) ⇒ the transmitter learns the new nonce over the other direction ⇒ recovery (≈ 0.5 s).
  • 32-bit tag: forgery probability per frame 2⁻³²; at 50 frames/s this takes on average ~1.4 years of continuous attempts on the correct hopping channel.
  • The default key is public ⇒ warnings at compile time, on the remote's screen and on the LED. Generate a private key with python3 tools/rflink_keygen.py (writes rflink_key_local.h into both repositories, already in .gitignore).

docs.title: 7. Link-quality estimation (rflink_quality.h)
docs.text:
• LQ = fraction of frames received in a 64-frame window indexed by seq (an unbiased binomial estimator, σ ≤ 6.25 %).
  • RSSI/SNR are low-pass filtered (first order, τ = 0.5 s, backward Euler: a = T/(τ + T)).
  • Margin M = SNR_filtered − SNR_min(SF) (SX1276 table 13, SX1261/2 §6.1.1).
  • Grading by Rayleigh outage probability P_out = 1 − exp(−10^(−M/10)): GOOD when P_out ≤ 1 % (M ≥ 20.0 dB), FAIR when ≤ 10 % (M ≥ 9.8 dB), POOR otherwise (Goldsmith, Wireless Communications, §3.2.1). No hand-picked thresholds.

docs.title: 8. From stick to propeller (rc_input.h) — the loop stays closed
docs.text:
stick → median 3 → Butterworth 2 (Tustin, pre-warped) → calibration → 3σ deadband → expo   [remote]
   → LoRa UL → authentication → rc_input → cmd_guard → attitude_ctrl (250 Hz) → rate_loop (1 kHz)
   → rotor_speed → DShot → ESC;   feedback: IMU (attitude, angular rate) + ESC RPM           [FC]
   → telemetry DL → remote display (MEASURED state) → pilot                                  [outer loop]
  • ANGLE mode: φ = r·θ_max, θ = −p·θ_max (FRD), ψ_sp integrates the yaw-rate command with the measured dt (limited by RC_DT_MAX_S), q_sp = q_z(ψ) ⊗ q_y(θ) ⊗ q_x(φ), T = t·T_max.
  • θ_max = ATT_CMD_TILT_MAX (full stick = exactly the cmd_guard limit), r_max = ½ of the attitude loop's yaw-rate limit (half the range is reserved for the correction term), T_max = maximum physical thrust.
  • Bumpless switching: while disarmed, or right after authority passes to the pilot ⇒ ψ_sp := ψ_measured.
  • Command authority: ANGLE ⇒ only RC feeds cmd_guard and Jetson commands are dropped (uros_app.c try_submit, on_arm); AUTO ⇒ only the Jetson. RC lost while the pilot holds authority ⇒ nobody feeds cmd_guard ⇒ the cmd_guard failsafe performs a bounded landing after CMD_TIMEOUT_S = 0.1 s = 5 frames. False-failsafe probability with independent packet loss p: p⁵ = 10⁻⁵ at p = 10 %.
  • Arm/disarm act on an EDGE between two consecutive fresh frames; arming must still pass cmd_guard_arm_check. KILL disarms on every frame while held and is latched until KILL is released and arm is switched off.
  • Stick failure (the remote sees an ADC stuck at a rail for ≥ 100 ms) ⇒ flag RFLINK_RC_STICK_FAULT ⇒ the FC feeds no set-point (entering the same proven failsafe path); ARM/KILL keep working.
  • RTH: the FC has no position loop yet ⇒ the request is only forwarded to the Jetson through the rc_rth_request key of /jetowl/status.

docs.title: 9. Firmware integration
docs.text:
1. CubeMX: enable SPI5 (mode 0, prescaler 16 = 12.5 MHz), GPIO per board_config.h section 2.8, rising-edge EXTI on PE10 and PF3. Set BOARD_CUBEMX_PERIPHERALS_READY = 1.
  2. app_freertos.c already calls RfLinkApp_Start() (returns false while the peripherals are missing).
  3. Every other SPI5 user (FRAM) must take RfLinkApp_SpiLock().
  4. Key: python3 tools/rflink_keygen.py, then rebuild both firmwares.
  5. Host check: ctest --test-dir build-host (test_rflink, test_rc_input).

New status keys in /jetowl/status: rc_authority (0 none, 1 pilot, 2 Jetson), rc_fresh, rc_link_lq_pct, rc_rssi_dbm, rc_snr_db, rc_rth_request.

docs.title: 10. Still to be measured on hardware (no data yet — not to be guessed)
docs.text:
• Actual RxDone timing offset (d) and the remote's transmit jitter ⇒ confirm g = 3 ms.
  • Real antenna isolation between the two modules on the airframe (measure the DL leakage RSSI at the UL module).
  • Real SF6/BW812 sensitivity of the Core1121 (section 5 uses the vendor figure plus a noise model).
  • Packet error rate versus distance, to validate the Rayleigh model of section 7.

docs.title: Keep or drop TrustZone? — A comparison for the decision
docs.text:
Source

Snapshot of docs/TRUSTZONE_TRADEOFF.md from TNG-Blue/JetOwl_FlightControl at commit 23b5ac3 (submodule Microcontroller/JetOwl_FlightControl). Regenerate with Scripts/mkdocs_hooks/snapshot_submodules.py after updating the submodule.

Decide before writing much code. Changing this configuration requires regenerating from STM32CubeMX, and any code outside the USER CODE BEGIN/END blocks will be overwritten.

docs.title: 1. Current state
docs.text: JetOwl_FlightControl.ioc sets Mcu.ContextProject=SecureNSecure with 4 contexts. The result is a three-stage run-time boot chain (FSBL → AppliSecure → AppliNonSecure) plus a flash-programming tool (ExtMemLoader).

docs.title: 2. Actual RAM cost (figures from the linker scripts)
docs.text:
SRAM map of the N657 (from Drivers/CMSIS/Device/ST/STM32N6xx/Include/stm32n657xx.h:3015-3023):

Region NS address Size Used by SRAM1_AXI 0x24000000 1 MB all of it taken by AppliSecure (0x34000000–0x34100000) SRAM2_AXI 0x24100000 1 MB all of it taken by AppliNonSecure (0x24100000–0x24200000) SRAM3_AXI 0x24200000 448 KB free SRAM4_AXI 0x24270000 448 KB free SRAM5_AXI 0x242E0000 448 KB free SRAM6_AXI 0x24350000 448 KB free CACHEAXI_RAM 0x243C0000 256 KB free (NPU cache RAM) VENC_RAM 0x24400000 128 KB free (video-encoder RAM) BKPSRAM 0x2C000000 8 KB free (backup SRAM)

Conclusion on RAM cost: practically zero. AppliSecure takes all of SRAM1 (1 MB), yet 1792 KB in SRAM3–SRAM6 are completely unused, not counting CACHEAXI_RAM and VENC_RAM. A flight control firmware (even with matrix EKFs and log buffers) rarely exceeds a few hundred KB. RAM is not a reason to drop TrustZone on this chip.

Note: AppliSecure's 399K ROM + 624K RAM are the linker script's allocation, not the space actually used. The secure code is currently only a few hundred bytes. The region can be shrunk in AppliSecure/STM32N657XX_LRUN_s.ld to make room if needed.

docs.title: 3. An important finding: the FSBL and AppliNonSecure OVERLAP
docs.text:
• The FSBL occupies 0x34180000–0x34200000 = the upper half of SRAM2 (through the secure alias).
  • AppliNonSecure occupies 0x24100000–0x24200000 = all of SRAM2 (through the non-secure alias).

Since 0x34… and 0x24… are the same physical RAM, AppliNonSecure overwrites the FSBL's region.

This is by design — the FSBL has finished its job by the time the application runs. But it has a practical consequence:

The FSBL cannot keep state in its own RAM to hand over to the application. To pass data from the FSBL to the application (boot reason, selected OTA slot, boot-stage error code), another region must be used: BKPSRAM (0x2C000000, 8 KB) or the RTC backup registers. This is required for an A/B OTA implementation.

This holds for both options — dropping TrustZone does not make it go away.

docs.title: 4. Comparison
docs.text: Criterion Keep TrustZone (4 contexts) Drop TrustZone (FSBL + 1 application) RAM cost Negligible (1792 KB still free) Negligible Build steps 3 run-time images; Secure must be built first 2 run-time images Debugging Two contexts to attach; breakpoints do not cross the secure/non-secure boundary transparently One context, noticeably simpler Call overhead NSC calls through a veneer: a few tens of extra cycles + SG + checks. Negligible at low rates (arming, OTA); significant inside the 1 kHz loop None Peripheral configuration Every peripheral must be assigned a CID/security attribute through RIF in CubeMX. A wrong assignment → IAC fault at run time, hard to diagnose No assignment needed Safety benefit The motor arming latch, the OTA authentication key and a safety watchdog are out of reach of bugs in the flight application (a buffer overflow in the NMEA/LoRa parser cannot touch them) A bug in the application can touch everything Cost of switching later — Requires editing the .ioc + regenerating; the later it is done, the more code is lost

docs.title: 5. Recommendation
docs.text:
Keep TrustZone, under two conditions:

  1. Draw the boundary correctly. The whole flight control loop (1 kHz) runs entirely in the non-secure state, with no NSC calls inside the loop. The secure side keeps only three jobs, all at very low rates:

    • the motor arm/disarm latch (called a few times per flight),
    • verification of the OTA image signature before a slot swap is allowed,
    • a safety watchdog (if the non-secure application hangs, the secure side cuts the motor output).

    With this boundary the NSC veneer cost is not measurable within the 1 kHz loop's time budget.

  2. Assign every flight peripheral to non-secure by default in RIF. Keep in secure only what belongs to the three jobs above. See docs/CUBEMX_SETUP.md.

Reason for keeping it: the measurable cost is debugging complexity, not RAM or speed. The benefit — isolating the motor safety latch from parsers of external data (NMEA from the GNSS, LoRa packets from the ground, firmware from the OTA network) — addresses exactly the kind of risk an unmanned aircraft must defend against: those parsers process data controlled by outside parties, and a bug there must never lead to motors spinning unintentionally.

Drop TrustZone when: you are at the prototype stage, value iteration/debug speed over product safety, and accept that the architecture will have to be reworked before a product release.

docs.title: 6. If you decide to drop TrustZone — procedure
docs.text:
1. Open JetOwl_FlightControl.ioc in STM32CubeMX.
  2. Project Manager → change the context configuration: remove the Secure/NonSecure pair and keep the FSBL + a single Appli (Mcu.ContextProject will no longer be SecureNSecure).
  3. Generate Code.
  4. Clean up manually: delete AppliSecure/, Secure_nsclib/ and the line DEPENDS JetOwl_FlightControl_AppliSecure if CubeMX does not remove them.
  5. Remove the -mcmse flag from the remaining application's CMakeLists.txt.
  6. Application/ and Drivers/JetOwl/ need no changes — they sit at the top level precisely so that they survive this change; only target_sources/target_include_directories in the new application's CMakeLists.txt must point to them again.

Do this before writing application code. The more is written inside Core/, the riskier the regeneration becomes.

docs.title: Remote_UAV — ground controller for the JetOwl UAV
Remote_UAV — ground controller for the JetOwl UAV
docs.text:
Source

This page is rendered from Microcontroller/Remote_UAV/README.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in Microcontroller/Remote_UAV/.

Arduino GIGA R1 WiFi + GIGA Display Shield + 2 × Waveshare Core1121-XF (Semtech LR1121) forming a full-duplex link: one module only transmits commands (2.4 GHz, frequency hopping, 50 Hz), the other only receives telemetry (second band, 10 Hz). The far end is the JetOwl_FlightControl firmware (STM32N657).

Item Reference Version 2.1.0 (CHANGELOG.md) Link design (mathematics, timing, security) docs/LINK_DESIGN.md Stick signal chain (filtering, calibration) docs/SIGNAL_CHAIN.md Wiring docs/WIRING.md User interface, gestures, Wi-Fi / Bluetooth docs/UI.md

docs.title: 1. Architecture
docs.text:
Remote_UAV/
├── Remote_UAV.ino              only calls remote::app_begin() / app_loop()
├── src/
│   ├── app/                    pin and timing configuration, shared state, thread start-up
│   ├── input/                  stick_dsp.c (pure C, unit-tested) + 500 Hz thread: sticks, buttons, calibration
│   ├── net/                    Wi-Fi + Bluetooth LE (own thread, commands through a queue)
│   ├── radio/                  LR1121 port layer for mbed + uplink / downlink threads
│   ├── rflink/                 SHARED LIBRARY — identical to JetOwl_FlightControl/Application/RfLink
│   ├── storage/                calibration stored in KVStore (CRC-32)
│   ├── system/                 watchdog, RGB LED, buzzer
│   └── ui/                     LVGL 9: dashboard, pull-down drawer, Wi-Fi/BT pages, keyboard, Vietnamese font
├── tests/host/                 C tests on the host (stick_dsp, rflink, ui_logic)
├── tests/sim/                  full LVGL user-interface simulation on the host (scenarios + screenshots)
├── tools/gen_fonts.sh          regenerates the Vietnamese font
└── docs/
Thread Priority Period Job uplink Realtime 20 ms (hardware Ticker) RC frame → AES-CMAC → channel hop → transmit input High 2 ms ADC → median of 3 → 2nd-order Butterworth → calibration → 3σ deadband → expo; buttons; battery downlink AboveNormal interrupt-driven receive telemetry, authenticate, LQ/RSSI/SNR supervisor AboveNormal 250 ms watchdog (kicked only when every thread is on time), LED, buzzer ui BelowNormal 5 ms LVGL / 100 ms data display + touch (LVGL runs in this thread only) net Low on command Wi-Fi / BLE (blocking calls), not supervised by the watchdog

Everything the screen shows about the aircraft comes from measured telemetry (the feedback path to the pilot), never from the commands the remote has sent.

docs.title: 2. Build and flash
docs.text:
1. Arduino IDE 2.x or arduino-cli, board package Arduino Mbed OS Giga Boards (arduino:mbed_giga).
  2. Libraries (Library Manager): lvgl 9.2.2, Arduino_GigaDisplayTouch, ArduinoBLE. WiFi, Arduino_H7_Video (with lv_conf) and KVStore ship with the core. ArduinoGraphics is no longer required.
  3. Link key (mandatory before flight): in the JetOwl_FlightControl repository run python3 tools/rflink_keygen.py — it writes src/rflink/rflink_key_local.h in both repositories (already in .gitignore). Without this file the public default key is used: a compile-time warning, red text on the screen and a blinking LED.
  4. Open Remote_UAV.ino, select Arduino GIGA R1 → Upload. From the command line: 
    arduino-cli compile --fqbn arduino:mbed_giga:giga .
arduino-cli upload  --fqbn arduino:mbed_giga:giga -p /dev/ttyACM0 .
    (Test build: 861 KB flash of 1.97 MB, 256 KB static RAM of 524 KB.)
  5. First time only: run the examples STM32H747_System → QSPIFormat (QSPI partition for KVStore: calibration, saved Wi-Fi networks), then WiFiFirmwareUpdater (Wi-Fi/BT firmware of the Murata module) — once each.

The band plan and regulatory region are selected with RFLINK_PLAN / RFLINK_REGION in src/rflink/rflink_config.h (default: UL 2.4 GHz + DL 921.4 MHz AS923 for Vietnam). Both firmwares must use the same values. The LR1121 has no 1.2 GHz band — the chip supports 150–960 MHz, 2000–2100 MHz and 2400–2500 MHz.

docs.title: 3. Operation
docs.text:
Control Effect Sticks R/P/Y/T ANGLE mode: proportional tilt (≤ 35°), yaw = heading rate, throttle = linear thrust ARM (press) toggles the measured arm state; refused if throttle > 20 %, calibration is running, or a stick has failed KILL (hold) disarms immediately, latched on the FC until KILL is released and ARM is off — use a guarded switch MODE ANGLE (pilot flies) ↔ AUTO (Jetson flies); the screen shows the authority confirmed by the FC RTH sends a 1 s request, the FC forwards it to the Jetson (rc_rth_request) Screen Calibrate → Next → Next calibration: (1) sticks centred, throttle low; (2) move every stick to its full travel Swipe down from the top edge quick-settings drawer: tap Wi-Fi/Bluetooth = on/off; long-press = network list (password via the on-screen keyboard) / BLE devices (tap to connect)

The default screen is landscape 800 × 480. Wi-Fi/BLE are locked while the aircraft is ARMED so they cannot interfere with the 2.4 GHz uplink (docs/UI.md section 5).

Telemetry lost while the aircraft is ARMED ⇒ the buzzer sounds at 2 Hz. Uplink lost on the UAV ⇒ the FC performs a bounded autonomous landing after 0.1 s (cmd_guard); the remote does nothing.

docs.title: 4. Host tests
docs.text:
cmake -S tests/host -B build-host && cmake --build build-host
ctest --test-dir build-host --output-on-failure      # test_stick_dsp, test_rflink, test_ui_logic

cmake -S tests/sim -B build-sim && cmake --build build-sim -j      # needs lvgl 9.2.2 + the GIGA core
ctest --test-dir build-sim --output-on-failure        # swipe/tap/long-press/typing scenarios + heap
build-sim/ui_sim --shots /tmp/shots                   # screenshot of every step (PPM 800×480)

docs.title: 5. Not yet verified on hardware
docs.text: All code compiles for the GIGA and passes the host tests, but it has not run with real modules. Still to be measured: antenna isolation between the two modules and packet error rate versus distance (docs/LINK_DESIGN.md section 10); Wi-Fi/BLE on the Murata module, touch responsiveness and the real LVGL heap (docs/UI.md section 11).

docs.title: Link Design
docs.text: Copy of JetOwl_FlightControl/docs/RFLINK.md — the src/rflink/ library is identical to Application/RfLink/ there; update the document in both places.

docs.title: Full-duplex LoRa control link (Remote_UAV ↔ JetOwl_FlightControl)
docs.text:
Source

This page is rendered from Microcontroller/Remote_UAV/docs/LINK_DESIGN.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in Microcontroller/Remote_UAV/docs/.

Design document for Application/RfLink/ (a pure-C library, shared verbatim with Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL/Microcontroller/Remote_UAV/src/rflink/), Application/Control/Src/rc_input.c and Application/Interface/Src/rflink_app.c. Every figure below is either checked by a host test (tests/host/test_rflink.c, test_rc_input.c) or cited.

docs.title: 1. Hardware
docs.text:
Remote_UAV (ground) JetOwl_FlightControl (UAV) MCU Arduino GIGA R1 WiFi (STM32H747) + GIGA Display Shield STM32N657 (NUCLEO-N657X0-Q) UL module (uplink, commands) Core1121-XF #1 — transmit only, SPI1 (D11–D13) Core1121-XF #1 — receive only, SPI5 DL module (downlink, telemetry) Core1121-XF #2 — receive only, SPI (header D89–D91) Core1121-XF #2 — transmit only, SPI5

Chip: Semtech LR1121, 32 MHz TCXO at 3.0 V, RF switch on DIO5/DIO6 (table from the Waveshare BSP). Frequency ranges supported by the chip (Semtech lr1121_common.h): 150–960 MHz, 2000–2100 MHz (S-band), 2400–2500 MHz. The LR1121 has no 1.2 GHz band.

FC pins: Application/Interface/Inc/board_config.h sections 2.4 and 2.8. Remote pins: Remote_UAV/src/app/app_config.h and Remote_UAV/docs/WIRING.md.

docs.title: 2. Why full duplex needs TWO modules at EACH end
docs.text:
A LoRa transceiver is half-duplex: it cannot transmit and receive at the same time. Full duplex here is FDD (frequency-division duplex): each end has two modules, each module handles one direction only, and the two directions use two different bands and run simultaneously:

flowchart LR
    subgraph GND[Remote_UAV – GIGA R1]
        S[Sticks + buttons] --> F[Filtering + calibration] --> TXu[LR1121 UL<br/>TRANSMIT only]
        RXd[LR1121 DL<br/>RECEIVE only] --> UI[Display<br/>MEASURED state]
    end
    subgraph AIR[UAV – STM32N657]
        RXu[LR1121 UL<br/>RECEIVE only] --> RC[rc_input] --> CG[cmd_guard] --> AT[attitude_ctrl → rate_loop → ESC]
        IMU[IMU + ESC RPM] --> AT
        AT --> TLM[telemetry] --> TXd[LR1121 DL<br/>TRANSMIT only]
    end
    TXu -- "2.4 GHz FHSS, 50 Hz" --> RXu
    TXd -- "sub-GHz 921.4 MHz, 10 Hz" --> RXd

Consequences: there is no TX/RX turnaround time, telemetry never blocks commands, and command latency does not depend on traffic in the opposite direction.

docs.title: 2.1 Band choice: why commands use 2.4 GHz and telemetry sub-GHz (default)
docs.text:
Criterion Commands (UL) 2.4 GHz Telemetry (DL) sub-GHz Worldwide regulation ISM 2400–2483.5 MHz; FHSS with ≥ 15 channels is compliant under ETSI EN 300 328 §4.3.1.4 and FCC 15.247(a)(1)(iii) Region-dependent (AS923 / EU868 / US915) Bandwidth → ToA BW 812 kHz ⇒ ToA 5.2 ms ⇒ 50 Hz feasible BW 250 kHz ⇒ ToA 41 ms ⇒ 10 Hz Link budget sufficient for line of sight (section 5) large margin

TX→RX isolation on the same airframe. With a 13 dBm transmit antenna and a receive antenna d ≈ 10 cm apart: FSPL = 20 log₁₀(4πd/λ) ≈ 20 dB at 2.44 GHz ⇒ a blocker of ≈ −7 dBm at the receiver, while the wanted packet arrives near the sensitivity limit (≈ −105 dBm) ⇒ ≈ 98 dB of selectivity is needed. Placing the two directions in two bands ~1.5 GHz apart lets each module's matching network and antenna provide most of that; putting both at 2.4 GHz (RFLINK_PLAN_2G4_DUAL) is usable only with widely separated antennas.

Harmonics. rflink_check_config() rejects a configuration in which the 2nd or 3rd harmonic of the DL falls inside the UL range (a non-linear PA radiates its strongest harmonics at orders 2–3). 921.4 MHz → 1842.8 / 2764.2 MHz: outside 2402–2478 MHz.

S-band 2000–2010 MHz (RFLINK_PLAN_2G4_SBAND) is a mobile-satellite-service (MSS) band and requires a licence.

docs.title: 2.2 Three band plans (rflink_config.h)
docs.text:
RFLINK_PLAN UL DL DL ToA / period 2G4_SUBGHZ (default) 2402–2478 MHz, 20 channels, 4 MHz step 921.4 MHz (AS923, Vietnam) 41.1 ms / 100 ms — RFLINK_REGION_EU868 as above 869.525 MHz (g3, duty ≤ 10 %) 41.1 ms / 500 ms = 8 % — RFLINK_REGION_US915 as above 915 MHz, BW 500 kHz (DTS) 20.5 ms / 100 ms 2G4_SBAND as above 2005 MHz — licence required 25.3 ms / 100 ms 2G4_DUAL 2402–2447 MHz, 16 channels 2478 MHz 25.3 ms / 100 ms

To change the plan or region, add -DRFLINK_PLAN=... / -DRFLINK_REGION=... to both firmwares.

docs.title: 3. Physical layer and timing
docs.text:
Time on air from the Semtech formula (AN1200.13; lr11xx_radio_get_lora_time_on_air_numerator, tested against an independent implementation of the formula):

n_payload = 8 + max(ceil((8PL − 4SF + 28 + 16CRC − 20IH − 8FS) / (4(SF − 2DE))) · (CR + 4), 0)
T = (n_pre + 4.25 + 2FS + n_payload) · 2^SF / BW          FS = 1 when SF ≤ 6 (fine synch)
UL (RC) DL (TLM) SF / BW / CR 6 / 812 kHz / ⅘ 7 / 250 kHz / ⅘ Preamble 12 (SF6 requires ≥ 12) 8 Frame 21 B (9 header + 8 payload + 4 tag) 37 B (9 + 24 + 4) ToA 5.22 ms 41.08 ms Period 20 ms (50 Hz) 100 ms (10 Hz) Output power 13 dBm (HF PA maximum) 14 dBm

Command latency (stick → set-point in cmd_guard), mean: stick filter ≈ 28 ms (group delay of the 2nd-order Butterworth, f_c = 7.93 Hz, see Remote_UAV/src/input/stick_dsp.h) + frame wait T/2 = 10 ms + ToA 5.2 ms + processing < 1 ms + attitude-loop tick ≤ 4 ms ⇒ ≈ 46 ms.

docs.title: 4. Frequency hopping and synchronisation (rflink_fhss.h)
docs.text:
• The channel sequence is a permutation π of {0..19} (Fisher–Yates + xorshift32, seed derived from the master key). Frame number seq is transmitted on channel π[seq mod 20].
  • Lock: frame k received at r_k ⇒ listen immediately on π[k+1] with deadline D = r_k + T + g. Past the deadline ⇒ hop to π[k+2] before frame k+2 starts, with margin T − ToA − g = 20 − 5.22 − 3 = 11.8 ms > 0.
  • Clock drift: 100 ppm in total ⇒ still inside the g = 3 ms window after at most g/(εT) = 1500 consecutive lost frames; the "blind hopping" limit is set to 50 frames (1 s), after which the receiver enters SEARCH.
  • SEARCH: park on π[0]; since π is a permutation the transmitter visits that channel at least once every 20 frames ⇒ re-acquisition ≤ 20 × 20 ms = 0.4 s (no packet loss).

docs.title: 5. Link budget (theoretical, free space)
docs.text:
Sensitivity S = −174 + 10 log₁₀ BW + NF + SNR_min. From the Waveshare figure (−111 dBm at SF7/BW800) ⇒ NF ≈ 11.4 dB ⇒ SF6/BW812: S ≈ −108.5 dBm.

UL: PL_max = 13 + 2 + 2 − (−108.5) = 125.5 dB. Subtracting a 10 dB fading margin (Rayleigh P_out 10 %, section 7) ⇒ FSPL 115.5 dB ⇒ d = 10^((115.5 − 100.2)/20) km ≈ 5.8 km in free space at 2.44 GHz. The sub-GHz DL has far more margin (≈ 100 km in theory) ⇒ the UL limits the range — sufficient for visual-line-of-sight flight. The real range is lower (Fresnel zone, shadowing by the airframe, antennas).

docs.title: 6. Framing, authentication, replay protection (rflink_proto.h)
docs.text:
off size  field
0   1     hdr = (version << 4) | type        type 1 = RC, 2 = TLM
1   4     nonce_tx (current nonce of the transmitter)
5   4     seq      (frame counter of the transmitter)
9   N     payload
9+N 4     tag = AES-CMAC_Kdir(nonce_rx || frame[0..9+N))[0..3]
  • AES-128 (FIPS-197) + CMAC (NIST SP 800-38B), tested against the FIPS-197 C.1 and RFC 4493 vectors.
  • Per-direction keys K_UL, K_DL and the hopping seed are derived with a counter-mode KDF (NIST SP 800-108r1, PRF = CMAC) from a 128-bit master key (rflink_key.h).
  • Replay protection without non-volatile memory: the tag covers the receiver's random nonce (LR1121 GetRandomNumber, generated at boot) ⇒ a frame recorded before that boot carries a wrong tag. Within a session, seq must increase strictly. If the transmitter reboots (seq back to 0) ⇒ 3 frames with a valid tag but stale sequence ⇒ the receiver changes its nonce (rekey) ⇒ the transmitter learns the new nonce over the other direction ⇒ recovery (≈ 0.5 s).
  • 32-bit tag: forgery probability per frame 2⁻³²; at 50 frames/s this takes on average ~1.4 years of continuous attempts on the correct hopping channel.
  • The default key is public ⇒ warnings at compile time, on the remote's screen and on the LED. Generate a private key with python3 tools/rflink_keygen.py (writes rflink_key_local.h into both repositories, already in .gitignore).

docs.title: 7. Link-quality estimation (rflink_quality.h)
docs.text:
• LQ = fraction of frames received in a 64-frame window indexed by seq (an unbiased binomial estimator, σ ≤ 6.25 %).
  • RSSI/SNR are low-pass filtered (first order, τ = 0.5 s, backward Euler: a = T/(τ + T)).
  • Margin M = SNR_filtered − SNR_min(SF) (SX1276 table 13, SX1261/2 §6.1.1).
  • Grading by Rayleigh outage probability P_out = 1 − exp(−10^(−M/10)): GOOD when P_out ≤ 1 % (M ≥ 20.0 dB), FAIR when ≤ 10 % (M ≥ 9.8 dB), POOR otherwise (Goldsmith, Wireless Communications, §3.2.1). No hand-picked thresholds.

docs.title: 8. From stick to propeller (rc_input.h) — the loop stays closed
docs.text:
stick → median 3 → Butterworth 2 (Tustin, pre-warped) → calibration → 3σ deadband → expo   [remote]
   → LoRa UL → authentication → rc_input → cmd_guard → attitude_ctrl (250 Hz) → rate_loop (1 kHz)
   → rotor_speed → DShot → ESC;   feedback: IMU (attitude, angular rate) + ESC RPM           [FC]
   → telemetry DL → remote display (MEASURED state) → pilot                                  [outer loop]
  • ANGLE mode: φ = r·θ_max, θ = −p·θ_max (FRD), ψ_sp integrates the yaw-rate command with the measured dt (limited by RC_DT_MAX_S), q_sp = q_z(ψ) ⊗ q_y(θ) ⊗ q_x(φ), T = t·T_max.
  • θ_max = ATT_CMD_TILT_MAX (full stick = exactly the cmd_guard limit), r_max = ½ of the attitude loop's yaw-rate limit (half the range is reserved for the correction term), T_max = maximum physical thrust.
  • Bumpless switching: while disarmed, or right after authority passes to the pilot ⇒ ψ_sp := ψ_measured.
  • Command authority: ANGLE ⇒ only RC feeds cmd_guard and Jetson commands are dropped (uros_app.c try_submit, on_arm); AUTO ⇒ only the Jetson. RC lost while the pilot holds authority ⇒ nobody feeds cmd_guard ⇒ the cmd_guard failsafe performs a bounded landing after CMD_TIMEOUT_S = 0.1 s = 5 frames. False-failsafe probability with independent packet loss p: p⁵ = 10⁻⁵ at p = 10 %.
  • Arm/disarm act on an EDGE between two consecutive fresh frames; arming must still pass cmd_guard_arm_check. KILL disarms on every frame while held and is latched until KILL is released and arm is switched off.
  • Stick failure (the remote sees an ADC stuck at a rail for ≥ 100 ms) ⇒ flag RFLINK_RC_STICK_FAULT ⇒ the FC feeds no set-point (entering the same proven failsafe path); ARM/KILL keep working.
  • RTH: the FC has no position loop yet ⇒ the request is only forwarded to the Jetson through the rc_rth_request key of /jetowl/status.

docs.title: 9. Firmware integration
docs.text:
1. CubeMX: enable SPI5 (mode 0, prescaler 16 = 12.5 MHz), GPIO per board_config.h section 2.8, rising-edge EXTI on PE10 and PF3. Set BOARD_CUBEMX_PERIPHERALS_READY = 1.
  2. app_freertos.c already calls RfLinkApp_Start() (returns false while the peripherals are missing).
  3. Every other SPI5 user (FRAM) must take RfLinkApp_SpiLock().
  4. Key: python3 tools/rflink_keygen.py, then rebuild both firmwares.
  5. Host check: ctest --test-dir build-host (test_rflink, test_rc_input).

New status keys in /jetowl/status: rc_authority (0 none, 1 pilot, 2 Jetson), rc_fresh, rc_link_lq_pct, rc_rssi_dbm, rc_snr_db, rc_rth_request.

docs.title: 10. Still to be measured on hardware (no data yet — not to be guessed)
docs.text:
• Actual RxDone timing offset (d) and the remote's transmit jitter ⇒ confirm g = 3 ms.
  • Real antenna isolation between the two modules on the airframe (measure the DL leakage RSSI at the UL module).
  • Real SF6/BW812 sensitivity of the Core1121 (section 5 uses the vendor figure plus a noise model).
  • Packet error rate versus distance, to validate the Rayleigh model of section 7.

docs.title: Stick signal chain (Remote_UAV)
docs.text:
Source

This page is rendered from Microcontroller/Remote_UAV/docs/SIGNAL_CHAIN.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in Microcontroller/Remote_UAV/docs/.

Code: src/input/stick_dsp.{h,c} (pure C, tested by tests/host/test_stick_dsp.c) and src/input/input_task.cpp. Applicable rule: .claude/rules/control-systems.md.

potentiometer → 12-bit ADC @ 500 Hz → median of 3 → 2nd-order Butterworth (f_c = 7.93 Hz)
              → min/centre/max calibration → 3σ deadband → expo → 50 Hz RC frame

docs.title: 1. Sensor
docs.text:
Measurement model y[k] = x(t_k) + v[k]; 12-bit ADC (analogReadResolution(12)), f_s = 500 Hz = 10 × the uplink rate. The noise v (ADC + wiper) has its σ measured per axis during calibration.

Fault: a raw value stuck near 0 or 4095 (±8 counts) for ≥ 100 ms (= 5 uplink frames) ⇒ broken wiper or short to a supply rail ⇒ flag RFLINK_RC_STICK_FAULT: the FC ignores the stick values (bounded failsafe, as for a lost link); ARM/KILL keep working.

docs.title: 2. Outlier rejection
docs.text: Median of 3 samples: removes any single-sample spike regardless of amplitude (wiper bounce, interference from the 2.4 GHz transmit burst) while preserving monotonic edges (Tukey 1977). Delay: 1 sample = 2 ms.

docs.title: 3. Anti-aliasing filter
docs.text:
The stick values are resampled at 50 Hz when the frame is built ⇒ every component above f_N = 25 Hz aliases. 2nd-order Butterworth: |H(f)|² = 1 / (1 + (f/f_c)⁴). Requiring

|H(f_N)| ≤ −A dB:

f_c = f_N / (10^(A/10) − 1)^(1/4);   A = 20 dB  ⇒  f_c = 25 / 99^(1/4) = 7.93 Hz

Bilinear discretisation with pre-warping (Oppenheim & Schafer, §7.2), K = tan(π f_c / f_s): b0 = K²/(1 + √2K + K²), b1 = 2b0, b2 = b0, a1 = 2(K² − 1)/(…), a2 = (1 − √2K + K²)/(…). The test checks |H(0)| = 1, |H(f_c)| = −3.01 dB, |H(25 Hz)| ≤ −19.9 dB.

Cost: group delay at DC √2/(2π f_c) = 28 ms; phase lag 32° at 3 Hz (upper edge of the manual piloting bandwidth). The filter starts in the steady state of the first sample (no "throttle to zero" transient at power-on).

docs.title: 4. Calibration
docs.text:
Two on-screen steps (CAL → NEXT → NEXT), allowed only while the aircraft is disarmed:

  1. Sticks centred, throttle low: N = 200 samples per axis ⇒ mean + σ (Welford 1962). Relative error of the estimated σ: 1/√(2(N−1)) = 5 %.
  2. Move every stick to its full travel ⇒ min/max.

Piecewise-linear mapping per half: x ≥ centre → (x − c)/(max − c); x < centre → (x − c)/(c − min), clamped to [−1, 1]; throttle → [0, 1]. A calibration with a sweep < 200 counts is rejected. The result is stored in KVStore with an IEEE CRC-32.

docs.title: 5. Deadband from the measured noise
docs.text: d = 3σ / half_travel (99.73 % of Gaussian samples lie within ±3σ) ⇒ a centred stick reads exactly 0 — important because the FC integrates the yaw stick into a heading. Rescaled so the map stays continuous and still reaches ±1: y = sign(x)·max(|x| − d, 0)/(1 − d).

docs.title: 6. Expo (stick feel)
docs.text: y = (1 − e)x + e x³, e ∈ [0, 1]: odd, monotonic (y' = 1 − e + 3e x² > 0), y(±1) = ±1. Default e = 0.

docs.title: 7. Buttons
docs.text:
Integrating debounce (Ganssle 2008): the state changes when the input has been stable for 20 ms (measured contact bounce < 10 ms).

ARM closes the loop on the measured state: a press ⇒ desired = NOT(armed according to telemetry). If the FC has not reflected it after 1 s ⇒ the request is withdrawn and the FC's refusal reason is shown (high nibble of the reasons byte in the TLM frame: fc_arm_result_t). The arming throttle limit of 20 % equals the FC's ARM_THRUST_MAX_RATIO (thrust is linear in throttle), so the remote refuses exactly what the FC would refuse.

docs.title: 8. Remote battery
docs.text: V = ADC · 3.3/4095 · 3 (20 k/10 k divider), first-order filter τ = 1 s, evaluated every 50 ms (a = 0.05/1.05). Warning below 7.0 V = 3.5 V/cell (≈ 10 % capacity remaining).

docs.title: Display user interface (Remote_UAV)
docs.text:
Source

This page is rendered from Microcontroller/Remote_UAV/docs/UI.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in Microcontroller/Remote_UAV/docs/.

Code: src/ui/ (LVGL 9.2.2), src/net/connectivity.{h,cpp} (Wi-Fi / Bluetooth LE). Hardware-independent logic: src/ui/ui_logic.{h,c} (tested by tests/host/test_ui_logic.c). Full user-interface simulation on the host: tests/sim/ (section 9).

GIGA Display Shield 800 × 480, GT911 capacitive touch, landscape by default: Arduino_H7_Video(800, 480, GigaDisplayShield) on the native 480 × 800 panel with LV_DISPLAY_ROTATION_270; LVGL rotates the touch coordinates by the same transform, so no manual coordinate mapping is needed.

The on-screen text is in Vietnamese (section 10). This document gives the labels in English.

docs.title: 1. Layout
docs.text:
┌──────────── status bar (swipe down from here) ─────── Wi-Fi BT Battery ┐
│ SAFE/ARMED │ ANGLE ▶ PILOT/JETSON │ UL FAIR │ DL GOOD                   │
├──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ artificial horizon       │ telemetry: heading, thrust, TLM age,        │
│ (roll / pitch from FC)   │ UL/DL LQ RSSI SNR, margin, battery, RPM     │
├──────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ R ▭  P ▭  Y ▭  T ▭                    [Calibrate] [Next] [Cancel]      │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Everything the screen says about the aircraft comes from measured telemetry (the closed-loop feedback to the pilot), never from the commands the remote has sent.

LVGL layer Content File lv_screen_active() dashboard ui_dashboard.cpp lv_layer_top() Wi-Fi page, password page, Bluetooth page ui_wifi.cpp, ui_bt.cpp dimming layer + quick-settings drawer + top-edge strip ui_quick.cpp toast ui_common.cpp

docs.title: 2. Quick-settings drawer (swipe down)
docs.text: Gesture Result Swipe down from the top edge (28 px) the drawer follows the finger; released past half way or flung down ⇒ opens Tap the Wi-Fi / Bluetooth tile on/off Long-press the Wi-Fi tile (400 ms) turn on if off, scan, open the network list Long-press the Bluetooth tile turn on if off, scan for 6 s, open the device list Swipe up on the drawer, or tap the dimmed area close

docs.title: 2.1 Gesture constants
docs.text:
Taken from Android ViewConfiguration (AOSP frameworks/base/core/java/android/view/ViewConfiguration.java), converted from dp to the pixels of this display:

density:  √(800² + 480²) / 5.0 in = 186.6 ppi      1 dp = 1/160 in = 1.166 px
TOUCH_SLOP               8 dp   →  9.3 px    minimum movement that becomes a drag
MINIMUM_FLING_VELOCITY  50 dp/s → 58 px/s    release velocity that counts as a fling
status bar              24 dp   → 28 px      edge area that starts a drawer drag
DEFAULT_LONG_PRESS_TIMEOUT 400 ms            = LVGL's default long_press_time

docs.title: 2.2 Drawer model
docs.text:
Visible height h ∈ [0, H], H = 300 px.

  • Closed: press inside the edge area, h = clamp(y − y₀, 0, H).
  • Open: drag starting on the drawer, h = clamp(H + (y − y₀), 0, H).

The release velocity v is a first-order low-pass filter of the difference Δy/Δt. Time constant τ = 50 ms, backward-Euler discretisation: a = Δt / (τ + Δt).

Touch is read every Δt = 10 ms (UI_TOUCH_READ_MS, matching the GT911's ~100 Hz report rate), so a = 1/6:

  • A 1 px jitter on one sample (100 px/s in the difference) is reduced to ≤ 17 px/s, below the 58 px/s fling threshold.
  • A real fling (≥ 300 px/s) crosses the threshold after τ·ln(300/242) = 11 ms.

Decision on release, as on Android:

|v| ≥ v_fling  →  open = (v > 0)        (the fling direction wins)
otherwise       →  open = (h ≥ H/2)

After release the drawer animates to its final position in 200 ms (Android config_shortAnimTime, ease-out).

docs.title: 3. Wi-Fi
docs.text:
1. Long-press the Wi-Fi tile to open the list of scanned networks, sorted by RSSI. The connected network is listed first. Each row shows signal bars, SSID, WPA/Open and dBm.
  2. Tap a WPA network to open the password page with a phone-style on-screen keyboard (lv_keyboard):
    • abc, ABC and 1# layouts with letters, digits and symbols.
    • 👁 shows/hides the password.
    • ✓ or "Connect" connects.
  3. A WPA2-PSK passphrase must be 8–63 characters (IEEE 802.11i-2004, Annex H.4); a passphrase of the wrong length is not sent.
  4. Tap the connected network to open the Disconnect / Forget / Close dialog.
  5. After a successful connection the SSID and password are stored in KVStore (/kv/wifi_saved, CRC-32). At the next power-on the remote reconnects to this network.

The signal bars use the mapping of Android WifiManager.calculateSignalLevel (API ≤ 29): rssi ≤ −100 → 0, rssi ≥ −55 → L−1, otherwise ⌊(rssi + 100)(L − 1)/45⌋.

Security: the password is stored unencrypted in the GIGA's QSPI flash. Anyone with the board and a USB cable can read it. Do not use networks whose password matters; use "Forget" before handing the device over.

docs.title: 4. Bluetooth
docs.text:
The GIGA R1 supports Bluetooth Low Energy only (ArduinoBLE, central role). Bluetooth Classic (audio, SPP, pairing from a phone's Bluetooth menu) is not available on this board.

  • Long-press the Bluetooth tile to scan for BT_SCAN_MS = 6 s. Per Bluetooth Core v5.3 Vol 6 Part B §4.4.2.2 the advertising interval lies within 20 ms … 10.24 s, and connectable devices typically use ≤ 1.28 s, so 6 s sees each device ≥ 4 times.
  • The list shows the name (or "Unnamed"), address, signal bars and dBm.
  • Tap a device to connect; tap the connected device to disconnect.

docs.title: 5. Coexistence with the 2.4 GHz control link
docs.text:
Wi-Fi/BLE share the 2.4 GHz band with the LoRa uplink (FHSS 2402–2478 MHz, 20 channels, 4 MHz step).

  • One 20 MHz Wi-Fi channel overlaps 5 of the 20 hopping channels (25 %).
  • Wi-Fi scanning and handshakes transmit in bursts and can destroy RC frames that happen to hop onto those channels.
  • The FC tolerates 4 consecutive lost frames before entering failsafe (cmd_guard, 0.1 s).

Therefore, with NET_BLOCK_WHEN_ARMED = 1, while the aircraft is ARMED:

  • Switching on, scanning and connecting are refused, with a toast explaining why. "ARMED" here means the last ARMED state reported by telemetry (even when that telemetry is stale, since losing telemetry in flight is exactly when the uplink must not be disturbed), or a pending ARM request from the remote (arm_desired).
  • An existing connection is kept.

docs.title: 6. Threads and thread safety
docs.text:
Thread Priority Job ui BelowNormal lv_timer_handler() every 5 ms, data refresh every 100 ms (telemetry is 10 Hz) net Low every blocking Wi-Fi/BLE call (scanNetworks, begin, BLE.scan, connect)
  • LVGL is not thread-safe: only ui_begin() (before the threads start) and ui_task() call LVGL.
  • The UI sends requests to net through rtos::Mail<NetCmd, 8> and reads its state with net_snapshot() (mutex-protected), so the interface never freezes while scanning.
  • net is not among the threads supervised by the watchdog: WiFi.begin() may block for up to WIFI_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 s.

docs.title: 7. LVGL memory
docs.text:
Measured with lv_mem_monitor in the simulation (real LVGL + real UI code):

State Used Peak dashboard + pages + drawer + keyboard, no list rows 47 KiB 48 KiB + 24 Wi-Fi networks (NET_MAX_AP) 80 KiB 84 KiB + 20 BLE devices (NET_MAX_BT), Wi-Fi page closed 88 KiB 91 KiB
  • The default 64 KiB heap (LV_MEM_SIZE in the core's Arduino_H7_Video/src/lv_conf_9.h) overflows as soon as the first scan result arrives; LVGL then halts in LV_ASSERT_MALLOC. The simulation reproduces this failure exactly.
  • TLSF accepts pools of at most block_size_max = 2^⌈log₂ LV_MEM_SIZE⌉ = 64 KiB, so a single 96 KiB pool is silently rejected by lv_tlsf_add_pool.
  • ui_begin() therefore adds UI_LVGL_POOL_COUNT = 2 pools of 48 KiB each. Total usable memory is 152 KiB, 40 % above the 91 KiB peak.
  • A closed page frees its rows, so the two lists never coexist.
  • Transparent lists drop the theme's clip_corner, which forces LVGL to draw rounded corners through two 768 px-wide ARGB8888 layers occupying ~30 KiB each.
  • Signal bars are one custom-drawn object (LV_EVENT_DRAW_MAIN) instead of 4 child objects.
  • Every 10 s, Serial prints [UI] lvgl heap used … / … B, max … for checking on real hardware.

docs.title: 8. Artificial horizon
docs.text:
The aircraft symbol is fixed at the centre of the box. The world rotates by −roll, and pitch shifts the horizon by k = 120 px / 45° along the rotated vertical axis.

With c = cos(−φ), s = sin(−φ) and C the centre of the box:

body point (x, y) → screen  P = C + (x·c − y·s,  x·s + y·c)
horizon: y = off = θ·k ;  pitch ladder ±10/20/30°: y = off − δ·k
  • Lines (horizon, pitch ladder) are clipped to the box with Liang–Barsky (ACM TOG 3(1), 1984), because the points of an lv_line must lie inside the widget.
  • Ground is the half-plane n·P ≥ off + n·C with n = (−s, c). It is filled with one very thick line (ui_ground_band):
    • Every point of the box lies within R/2 of C, with R = √(w² + h²). Their signed distance to the horizon therefore lies in [s_c − R/2, s_c + R/2], with s_c = n·C − d.
    • The band [max(0, s_c − R/2), s_c + R/2] covers exactly the ground. Its lower edge is the horizon whenever the horizon crosses the box.
    • A host test checks 25 roll/pitch combinations on a 5 px grid: no point is misclassified.
  • Triangles are not used because LVGL 9.2's software triangle rasteriser fills triangles with a vertical edge incorrectly, and every polygon clipped to the box has such edges (the defect was observed in the simulation).

docs.title: 9. Host simulation
docs.text:
cmake -S tests/sim -B build-sim && cmake --build build-sim -j
ctest --test-dir build-sim --output-on-failure        # ui_scenario, ui_scenario_worst_case_heap
build-sim/ui_sim --shots /tmp/shots                   # 800×480 PPM screenshot of each step
cmake -S tests/sim -B build-sim -DUI_SIM_SANITIZE=ON  # ASan + UBSan (slower)

The simulation uses the same LVGL library and lv_conf_9.h as the GIGA core (with only Arm-2D disabled) and the real src/ui/ code. Taps and swipes are injected through a fake input device at the firmware's own timing. The scenario checks the effect of each step:

  1. Swipe the drawer open, then tap the Wi-Fi tile: wifi_on.
  2. Long-press the Wi-Fi tile: the network list is scanned.
  3. Tap a WPA network: the keyboard appears.
  4. Type matkhau123 (switching to the 1# layout) and press ✓: net_wifi_connect("TNG-Blue_Lab", "matkhau123").
  5. Long-press the Bluetooth tile: switched on and scanning. Tap a device: connects to the correct address.
  6. Swipe up to close the drawer, tap "Calibrate": the EVT_CAL_START flag is set.
  7. LVGL heap peak ≤ 80 % of the total pool (--worst: full lists of 24 + 20).

Requires the lvgl 9.2.2 library in ~/Arduino/libraries and the arduino:mbed_giga core (found automatically, or pass -DLVGL_DIR=… -DGIGA_VIDEO_DIR=…).

docs.title: 10. Vietnamese font

Regenerate with:

docs.title: 11. Not yet verified on hardware
docs.text:
The code compiles for the GIGA (arduino-cli compile --fqbn arduino:mbed_giga:giga) and runs correctly in the simulation, but has not run on a real board. Still to be checked:

  • Wi-Fi/BT firmware of the Murata 1DX module, stored in QSPI. The first time, run the example STM32H747_System → QSPIFormat, then WiFiFirmwareUpdater.
  • Real Wi-Fi scan and connection times; Wi-Fi and BLE active at the same time on the same chip.
  • Actual GT911 report rate on the shield (read register 0x8056); smoothness of the drawer drag.
  • The [UI] lvgl heap line on Serial with full lists, compared with the simulated figures of section 7.
  • RC frame loss while Wi-Fi is active in the DISARMED state (pre-flight preparation).

Source

docs.title: The two Core1121-XF LoRa modules
docs.text:
The two modules sit on two independent SPI buses of the GIGA (variants/GIGA/pins_arduino.h): SPI1 = D11/D12/D13 and SPI = the 6-pin header (D89 CIPO, D90 COPI, D91 SCK).

Core1121-XF UL module (transmit only, 2.4 GHz) DL module (receive only) 3V3 / GND 3V3 / GND 3V3 / GND CLK D13 (SPI1 SCK) D91 (SPI SCK, header) MOSI D11 (SPI1 COPI) D90 (SPI COPI, header) MISO D12 (SPI1 CIPO) D89 (SPI CIPO, header) CS D10 D6 BUSY D9 D5 DIO9 (IRQ) D8 D4 RESET D7 D3 Antenna 2.4 GHz antenna antenna for the DL band (sub-GHz by default)
  • The Core1121-XF kit includes both a sub-GHz and a 2.4 GHz antenna: each module must use the antenna for its own band. A wrong-band antenna removes the out-of-band filtering that full duplex depends on (docs/LINK_DESIGN.md section 2.1).
  • Place the two antennas as far apart as possible, with orthogonal polarisation if feasible.
  • The 2.4 GHz module transmits at 13 dBm ⇒ ~25 mA; the sub-GHz receiver draws ~9 mA (Waveshare). The GIGA's 3V3 supply is sufficient.

docs.text:
Signal Pin Notes Roll / pitch / yaw / throttle stick A0 / A1 / A2 / A3 10 kΩ potentiometer between 3V3 and GND, wiper to the pin Remote battery A4 20 k / 10 k divider (2S Li-ion → ≤ 2.8 V) ARM / KILL / MODE / RTH / AUX D2 / D14 / D15 / D16 / D17 push buttons to GND (internal pull-up) Buzzer D18 active buzzer, high = on Status LED on-board RGB LED green = good link, yellow = poor, red = lost

Avoid D22–D53: those pins share STM32 pins with the Display Shield's LTDC interface. D14–D17 are UART pins (Serial3/Serial4) — they can be used as GPIO because the firmware does not open those ports.

docs.title: JetOwl Vision
docs.text:
Source

Snapshot of README.md from TNG-Blue/JetOwl_Vision at commit 09cd68c (submodule Microcontroller/JetOwl_Vision). Regenerate with Scripts/mkdocs_hooks/snapshot_submodules.py after updating the submodule.

Vision firmware for the STM32N655 (Cortex-M55, VFBGA264) running FreeRTOS: it reads an IMX335 MIPI CSI-2 camera through the CSI host + DCMIPP, runs closed-loop auto-exposure (AE) and auto white balance (AWB), and is prepared for AI inference with X-CUBE-AI.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• MIPI CSI-2 camera: IMX335, 2 lanes RAW10 → DCMIPP ISP pipe 1 (black level, WB gain, demosaicing, statistics, downsizing 2592×1944 → 640×480, gamma) → RGB565 in AXISRAM3..6.
  • FreeRTOS (CMSIS-RTOS2): a camera thread woken by the frame IRQ, a lock-free buffer ring, CAM_AcquireFrame / CAM_ReleaseFrame API.
  • Closed-loop AE/AWB following the chain measurement → Kalman filter (disturbance estimation) → certainty-equivalence control → actuator quantisation → sensor → feedback:
    • Log-domain model \(z_k = u_{k-D} + d_k + v_k\), scene disturbance as a random walk.
    • Steady-state Kalman gain from the closed-form solution of the scalar Riccati equation.
    • Stability proven with the Jury / Schur–Cohn criterion, with margins for gain error \(\alpha\) and delay error; zero steady-state error (integral action).
    • Handling of saturated (censored) measurements; rate limiting and actuator saturation without windup.
  • I2C TIMINGR computed from the constraints of UM10204 and RM0486.
  • micro-ROS over UDP/Ethernet to the Jetson (ETH1 + LAN8742 RMII + lwIP 2.2.1): the jetowl_vision node publishes /jetowl_vision/image_preview (sensor_msgs/Image rgb8 160×120, 5 Hz, reliable) and /jetowl_vision/status (diagnostic_msgs/DiagnosticStatus, 1 Hz). The preview passes through an anti-aliasing box filter before decimation, error ≤ 0.5 LSB (host test). On the Jetson it is read by the vision_mcu link of ros2_jetowl_bridge (Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL). Details: docs/network/MICROROS_ETHERNET.md.
  • A/B OTA through Server_OTA (192.168.1.101:8080): a bootloader in the FSBL selects the slot, verifies SHA-256, loads into RAM, runs a new image on trial under the IWDG and rolls back automatically after 3 attempts if the image does not confirm itself healthy; downloads resume with HTTP Range and are checked at 4 levels; controlled through the micro-ROS services /jetowl_vision/ota/start, /jetowl_vision/ota/apply. The OTA layer is identical to JetOwl_FlightControl's. Details: docs/network/OTA.md.

Details, formulas and references: docs/camera/CAMERA_CSI_RTOS.md.
