docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Not yet run against hardware: bench / HIL evidence (control-systems.md §4) is still to be produced for all links. 0.4.0 built and tested (62 gtests in 9 suites) on ROS 2 Humble (ros:humble-ros-base).
  • FC: the firmware IMU path needs I2C1 + EXTI in CubeMX (BOARD_CUBEMX_PERIPHERALS_READY = 1); Imu covariances from the FC are zero ("unknown") until its Allan-variance log is recorded; header stamps are in agent time (rmw_uros_sync_session every 10 s).
  • vision_mcu: the JetOwl_Vision firmware has not run on hardware; its RMII pins/PHY are board items to check against the schematic. No CameraInfo is published: the IMX335 module has not been calibrated (intrinsics unknown), so none is invented.
  • Sensor link: clock-sync noise parameters of the STM32N6 board's timer clock (allan_dev_1s, random_walk_fm) are assumptions; measure the Allan deviation of the offset and update config/sensor_link.yaml.
  • Sensor link: quantisation noise of a slow or stopped encoder is not white; the reported speed σ is then optimistic.
  • Sensor link: imu/data orientation covariance uses roll/pitch/yaw variances on the diagonal (small-angle approximation of the rotation-vector covariance).
  • Sensor link: no authentication/encryption on the link: it is meant for a dedicated vehicle Ethernet segment.

docs.title: ROS2_Mission_Planner — mission layer above the flight controller
docs.text:
Source

This page is rendered from Source/ROS2_Mission_Planner/README.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in Source/ROS2_Mission_Planner/.

ros2_mission_planner 0.3.0 loads a mission and checks that it can be flown before arming. It then sequences the mission through ros2_flight_controller and supervises it until touchdown. The flight controller (FC) keeps the safety authority and runs the flight: trajectory, position loop and failsafes. The planner never commands velocities or set-points. It sends waypoint legs and navigation commands, then watches what the FC and the vehicle actually do.

 mission YAML / WaypointList ─▶ loader ─▶ survey / orbit generators ─▶ waypoints + keep-out zones
                                                                          │
     pre-flight analysis on the FC's own min-jerk trajectory (limits read from the FC):
     clearance to geofence + keep-out zones, detours, energy with the wind bound ─▶ accept / refuse
                                                                          │
 odometry/filtered ──┐                                                    ▼
 flight/status ──────┤                         ┌─▶ flight/waypoints (one leg, detour points included)
 battery/state ──────┼─▶ MissionExecutive ─────┤
 control/disturbance ┘    (10 Hz) state machine └─▶ flight/nav_command (ARM, TAKEOFF, START, HOVER,
       ▲                  + monitors + wind /                          RTH, LAND, DISARM)
       │                  power estimators
       └──── FC ─▶ ros2_control_system (MPC + ESKF) ─▶ vehicle ─▶ sensors ──┘

The loop is closed at mission level. A leg ends only when the FC reports HOVER and the measured position is inside the waypoint's acceptance radius. The FC's failsafes (RTH, LANDING, EMERGENCY_STOP, manual joystick) are followed rather than fought. The planner commands a return or a landing on its own in three cases:

  • the odometry goes stale (landing);
  • the vehicle leaves the geofence or enters a keep-out zone (return home);
  • the battery reaches the energy needed to return with the reserve (return home).

EMERGENCY_STOP (→ EMERGENCY) and RESET (→ IDLE) are accepted from every state; LAND from every airborne state.

stateDiagram-v2

    IDLE --> PREFLIGHT: START_MISSION
    PREFLIGHT --> TAKEOFF: PREFLIGHT_OK
    PREFLIGHT --> IDLE: ABORT

    HOLDING --> NAVIGATING: HOLD_COMPLETE
    NAVIGATING --> RTL: ALL_WAYPOINTS / ABORT
    HOLDING --> RTL: ALL_WAYPOINTS / ABORT
    NAVIGATING --> LANDING: LAND
    HOLDING --> LANDING: LAND
    RTL --> LANDING: RTL_REACHED / LAND

docs.title: Design (control-systems.md §5)
docs.text:
MISSION DESIGN
  Inputs      : odometry/filtered (ESKF, 100 Hz), flight/status (FC, 10 Hz), battery/state (BMS:
                SoC, V, I), control/disturbance (MPC d̂, 50 Hz), FC parameters (services + events)
  Filters     : SoC first-order low-pass α = T/(τ + T), τ = 5 s; measured/model power ratio
                low-pass τ = 20 s; odometry is already filtered by the ESKF
  Estimators  : wind: drag-law inversion of m d̂_xy + random-walk Kalman filter, 95 % disc
                ρ_w = 2.45 σ; power ratio r = max(1, r̂); energy-to-return along the planned
                return route with the wind disc
  Supervisor  : finite state machine IDLE → PREFLIGHT → TAKEOFF → NAVIGATING ⇄ HOLDING → RTL →
                LANDING → COMPLETE; EMERGENCY from any state; in-flight mission change
  Actuation   : legs of waypoints + START, acknowledged by the FC mode, re-sent after ack_timeout
                (3 retries), leg deadline 2·T_planned + 30 s; return = FC RTH or detour waypoints
  Loop        : closed on the FC's measured mode and odometry; watchdog 0.5 s → LAND
  Guarantees  : (1) clearance: c(p) (fence ∧ keep-out) is 1-Lipschitz ⇒ samples every Δt with
                    c ≥ v_pk·Δt/2 + margin keep the whole continuous path clear
                (2) detours: edges tangent to the inflated circle + FC path-deviation bound e_max
                    ⇒ c ≥ margin + v̄Δt/2 along the flown path by construction
                (3) energy: P̄(v, a, ŵ, ρ_w) ≥ P(v, a, w) for every wind in the disc; accept iff
                    SoC − 100·k·r·E/E_usable ≥ reserve; RTL when SoC_f ≤ reserve + 100·k·r·E_ret/E_usable
  Verification: 53 gtest cases (fake-FC executive tests included); SIL of the whole stack with a
                3.4 m/s wind, +10 % mass and aerodynamic drag: 4 scenarios, all checks pass
  Reference   : Richter, Bry & Roy 2013 (min-jerk); Leishman, Principles of Helicopter
                Aerodynamics §2.14, §5.4 (momentum theory, power); Simon, Optimal State
                Estimation §5.1 (Kalman filter); Galceran & Carreras 2013 (coverage)

docs.title: Clearance along the trajectory, not only at the waypoints
docs.text:
The signed clearance c(p) is the minimum of these terms:

  • Horizontal fence: for the cylinder around home, R − ‖p_xy − home_xy‖. For a polygon, ± the distance to its nearest edge.
  • Altitude: z − z_min and z_max − z.
  • Keep-out zones: for each vertical cylinder {‖p_xy − c‖ ≤ r, z ≤ top} (a mast, a tree line, a building), its exact signed distance:
    • d_r = ‖p_xy − c‖ − r and d_z = z − top;
    • √(d_r² + d_z²) above the rim, max(d_r, d_z) elsewhere.

Each term is 1-Lipschitz, because the signed distance to a convex set is. Their minimum is therefore 1-Lipschitz too: |c(p) − c(q)| ≤ ‖p − q‖.

The analysis evaluates the same minimum-jerk trajectory the FC will fly (ros2_flight_controller::MinJerkTrajectory, with the FC's own limits) every Δt = 0.1 s. Between two samples, any point lies within v_pk·Δt/2 of one of them. So c ≥ v_pk·Δt/2 + margin at every sample proves c > 0 on the whole path. A leg can have all its waypoints inside and still be rejected when the path between them crosses a notch of the fence (test RejectsPathThroughKeepOutNotch).

docs.title: Detours around keep-out zones
docs.text:
A segment AB that enters a zone is rerouted around it:

  1. Inflate the zone. Its radius becomes ρ = r + margin + v̄Δt/2 + b. The buffer b is at least the FC's trajectory.max_path_deviation_m.
  2. Build the detour. AB is replaced by A → V_0 … V_{n−1} → B. The V_k are the vertices of the polygon circumscribed about the circle ρ between the tangent points of A and B:
    • vertex radius ρ / cos(δ/2);
    • δ ≤ 45°;
    • the shorter side is tried first.
  3. Why it clears. Every edge lies on a tangent line of the circle, so the polyline stays at least ρ from the centre. The FC keeps the flown trajectory within e_max ≤ b of the polyline. Because c is 1-Lipschitz, the clearance test therefore passes by construction.
  4. Verify anyway. The test still runs, because the outer fence or other zones can interfere. If it fails, the other side and larger buffers are tried.

The return path works the same way. When the FC's straight RTH is clear, the planner sends RTH. Otherwise it flies the verified detour route as waypoints and sends LAND above home.

A zone taller than the RTH altitude raises a warning at start. The reason is that a failsafe RTH decided by the FC itself flies straight and does not know the zones.

The FC-side fix that makes the detour guarantee hold is described in its changelog. The minimum-jerk spline could leave the waypoint polyline by tens of metres; the FC now bounds that deviation by adding stops at the offending knots.

docs.title: Energy with wind
docs.text:
Electrical power in steady flight comes from momentum theory (Leishman §2.14, §5.4). The inputs are the ground velocity v, the acceleration a and the wind w, with air velocity V_a = v − w:

F_aero = −(½ρ C_D A ‖V_a‖ V_a + c_H V_a,xy)        C_D A = 0.05 m², c_H = Σ k_H ω_hover = 0.571 N·s/m
f      = m a + m g e_z − F_aero,  T = ‖f‖            required rotor force
P      = P_hover (T / m g)^{3/2} + max(0, f·V_a) / η_p     P_hover = 383 W, η_p = 0.5
  • First term. It is exact for the static propeller model: T ∝ ω² and P ∝ ω³, so P ∝ T^{3/2}. In forward flight it is an upper bound, because the induced velocity drops below its hover value.
  • Second term. It is the climb and parasitic power.
  • Bound over the wind disc. P̄(v, a, ŵ, ρ_w) bounds P for every wind with ‖w − ŵ‖ ≤ ρ_w. It follows from the triangle inequality and the monotonicity of the drag law; the proof is in mission_analysis.h, and it is checked on 20 000 random cases in Power.HoverAndBoundDominatesModel.
  • Where the wind disc comes from. Before take-off it is ŵ = 0 with ρ_w = the design wind (5 m/s, any direction). In flight it is the estimate below.

Mission energy is E = ∫ P̄ dt over take-off, every planned leg, holds, the return and the landing. A mission is accepted when SoC − 100·k·r·E / E_usable ≥ reserve, with k = 1.2 and E_usable = 88.8 Wh.

Wind estimate. The MPC disturbance observer of ros2_control_system publishes the unmodelled acceleration d̂ on control/disturbance.

  • In steady flight the horizontal aerodynamic force is F = m d̂_xy, and it satisfies F = −D(‖V_a‖) V_a/‖V_a‖.
  • The drag law D(V) = ½ρC_DA V² + c_H V is strictly increasing, so it inverts uniquely: ‖V_a‖ = (−c_H + √(c_H² + 2ρC_DA‖F‖)) / (ρC_DA).
  • The wind measurement is then w_meas = v_xy + F ‖V_a‖/‖F‖.
  • A random-walk Kalman filter gives ŵ and σ. The disc ρ_w = 2.45 σ holds the truth with 95 % probability for an isotropic 2-D Gaussian (1 − e^{−3}).

Measured-power correction. When the BMS reports voltage and current, the planner computes r̂ = LPF(V·|I| / P(v, 0, ŵ)) and uses r = max(1, r̂). The model is only ever scaled up, so it stays an upper bound. This covers a heavier payload, an aged battery or cold air.

docs.title: Flight-controller profile read at run time
docs.text:
The planner reads these parameters from the FC's parameter services at start-up and again on every change the FC announces on /parameter_events:

  • speed limits, velocity-loop time constants, acceleration and minimum segment time;
  • take-off altitude, landing descent speed, RTH altitude and RTH speed;
  • the path-deviation bound.

The profile is then computed by the FC's own PositionController::trajectory_limits(). With flight_controller.require_sync: true, mission/start is refused until the parameters have been read.

docs.title: In-flight mission change
docs.text:
A mission uploaded while NAVIGATING or HOLDING goes through these steps:

  1. It is analysed from the current position. The analysis uses the current SoC, the wind disc and the power ratio, and assumes no take-off.
  2. If it is feasible, the planner sends HOVER and waits for the FC to hover.
  3. It then continues with the new plan. Home is unchanged.

An infeasible mission is rejected, and the running mission continues.

docs.title: Patterns
docs.text: Pattern Rule Example Survey (boustrophedon) footprint W = 2h·tan(FOV/2), spacing s = W(1 − overlap), n = ⌈H/s⌉ + 1 lines; every point of the area is within W/2 of a line 50 × 40 m at 12 m, FOV 70°, overlap 0.3 → s = 11.8 m, 5 lines Orbit chord sagitta e = R(1 − cos(π/N)) ⇒ N = ⌈π / acos(1 − e/R)⌉ points per turn (smallest N with error ≤ e) R = 15 m, e = 0.2 m → N = 20

docs.title: Mission file
docs.text:
mission:
  name: "demo square"
  frame: home            # home (relative to the arming position, default) | odom
  end_action: rtl        # rtl | land | hover
  defaults: {acceptance_radius: 1.5, hold_time: 0.0}
  waypoints:
    - {x: 10, y: 0, z: 5, heading_deg: 0, hold_time: 2.0}
    - {x: 10, y: 10, z: 5, action: navigate}   # navigate | takeoff | land | rtl | hover
  survey: {...}          # optional, appended after the waypoints (see config/missions/)
  orbit: {...}
  keep_out:              # optional known obstacles, same frame as the waypoints
    - {name: mast, x: 12, y: 0, radius: 3, top: 20}   # top omitted = unlimited height

The altitude z and the zone top are relative to the take-off point (AGL at home) when frame: home. Per-waypoint speed fields are ignored with a warning, because the FC's trajectory limits set the speed.

Examples:

  • config/waypoint_mission.yaml
  • config/missions/survey_example.yaml
  • config/missions/orbit_example.yaml
  • config/missions/keep_out_example.yaml
  • config/missions/retask_example.yaml (in-flight upload)

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
Kind Name Type Notes sub odometry/filtered nav_msgs/Odometry ESKF of ros2_control_system; twist in the child frame (REP-105) sub flight/status std_msgs/String FC mode (mode:XXX …) sub battery/state sensor_msgs/BatteryState percentage in [0, 1]; voltage·|current| = power sub control/disturbance geometry_msgs/Vector3Stamped MPC d̂ [m/s²] → wind estimate sub mission/upload std_msgs/String mission YAML text (also in flight) sub mission/upload_waypoints ros2_mission_planner/msg/WaypointList frame_id odom = absolute, otherwise home-relative pub flight/waypoints geometry_msgs/PoseArray one leg, frame odom, detour points included pub flight/nav_command std_msgs/String ARM, TAKEOFF, START, HOVER, RTH, LAND, DISARM pub mission/status ros2_mission_planner/msg/MissionStatus state, progress, SoC / required SoC, wind + radius, power ratio pub mission/geofence ros2_mission_planner/msg/GeofenceStatus clearance, binding constraint, keep-out name pub mission/preview nav_msgs/Path planned route (with detours after start), transient local pub mission/diagnostics diagnostic_msgs/DiagnosticArray srv mission/start, mission/abort, mission/reset, mission/reload std_srvs/Trigger

The mission can start only while the FC is DISARMED. start first runs the analysis with home at the current position and the design wind. After arming, it re-runs the analysis with the home recorded at arming.

Parameters: config/mission_planner_params.yaml. Every value is tagged with its source: vehicle, FC (read at run time), or assumption.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
The interfaces are generated in this package (sources in msgs/msg/, types ros2_mission_planner/msg/*):

Message Topic Content MissionStatus mission/status state, progress, SoC and SoC needed to return, wind estimate with its 95 % radius, measured-power ratio, return route type GeofenceStatus mission/geofence signed clearance, binding constraint (range, polygon, altitude, keep-out zone) WaypointList mission/upload_waypoints waypoints with acceptance radii, hold times, actions, end action; header.frame_id: odom = absolute, otherwise relative to home

The STATE_* and VIOLATION_* constants equal MissionState and GeofenceViolation. A package that only needs the messages still depends on the whole planner (and through it on ros2_flight_controller).

ros2 interface show ros2_mission_planner/msg/MissionStatus
ros2 topic echo /mission/status

docs.title: Launch
docs.text:
# Planner only (FC and control stack already running)
ros2 launch ros2_mission_planner mission_planner.launch.py \
  mission_file:=$(ros2 pkg prefix ros2_mission_planner)/share/ros2_mission_planner/config/waypoint_mission.yaml
ros2 service call /mission/start std_srvs/srv/Trigger

# Whole stack: control system + flight controller + mission planner
ros2 launch ros2_mission_planner autonomous_mission.launch.py auto_start:=true

# Re-task in flight
ros2 topic pub --once /mission/upload std_msgs/msg/String "{data: '$(cat retask.yaml)'}"

docs.title: Build and test
docs.text:
colcon build --packages-up-to ros2_mission_planner
colcon test --packages-select ros2_mission_planner && colcon test-result --verbose

The full-stack SIL runs the planner, the FC, the MPC and the ESKF against a simulated vehicle:

  • 3.4 m/s wind that none of the nodes knows;
  • +10 % mass;
  • airframe drag and rotor H-force;
  • IMU biases and GNSS noise.
python3 ../ROS2_Control_System/tests/sil/uav_stack_sil.py \
  --estimator  install/ros2_control_system/lib/ros2_control_system/uav_state_estimator \
  --controller install/ros2_control_system/lib/ros2_control_system/uav_trajectory_controller \
  --flight     install/ros2_flight_controller/lib/ros2_flight_controller/flight_controller_node \
  --control-params install/ros2_control_system/share/ros2_control_system/config/uav_control.yaml \
  --mission-planner install/ros2_mission_planner/lib/ros2_mission_planner/mission_planner_node \
  --mission-params  install/ros2_mission_planner/share/ros2_mission_planner/config/mission_planner_params.yaml \
  --mission-file    install/ros2_mission_planner/share/ros2_mission_planner/config/waypoint_mission.yaml \
  [--update-file    install/ros2_mission_planner/share/ros2_mission_planner/config/missions/retask_example.yaml]
Scenario Waypoint miss Control RMS Touchdown Wind estimate (truth 3.0, −1.5) Power ratio (truth ≈ 1.15) Other waypoint_mission.yaml 0.09 m 4.1 cm 4.5 cm (2.97, −1.50) ± 0.43 1.13 71 s, 9/9 checks keep_out_example.yaml 0.07 m 3.3 cm 8.9 cm (2.98, −1.49) ± 0.43 1.14 2 detour points; ≥ 6.2 m from both zone centres (r = 3 m); return flown as waypoints; 11/11 checks waypoint_mission + retask_example in flight 0.16 m 3.6 cm 4.0 cm (3.00, −1.49) ± 0.43 1.14 HOVER mid-leg, switched plan, 10/10 checks

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• The wind estimate assumes steady flight and the drag model of the vehicle description (C_D A, c_H are assumptions until measured). During aggressive manoeuvres d̂ also carries the inner-loop lag. The measurement σ is inflated to 1 m/s for that, and the energy estimate uses the 95 % disc, not the point estimate.
  • η_p = 0.5 for the climb and parasitic power is an assumption. The measured-power ratio corrects the model upwards only, so an optimistic η_p is caught in flight but a pessimistic one is not relaxed.
  • Keep-out zones are known static cylinders from the mission file. Moving or unknown obstacles are handled below the planner by the MPPI mode of ros2_control_system. An FC-decided failsafe RTH flies straight; a warning is raised when a zone reaches above the RTH altitude.
  • An in-flight change stops the vehicle (HOVER) before switching; it does not blend into the new route.
  • HIL and bench evidence are still to be produced. They need the vehicle, a battery with a current sensor and a thrust stand; nothing more can be proven in software.

docs.title: ROS2_Monitoring — terminal node manager and monitor for ROS 2
docs.text:
Source

This page is rendered from Source/ROS2_Monitoring/README.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in Source/ROS2_Monitoring/.

ros2_monitoring 0.3.0 is an animated curses dashboard (ros2_monitoring executable, ros2_monitoring/main.py). It creates one node, ros2_monitoring_py, that reads the ROS graph and, on the NODES page, calls other nodes' lifecycle and parameter services when you ask it to. It publishes and subscribes to nothing and closes no control loop.

Screenshot from a simulated graph (the test harness), 132 × 38 terminal, dark theme. Grouped by namespace; a NEW node, a LOST node, lifecycle states; Overview tab of the selected node.

Page Source SYS Framed panels: CPU cores, GPU, memory & disk, system, sensors, processes (core/system_interface.py) NODES Node manager (gui/pages/nodes.py, model in core/node_manager.py) TOPICS, GRAPH ROS 2 graph through rclpy (controller/ros2_controller.py) DOCKER Docker engine (core/docker_interface.py), optional K8S kubectl (core/kubectl_interface.py), optional, refreshed every 5 s GPU (in SYS) Jetson / NVIDIA GPU (core/gpu_interface.py), optional 
ros2 run ros2_monitoring ros2_monitoring --start-page nodes
ros2 run ros2_monitoring ros2_monitoring --theme light --color-filter --no-anim
ros2 launch ros2_monitoring ros2_monitoring.launch.py page:=nodes terminal:='xterm -e'

Options: --interval/-i, --start-page/-p (system nodes topics graph docker kubernetes), --loop/-l, --loop-time/-t, --debug/-d, --no-gpu, --no-docker, --no-kubernetes, --theme dark|light, --color-filter (Okabe–Ito colour-blind palette), --no-anim, --no-splash. --ros-args … appended by ros2 run is ignored. The launch file opens the dashboard through a terminal prefix (terminal:=, default xterm -e) because curses needs an interactive terminal, which ros2 launch does not give a node.

Logs: $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/ros2_monitoring.log while the screen is open (stdout/stderr included), $ROS_LOG_DIR or ~/.ros/log/ros2_monitoring/ otherwise.

docs.title: Look
docs.text:
• Header: gradient bar, shimmering title, breadcrumb (› NODES), status chips (ROS 2 LED, clock, node and topic counts, total CPU with a 3 s trend). Chips drop from the right on narrow terminals.
  • Tab bar: page icons; a pill slides to the active page.
  • Status bar: toasts, otherwise the latest node events (joined / lost / transitions); key caps for the page's shortcuts.
  • Tables use a header band and zebra rows. 256-colour terminals get the full palette; 8-colour terminals a basic one; F2 switches dark/light (the light theme expects a light terminal background), --color-filter the Okabe–Ito palette.
  • curses can address only 255 colour pairs per attribute; pairs are allocated on demand and the least recently used one is recycled (NColors.pair). A full frame uses about 80.

docs.title: NODES — node manager
docs.text:
Column Meaning LED ● alive (breathing), ◐ inactive, ○ unconfigured, ⊘ finalized, ✗ lost, spinner while a transition runs STATE NEW (6 s after joining), LOST <age> (kept 8 s), lifecycle state, or running PUB / SUB / SRV endpoint counts from get_*_names_and_types_by_node PID matched process; * = matched by executable name, — = no match CPU% / CPU TREND low-pass filtered CPU (100 % = one core) and its history MEM / UP resident memory, time since the node (re)joined

Rows are grouped by namespace (g toggles); each group header shows its node count and summed CPU. The KPI chips above the table (alive, lost, new, lifecycle) flash when a count changes.

Detail panel tabs: Overview (tiles with three-row seven-segment figures for CPU, memory, uptime and PID; a 60 s CPU area chart whose columns are linearly interpolated between samples; the command line), Publishers / Subscribers (with the peer nodes of each topic), Services (servers and clients), Parameters (list_parameters + get_parameters), Lifecycle (state machine, available transitions).

Key Action ↑ ↓ j k · PgUp PgDn · Home End select a node / · c filter by name (Esc cancels) · clear the filter s · r cycle the sort key (name, cpu, mem, state, pubs, subs, uptime, namespace) · reverse Enter d · [ ] · J K show/hide details · switch tab · scroll the tab p load parameters l lifecycle transition — offers exactly the transitions the node reports x stop the node's process: dialog with PID, match rule, command line and every node in that process; Cancel is the default, then SIGINT (clean rclpy/rclcpp shutdown) or SIGTERM h · g hide/show lost nodes · group by namespace on/off mouse click a row to select, a header to sort, a tab to switch

Global keys: ←/→ Tab pages, 1–9 jump, F1/? help, F2 theme, F3 animations, F5 refresh, F12 last log line, Ctrl-L redraw, q quit.

docs.title: Node → process matching and stop safety
docs.text:
ROS 2 does not publish a node's PID. core/node_manager.match_processes applies, in order:

  1. exact — the command line carries __node:=<name> or <old>:__node:=<name> (plus __ns:=<ns> when given), which is how ros2 run/ros2 launch rename nodes;
  2. name — otherwise, the single process whose executable (or Python script) name equals the node name. Two candidates ⇒ no match.

Nodes hosted in a component container without such remaps get no PID and cannot be stopped from here. stop_node re-reads the process before signalling and refuses if the PID now belongs to a different process (start time changed), if it is the monitor itself, or if permission is denied.

docs.title: Measurement and animation maths
docs.text:
Nothing here is a control loop, but the displayed numbers and the motion are derived, not tuned:

Stage Model Sensor psutil cpu_percent() = 100·Δ(cpu time)/Δ(wall) over one controller period T (0.5 s): a box-car mean. Kernel tick 4 ms (250 Hz) ⇒ quantisation 0.4 %/T[s] = 0.8 % at T = 0.5 s Filter H(s) = 1/(τs+1), τ = 2 s, exact ZOH for irregular steps: y += α(x − y), α = 1 − e^(−Δt/τ); step response 63.2 % at t = τ; corner 0.08 Hz ≪ 1 Hz Nyquist (Franklin, Powell, Workman, Digital Control of Dynamic Systems, §4.3) Motion critically damped tracker ẍ + 2ωẋ + ω²(x − r) = 0, applied in closed form each frame: e(t) = (e₀ + (v₀ + ωe₀)t)e^(−ωt). Eigenvalues e^(−ωΔt) < 1 for every Δt ⇒ unconditionally stable and frame-rate independent; from rest no overshoot; 2 % settling t_s = 5.834/ω (Ogata, Modern Control Engineering, §5-3) Fades / pulses e^(−age/τ) tints for NEW/LOST rows, raised cosine (1 − cos 2πt/T)/2 for LEDs, cubic ease-out 1 − (1 − u)³ for pop-ins and wipes

test/test_anim.py and test/test_node_manager.py check each of these statements (closed form, h + h = 2h stepping, settling time, no overshoot, 63.2 % at τ, irregular-step exactness).

docs.text:
flowchart TD
    S(["main()"]) --> A["parse CLI (ROS args stripped), file logging"]
    A --> B{"controller, GUI and<br/>at least one page importable?"}
    B -- no --> X(["exit 1"])

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
cd Source/ROS2_Monitoring && python3 -m pytest test -q

test_tui_smoke.py runs the real window in a pseudo-terminal with a stub controller, drives the keys and checks that it drew, logged no error and quit cleanly. No ROS 2 installation is needed.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• CPU/MEM are per process: nodes sharing a process show the same values (the Overview tab says how many share it).
  • Lifecycle and parameter actions need lifecycle_msgs and rcl_interfaces at runtime; without them the panel says the clients are unavailable.
  • The TOPICS page still shows frequency/bandwidth as 0 — the controller does not subscribe to topics (core/ros2_interface.TopicMonitor exists but is not wired in).

docs.title: ROS2_Network_Bridge — MAVLink ground-station link
docs.text:
Source

This page is rendered from Source/ROS2_Network_Bridge/README.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in Source/ROS2_Network_Bridge/.

ros2_network_bridge 0.4.0 connects the UAV stack to a ground control station (QGroundControl or any MAVLink v2 GCS) over UDP, TCP, a serial telemetry radio, or a TLS relay for consoles on another network. It does three things:

  • Downlink: sends telemetry from the stack to the GCS, within a bandwidth budget.
  • Uplink: turns GCS commands into discrete commands for ros2_flight_controller and ros2_mission_planner. A command is acknowledged only once the flight controller's measured mode confirms it.
  • Datalink loss: runs the failsafe when the GCS link is lost.
  • Observers: the JetbotNanoOWL Android console reads the same downlink. It fuses ODOMETRY (pose and twist with their covariances) in its EKF and only sends a MAV_TYPE_LOG heartbeat, so it is never taken for the GCS (Jetbot console).

Like the other nodes, it has a ROS-free core (network_bridge_core: codec, conversions, link supervision, transports) behind a thin ROS 2 node. The core is tested with gtest and with the full-stack SIL.

 odometry/filtered ─┐                          ┌─▶ HEARTBEAT 1 Hz, SYS_STATUS 1 Hz,
 gps/fix ───────────┤   telemetry.h            │   ATTITUDE 10 Hz, LOCAL_POSITION_NED 10 Hz,
 battery/state ─────┼─▶ ENU/FLU → NED/FRD, ────┤   GLOBAL_POSITION_INT 5 Hz, ODOMETRY 5 Hz, STATUSTEXT
 flight/status ─────┤   budget, heartbeat map  │        (MAVLink v2, UDP / TCP / serial)
 mission/status ────┘                          │                    ▲ │
                                               │                    │ ▼
 flight/nav_command ◀── gcs_link.h ◀── COMMAND_LONG ◀── parser (CRC, resync) ◀── GCS
 mission/start|abort ◀─┘   │  └──▶ COMMAND_ACK (IN_PROGRESS → ACCEPTED / FAILED / DENIED)
                           └── GCS heartbeat watchdog → link-loss failsafe

docs.title: io_step — one 10 ms cycle
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    T(["io_timer 10 ms"]) --> R["transport.read (non-blocking)"]
    R --> P{"bytes?"}
    P -- yes --> P1["parser: STX, CRC, byte-wise resync → frames"]
    P1 --> F["GcsLink.on_frame: HEARTBEAT → watchdog,<br/>COMMAND_LONG → pending command"]
    P -- no --> S
    F --> S["GcsLink.step: link up / lost,<br/>pending command confirmed by measured FC mode?"]
    S --> S1{"link lost, flying, not RTH/LAND/manual,<br/>planner not in control?"}
    S1 -- yes --> S2["failsafe: RTH (or LAND / HOVER),<br/>re-sent every 2 s until the mode confirms"]
    S1 -- no --> N
    S2 --> N["apply: publish flight/nav_command for each output command"]
    N --> C["call mission/start or mission/abort<br/>(result → ACK ACCEPTED / DENIED)"]
    C --> A["send COMMAND_ACK: IN_PROGRESS, then ACCEPTED,<br/>or FAILED after ack_timeout_s"]
    A --> O["send telemetry streams within the budget:<br/>HEARTBEAT, SYS_STATUS, ATTITUDE,<br/>LOCAL_POSITION_NED, GLOBAL_POSITION_INT"]
    O --> TX["flush STATUSTEXT queue (rate-limited)"]

    CB(["odometry, gps, battery, status callbacks"]) --> CB1["ENU/FLU → NED/FRD, cache inputs"]
    D(["timer 1 s"]) --> D1["publish network/gcs_connected, network/diagnostics"]

docs.title: Design (control-systems.md §5)
docs.text:
LINK DESIGN
  Sensor      : GCS frames over the transport; MAVLink v2 CRC-16/MCRF4XX + CRC_EXTRA (false
                accept 2⁻¹⁶ per candidate start byte), id/length checked from the header
  Filter      : parser resynchronises byte-wise; uplink loss from sequence gaps
                g = (seq − seq_prev − 1) mod 256, exponential forgetting λ = 0.99:
                p̂ = L/(L + R), L ← λL + g, R ← λR + 1
  Estimator   : link state from GCS heartbeats (MAV_TYPE_GCS): connected / lost after T = 5 s;
                false-loss rate λ_ft = 3600 f_hb (1 − p) p^⌈T f_hb⌉ per hour
                (T = 5 s, 1 Hz: p = 0.1 → 0.032 /h, p = 0.3 → 6.1 /h; Monte-Carlo checked)
  Supervisor  : discrete commands only (no set-points over a lossy link); ACK closed on the
                flight controller's measured mode within 3 s; DISARM refused while flying;
                termination disabled unless allowed; RTL during a mission → mission/abort
                (the planner's return respects keep-out zones)
  Actuation   : flight/nav_command, mission/start, mission/abort
  Failsafe    : link lost + flying + not returning / landing / manual + mission planner not in
                control → RTH (or LAND / HOVER), re-sent every 2 s until the mode confirms it
                (3 retries); a validated mission continues by default
  Odometry    : ODOMETRY #331, LOCAL_NED / BODY_FRD; Σ_mav = J Σ_ros Jᵀ with
                J_pose = blockdiag(T, E⁻¹T) (ROS fixed-axis rotation error → ZYX Euler error,
                E = [Rz Ry e_x, Rz e_y, e_z], det E = cos θ), J_twist = blockdiag(B, B);
                unknown (all-zero / non-finite) or gimbal-locked covariance → NaN, never 0
  Budget      : B = Σ f_i (12 + len_i) = 2301 B/s at the default rates; C = baud/10 (serial 8N1)
                or bps/8; if B > u_max C, periodic rates × s = (u_max C − B_hb)/(B − B_hb)
  Frames      : p_ned = T p_enu, R_ned←frd = T R_enu←flu B, T = [[0,1,0],[1,0,0],[0,0,−1]],
                B = diag(1, −1, −1); ZYX Euler of R_ned←frd
  Scan        : LaserScan → OBSTACLE_DISTANCE #330, BODY_FRD, 360 one-degree sectors in 5
                messages (offsets −180, −108, −36, 36, 108°); ray → body by the mount (ψ_m, t_m),
                de-skewed to the stamp with the body twist held over the revolution,
                p_ref = Rz(ω dt) p_b + v dt (neglected chord |v||ω|dt²/2 = 5 mm at 1 m/s,
                1 rad/s, 0.1 s); sector = nearest echo within ±0.5°, max+1 = free, UINT16_MAX =
                no data; one scan in n = ⌈B_scan / (u_max C − B_streams)⌉ (Wi-Fi 1, 57.6 kBd 16)
  Relay       : TLS 1.2+, CA + host name or SPKI pin; backoff min(T_min·2^(k−1), T_max)
  Verification: 42 gtest cases, 7 of them relay transport against an in-process TLS server
                (pymavlink golden frames byte for byte incl. ODOMETRY and OBSTACLE_DISTANCE,
                scan sectors / mount / de-skew / decimation,
                J_pose against central differences at 200 random attitudes,
                relay: pin, wrong pin sends no token, untrusted cert, refusal back-off, 200 kB noise without a
                false frame, rotation reconstruction on 1000 random attitudes, link-loss
                policies, UDP loopback); SIL with a pymavlink GCS: 14/14 checks
  Reference   : MAVLink serialisation / CRC / command protocol (mavlink.io); REP-103, REP-105;
                PX4 datalink-loss failsafe (NAV_DLL_ACT) for the policy structure

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
MAV_CMD Action Acknowledged ACCEPTED when 400 COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM (p1 = 1 / 0) ARM / DISARM (DISARM refused while flying) mode ARMED_IDLE / DISARMED 22 NAV_TAKEOFF TAKEOFF mode TAKEOFF or HOVER 21 NAV_LAND LAND mode LANDING, LANDED or DISARMED 20 NAV_RETURN_TO_LAUNCH mission/abort while the planner flies, else RTH service success / mode RETURN_TO_HOME or LANDING 17 NAV_LOITER_UNLIM HOVER mode HOVER 300 MISSION_START mission/start service success (reason as STATUSTEXT when denied) 185 DO_FLIGHTTERMINATION EMERGENCY_STOP only with commands.allow_termination mode EMERGENCY_STOP others — UNSUPPORTED

Every accepted command is first answered with IN_PROGRESS. The final result follows: ACCEPTED, or FAILED after ack_timeout_s. A GCS retry of the pending command gets IN_PROGRESS again and is not re-sent to the flight controller.

docs.title: Telemetry
docs.text:
Message Source Notes HEARTBEAT flight/status MAV_TYPE_HEXAROTOR; custom_mode = index in the FC mode table below; SAFETY_ARMED, AUTO (autonomous modes), MANUAL_INPUT (joystick); state STANDBY / ACTIVE / CRITICAL (link-loss failsafe) / EMERGENCY SYS_STATUS battery/state, link voltage, current (positive discharging), remaining; drop_rate_comm = uplink loss ATTITUDE odometry/filtered NED/FRD Euler angles and body rates LOCAL_POSITION_NED odometry/filtered odometry origin; twist rotated from the child frame (REP-105) GLOBAL_POSITION_INT gps/fix + odometry relative_alt above the arming altitude, heading from the attitude ODOMETRY odometry/filtered pose in LOCAL_NED, twist in BODY_FRD, both 6×6 covariances mapped as in the design block; rates.odometry_hz (0 = off) OBSTACLE_DISTANCE scan (LaserScan) obstacle.enabled; 5 messages per scan, BODY_FRD, 1° sectors, mount and de-skew as in the design block; decimated to fit the link budget STATUSTEXT mission/status events, bridge rate-limited (5/s), split into 50-character chunks

The custom_mode table is: 0 DISARMED, 1 PRE_ARM_CHECK, 2 ARMED_IDLE, 3 TAKEOFF, 4 HOVER, 5 WAYPOINT_FOLLOW, 6 ORBIT, 7 PATH_MANAGE, 8 OBSTACLE_AVOID, 9 RETURN_TO_HOME, 10 LANDING, 11 LANDED, 12 MANUAL_JOYSTICK, 13 EMERGENCY_STOP.

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
Kind Name Type sub odometry/filtered nav_msgs/Odometry sub gps/fix sensor_msgs/NavSatFix sub battery/state sensor_msgs/BatteryState sub flight/status std_msgs/String sub mission/status ros2_mission_planner/msg/MissionStatus sub scan sensor_msgs/LaserScan (only with obstacle.enabled) pub flight/nav_command std_msgs/String pub network/gcs_connected std_msgs/Bool pub network/diagnostics diagnostic_msgs/DiagnosticArray (loss, false-trip rate, rx/tx B/s, CRC errors, failsafe) client mission/start, mission/abort std_srvs/Trigger

Parameters: config/network_bridge_params.yaml. It covers the transport, the rates, the command settings and the link_loss.* policy; each value is tagged with its source.

docs.title: Launch
docs.text:
# Bridge only (stack already running); QGroundControl on this machine
ros2 launch ros2_network_bridge network_bridge.launch.py

# Whole stack + GCS link, GCS on another host
ros2 launch ros2_network_bridge uav_with_gcs.launch.py gcs_host:=192.168.2.10

# Telemetry radio
ros2 launch ros2_network_bridge network_bridge.launch.py transport:=serial

# Jetbot graph → JetbotNanoOWL console on the phone
ros2 launch ros2_network_bridge jetbot_console.launch.py phone_host:=192.168.1.50

docs.title: Jetbot console
docs.text:
jetbot_console.launch.py points the bridge at the phone, reads the Jetbot's /odometry, raises ODOMETRY to 10 Hz and sets link_loss.action: none (a ground robot has no flight mode to fall back to). The console's EKF uses ODOMETRY as its feedback stream, so the rate sets its watchdog margin: with T_wd = 0.6 s the false-trip rate is 3600 f (1 − p) p^⌈T_wd f⌉ per hour — 0.03 /h at 10 Hz and 10 % loss, 16 /h at the 5 Hz yaml default. 10 Hz costs 2450 B/s, 2 % of a 1 Mbit/s IP budget. The console sends one HEARTBEAT per second as system 254, MAV_COMP_ID_LOG, MAV_TYPE_LOG: it brings learn_remote to the phone's address, but GcsLink only counts MAV_TYPE_GCS, so the console never connects or trips the failsafe.

The launch also enables obstacle.*: each LD19 scan (scan_topic:=/scan, mount yaw scan_mount_yaw_deg) goes out as OBSTACLE_DISTANCE, and the console places every fan with the 6-DoF pose at the fan's own timestamp. Slices taken at different heights and attitudes therefore stack into a 3-D voxel map (the console's docs/UAV_3D.md). At 10 Hz this costs 8950 B/s. That is every scan on Wi-Fi; on a 57.6 kBd radio the bridge sends one scan in 16.

On a UAV with ros2_flight_controller, use odom_topic:=/odometry/filtered. Set link_loss_action:=rth if a real GCS (QGroundControl) flies it beside the console. The console is never counted as a GCS, so the setting only acts on that GCS.

The UDP transport answers one remote. With learn_remote, the console and a QGroundControl on another host would take the downlink in turns; run a MAVLink router (e.g. mavlink-routerd) to serve both.

docs.title: Console on another network (transport: relay)
docs.text:
When the phone and the Jetson do not share a network, both are behind NAT, the phone usually behind its carrier's (CGNAT), and neither can reach the other. With transport: relay the bridge dials out over TLS to Server_Relay, and the console does the same; outbound TCP crosses every NAT, so no port is opened on the robot.

ros2 launch ros2_network_bridge jetbot_console.launch.py transport:=relay \
    relay_host:=relay.example.org relay_robot:=jetbot-01 \
    relay_token_file:=/etc/jetbot/relay.token [relay_pin:=<sha256 of the relay key>]
  • Trust. By default the bridge trusts the system CA store (or relay.ca_file) and checks the relay's host name. With relay.pin_sha256, the relay's public key (SHA-256 of the DER SPKI) is the anchor instead, so a self-signed relay works and a different key is refused before the token is sent.
  • Token. The token is read from relay.token_file, never from a parameter value, so it does not show in ros2 param or in process lists.
  • I/O. A dedicated thread connects, reads and writes. read() and write() only touch its queues, so the 10 ms I/O step never blocks on the network.
  • Reconnection. Back-off is min(T_min·2^(k−1), T_max) after k failures (1 s to 30 s). SIGPIPE is blocked on that thread only.
  • Safety. The relay forwards nothing from an observer to the vehicle except a verified HEARTBEAT. An observer can never send a command through it; GcsLink's safety rules still apply behind that.

docs.title: Build and test
docs.text:
colcon build --packages-up-to ros2_network_bridge
colcon test --packages-select ros2_network_bridge && colcon test-result --verbose

The full-stack SIL (../ROS2_Control_System/tests/sil/uav_stack_sil.py … --mission-planner … --network-bridge <network_bridge_node>) runs a pymavlink GCS against the real nodes and checks the following:

  • MISSION_START over MAVLink is acknowledged ACCEPTED.
  • LOCAL_POSITION_NED is within 0.18 m RMS of the truth, converted to NED.
  • The heartbeat custom_mode follows the flight modes.
  • 15 mission events arrive as STATUSTEXT.
  • After an 8 s GCS silence mid-mission, the bridge reports "mission planner in control — mission continues". The mission completes with only the planner's own RTH.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• OBSTACLE_DISTANCE is planar and carries no mount height, so the console places a fan at the body origin's height. The mount yaw and the horizontal offset are applied on the bridge.

  • MAVLink message signing is not implemented, so signed frames are rejected. Use a trusted network, udp.allowed_hosts and mavlink.gcs_system_id.

  • Only the command subset above is supported. There is no MAVLink mission protocol (MISSION_ITEM_INT) and no parameter protocol. Missions are uploaded through ros2_mission_planner (mission/upload, mission/upload_waypoints).
  • The loss estimator assumes fewer than 256 consecutive lost frames per GCS stream (sequence wrap). Longer outages already trip the link-loss detection.
  • The flight-controller custom_mode table must follow ros2_flight_controller::FlightMode.
  • ros2_flight_controller/include/.../mavlink_bridge.h is an older, unimplemented sketch. This package supersedes it, as it superseded ros2_communication_bridge, which was removed. The parameter migration table is in the CHANGELOG.
  • HIL with a real radio link is still to be done.

docs.title: ros2_night_vision_owl
docs.text:
Source

This page is rendered from Source/ROS2_Night_Vision_OWL/README.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in Source/ROS2_Night_Vision_OWL/.

Radiometric thermal detection and tracking for ROS 2 Humble. A Meridian MI48 camera (or a synthetic scene for software-in-the-loop) feeds a filter, a constant-false-alarm-rate (CFAR) hot-target detector and a multi-target Kalman tracker. Every stage has a closed-form model: thresholds come from a chosen false-alarm probability, measurement covariances from error propagation, gates from chi-square quantiles. None of them is tuned by eye.

docs.title: Signal chain
docs.text:
MI48 / synthetic                 thermal_detector_node                          thermal_tracker_node
┌──────────────┐  32FC1 °C  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐ Detection2DArray ┌─────────────────────────┐ Detection2DArray
│ sensor       │──────────▶│ bad-pixel fix ─▶ temporal LPF ─▶ CA-CFAR     │──────────────▶│ CV Kalman (DWNA)        │──────────────▶ tracks
│ y = T + n    │           │       │            (detect)       │          │  u, v, R (2x2)  │ + likelihood-ratio GNN │  u, v, P (2x2)
└──────────────┘           │       └────── raw frame ──▶ centroid + R     │               │ + M-of-N, NIS monitor  │
                           │  NETD estimator ─▶ noise floor ─┘            │               └──────────▲──────────────┘
                           └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘                          │
                                                                          predicted state gates the next scan (feedback)

This package ends at the estimator. It commands no actuator. A controller that follows a target (gimbal, heading) subscribes to tracks and closes its own loop on the estimated position and covariance. If detections stop, the tracker publishes an empty track list, so a consumer never acts on a stale track.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
colcon build --packages-select ros2_night_vision_owl
source install/setup.bash

# Software-in-the-loop: synthetic scene -> detector -> tracker
ros2 launch ros2_night_vision_owl night_vision_owl_pipeline.launch.py

# Hardware: MI48 over USB (port auto-detected), false-colour overlay on
ros2 launch ros2_night_vision_owl night_vision_owl_pipeline.launch.py source:=mi48 debug_image:=true

# Another node publishes <namespace>/image_temperature
ros2 launch ros2_night_vision_owl night_vision_owl_pipeline.launch.py source:=none

# Camera only (used by Docker/Kubernetes)
ros2 launch ros2_night_vision_owl camera.launch.py source:=mi48

# Algorithm tests (numpy/scipy only, no ROS needed)
python3 -m pytest test/unit -q

docs.title: Nodes
docs.text:
All topic names are relative. The launch file puts the nodes in the thermal namespace.

Executable Subscribes Publishes thermal_camera_node – image_temperature (32FC1 °C), camera_info, /diagnostics thermal_detector_node image_temperature detections (Detection2DArray), image_filtered, image_debug, /diagnostics thermal_tracker_node detections tracks (Detection2DArray), /diagnostics

* optional. Detections and tracks use pixel coordinates (u right, v down, pixel centres on integers). Each Detection2D carries:

Field Detection Track results[0].pose.pose.position centroid (u, v) filtered position (u, v) results[0].pose.covariance[0, 1, 6, 7] 2×2 centroid covariance R [px²] 2×2 position covariance P [px²] bbox the blob's box: centre u_min + (w − 1)/2, size w × h box of the track size, centred on the position id empty track id

The position is read from the field that carries its covariance: results[0].pose when that 2×2 block is positive definite, otherwise the bbox centre. The tracker accepts detections from other producers such as NanoOWL; when a producer leaves the covariance empty, the tracker uses the bbox centre with default_measurement_std_px. The ros2_qt dashboard reads the same fields (Vision tab → Thermal).

Parameters and their derivations are listed in config/thermal_pipeline.yaml. The detector's false-alarm probability, area limits and temperature gates can be changed at run time (ros2 param set). Every parameter is range-checked.

docs.title: 1. Sensor model
docs.text:
y[k](u, v) = T(u, v, t_k) + n[k](u, v), in °C, with n white in time and space and std σ_n, the sensor's NETD. The noise is measured, not assumed. For a static pixel, d = y[k] − y[k−1] ~ N(0, 2σ_n²), so

σ̂_n = 1.4826 · MAD(d) / √2

The MAD is taken over all pixels and smoothed over noise_averaging_frames. The MAD has a 50 % breakdown point. Moving targets and ego-motion bias the estimate upward, which lowers the false-alarm rate. The SIL check measured σ̂_n = 0.1009 K for a true 0.100 K.

docs.title: 2. Filtering
docs.text:
Temporal low-pass, exact ZOH discretisation. H(s) = ω_c/(s + ω_c) with a piecewise-constant input over one frame integrates exactly to

y[k] = y[k−1] + α_k (x[k] − y[k−1]),    α_k = 1 − exp(−ω_c Δt_k)

Δt_k comes from message stamps, so jitter is handled exactly. The project rule's α = ω_cT/(1+ω_cT) is the backward-Euler form of the same filter; the two agree to first order.

  • Noise. y[k] = Σ_i α(1−α)^i x[k−i], so for white input Var y / Var x = α² Σ(1−α)^{2i} = α/(2−α). With time-varying α_k the variance ratio follows r[k] = (1−α_k)² r[k−1] + α_k², with r = 1 at reset. The code tracks this exactly, transient included.
  • Target retention. A pixel covered for τ = d/v seconds reaches 1 − e^{−ω_c τ} of the contrast. Keeping 90 % requires v ≤ ω_c d / ln 10. At f_c = 4 Hz and d = 3 px that is 32.7 px/s.
  • Delay. The output's mean age obeys L[k] = (1−α_k)(Δt_k + L[k−1]), with steady state T(1−α)/α (23 ms at 25 Hz, f_c = 4 Hz). It is reported in the diagnostics. The tracker never sees it (see §3).

Bad pixels. NaNs and the static bad_pixels list are replaced by the median of their valid 3×3 neighbours. A per-frame Hampel filter is deliberately not used: a w×w window deletes every target smaller than ⌈w²/2⌉ px, which on an 80×62 array means every distant target.

Spatial matched filter (spatial_sigma_px, off by default). A Gaussian kernel g scales white-noise variance by exactly (Σg_i²)². It correlates neighbouring cells, which makes the CFAR threshold approximate. That is why it is off by default.

docs.title: 3. Detection: CA-CFAR
docs.text:
For each pixel under test (CUT), the background mean and std are estimated from N = (2R+1)² − (2G+1)² training cells around a guard band. The guard band keeps the target out of its own statistics. If the training cells and the CUT are i.i.d. Gaussian under H0, (y − μ̂)/(ŝ√(1+1/N)) follows a Student-t distribution with N−1 degrees of freedom, so

detect  ⇔  y − μ̂ > k · max(ŝ, σ_floor),    k = t⁻¹_{N−1}(1 − P_fa) · √(1 + 1/N)

gives a per-pixel false-alarm probability of exactly P_fa, whatever the background level. σ_floor = σ̂_n·√r is the filtered sensor noise, and it can only lower the rate. With the defaults (R = 5, G = 2, N = 96, P_fa = 1e-4), k = 3.89, compared with 3.72 when the statistics are known (4.6 % CFAR loss). The test measures the empirical per-pixel rate on Gaussian frames and checks it against a binomial 4σ band.

Detect on the filtered frame, measure on the raw frame. The temporal filter raises the SNR for the detection decision. Its output noise, however, is AR(1) in time with correlation 1−α. Centroids taken from it would feed coloured noise to the Kalman filter and make it over-confident; in SIL this showed up as gate misses and duplicate tracks. The blob found on the filtered frame therefore only picks the window. The centroid is measured on the raw frame, whose noise is white in time, and the Kalman filter does the temporal smoothing optimally itself.

Centroid and its covariance. The window W is the blob's bounding box grown by G. It is fixed once chosen, so the estimate is a smooth function of the data and the delta method applies. The weights are w_i = y_i − b_i, where b is a least-squares plane fitted to the undetected pixels around W; the plane is exact for any linear background. Then:

u_c = Σ u_i w_i / Σ w_i
Var(u_c)      = s² Σ (u_i − u_c)²          / (Σ w_i)²
Cov(u_c, v_c) = s² Σ (u_i − u_c)(v_i − v_c) / (Σ w_i)²
s² = RSS_plane / (n − 3)            (unbiased residual variance, floored by σ̂_n²)

Point-sampling a Gaussian PSF of std p adds a bias that depends on the sub-pixel phase ("pixel locking"). Poisson summation gives its first harmonic, −4πp² e^{−2π²p²} sin 2πx, which adds b²/2 per axis, capped at 1/12 px². Numerically this matches within 2 % for p ≥ 0.4 px.

Two validity guards apply. Blobs whose window touches the image border are dropped, because truncation biases the centroid by up to about 0.8 of the target radius. When Σw < 3 s √|W|, the ratio is ill-conditioned; the thresholded blob centroid is then used with the distribution-free bound Var = width²/12.

Measured detection NEES, e^T R^{-1} e against ground truth, with one target and noise from 0.1 to 0.3 K: 1.9–2.1 (χ²₂ mean = 2).

docs.title: 4. Estimation: constant-velocity Kalman filter
docs.text:
State x = [u, v, u̇, v̇]. Discrete white-noise acceleration (Bar-Shalom et al. §6.3.2):

F = [[I, T·I], [0, I]],   G = [T²/2 · I; T · I],   Q = σ_a² G Gᵀ,   H = [I 0]

The rule 0.5 a_max ≤ σ_a ≤ a_max sets σ_a. In the image plane, a_max includes ego-motion f·ω̇: an 80 px, 45° lens (f = 96.6 px) with 0.2 rad/s² platform yaw acceleration gives 19 px/s², hence the default of 20.

  • Observability. O = [H; HF] = [[I, 0], [I, T·I]] has rank 4 for any T > 0. The unit test checks rank 4 at T = 1e-3, 0.04 and 1 s.
  • Update. The Joseph form P = (I−KH)P(I−KH)ᵀ + KRKᵀ keeps P symmetric positive definite for any gain. The test runs 500 updates with R spanning 1e-8 to 1e2.
  • Consistency. In a Monte Carlo run of the true model, mean NEES and NIS fall inside the 99 % χ² bands (4 and 2 dof).

docs.title: 5. Association: likelihood-ratio GNN
docs.text:
For track i and detection j, compare "j is i" with "i was missed and j is clutter or a new target" (density β per px²):

c_ij = d²_ij + ln|2π S_ij| − κ,     κ = 2 ln( P_D / (β (1 − P_D P_G)) ),    d² = νᵀS⁻¹ν

An unassigned track or detection costs 0, so a pair is used only if c_ij < 0. The ln|2πS| term matters. With Mahalanobis distance alone, a vague detection (huge S) looks close to every track; in SIL it stole assignments. The gate d² ≤ χ²₂⁻¹(P_G) only speeds up the search, and the likelihood ratio makes the decision. The global optimum is found exactly as a square assignment problem on the augmented (n+m)×(m+n) matrix (Kuhn 1955; Crouse 2016, the scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment algorithm). The unit test checks the result against brute-force enumeration on 300 random problems.

docs.title: 6. Track management
docs.text:
• Confirmation. M of N hits (default 3 of 5). A tentative track is dropped once M can no longer be reached.
  • Deletion. A track is deleted after max_misses consecutive misses, or when its 1σ position error exceeds max_position_std_px, at which point the gate is meaningless.
  • No duplicates. An unassigned detection inside a confirmed track's gate does not start a new track. It is almost certainly a second return from that target.
  • Time. Δt comes from stamps. A scan older than the last one is rejected. A backward jump larger than max_backward_jump_s (bag loop, simulator reset) resets the tracker.

docs.title: 7. Run-time consistency monitor
docs.text: The mean NIS over the last K confirmed updates satisfies K·ε̄ ~ χ²(2K). /diagnostics reports ε̄ with its 95 % band [χ²⁻¹(0.025), χ²⁻¹(0.975)]/K (K = 100 gives [1.63, 2.41]). It raises WARN with the direction of the mismatch: over-confident means Q or R is too small, conservative means too large.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Evidence Where Result Filter step response = continuous system test_filters.py exact (1e-12) Variance ratio α/(2−α), jitter recursion test_filters.py Monte Carlo within 3–4 % NETD estimator, 0 % / 1 % hot-pixel contamination test_filters.py within 3 % / 5 % CFAR per-pixel P_fa test_cfar.py binomial 4σ band Centroid NEES (400 trials) test_cfar.py inside χ² 99 % band Pixel-locking formula vs numerical bias test_cfar.py within 2 % Planar background leaves centroid unbiased test_cfar.py mean error < 4 s.e.m. KF observability, DWNA Q, Joseph SPD test_kalman.py pass KF NEES / NIS Monte Carlo test_kalman.py inside χ² 99 % bands GNN = brute-force optimum test_association.py 300/300 M-of-N, deletion, out-of-order, clock jump test_tracker.py pass SIL: synthetic → detector → tracker, 30 s test_tracker.py see below

SIL over seeds 1–30 (2 targets, contrast 2 K, noise 0.3 K, dead pixel, 25 Hz):

  • coverage of targets away from the border: ≥ 98.7 %
  • frames with a false track: ≤ 3 out of 750
  • identity switches while targets are resolved: 0
  • position RMSE: 0.15–0.34 px
  • mean NIS: 1.89–2.46; track NEES against truth: 3.9–4.3 (χ²₄ mean 4)

Live ROS 2 Humble run. The package was built with colcon, colcon test passed (the suite plus the message-conversion tests), and the pipeline was started with ros2 launch (synthetic source, 80×62 at 25 Hz, x86 container with 4 cores):

Measurement Result Input and tracker scan rate 25.0 Hz Detector time per frame 3.0–3.5 ms (8.6–13.7 ms with debug_image:=true) Stamp-to-detection latency 3.6–4.2 ms On-line NETD estimate 0.2000–0.2010 K (true 0.200 K) Mean NIS (K = 100) 1.81–2.45 Parameter range check out-of-range ros2 param set rejected Tracker failsafe empty tracks published after the camera stopped

Not yet done: Jetson timing, hardware-in-the-loop with an MI48, and NIS/NEES on recorded thermal data. Those are the next steps of the verification order (SIL → HIL → bench).

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Unresolved targets. Two targets closer than about 2(G + target radius) px merge into one blob. Identity through such an encounter is not guaranteed, and the merged centroid corrupts the velocity estimate for about 1–2 s afterwards. JPDA or merged-measurement models would handle this; they are not implemented.
  • Gaussian background assumption. Heavy-tailed clutter (sky/foliage edges, sun glint) pushes the real P_fa above design. Detections before M-of-N confirmation are the protection.
  • Static fixed-pattern noise correlates centroid errors in time for slow targets, which pulls the NIS low (seen as 1.65–1.8 at 0.1 K noise). Flat-field (non-uniformity) correction on the camera removes it.
  • No ego-motion compensation. Camera rotation is absorbed by σ_a. With odometry, subtracting f·ω per frame would allow a smaller σ_a.
  • MI48 driver. The driver is the existing mi48_jetson_* module. Its CRC check has not been confirmed on hardware, so CRC failures are counted but not dropped by default (mi48.drop_crc_errors).

docs.title: Legacy components
docs.text: The C++ modules under src/night_vison_owl_*, the scripts/ utilities and the night_vision_owl_enhanced_pipeline / dual_thermal_owl_pipeline launch files are unchanged by this rework. They are built or installed only when their own dependencies are present, and they do not use the pipeline described above.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Y. Bar-Shalom, X.-R. Li, T. Kirubarajan, Estimation with Applications to Tracking and Navigation, Wiley 2001: DWNA model, NIS/NEES tests, gating.
  • S. S. Blackman, R. Popoli, Design and Analysis of Modern Tracking Systems, Artech House 1999: likelihood-ratio assignment, M-of-N.
  • M. A. Richards, Fundamentals of Radar Signal Processing, 2nd ed.: CA-CFAR.
  • H. M. Finn, R. S. Johnson, RCA Review 29, 1968: adaptive CFAR threshold.
  • G. F. Franklin, J. D. Powell, M. Workman, Digital Control of Dynamic Systems, ch. 6: ZOH equivalents.
  • D. Simon, Optimal State Estimation, Wiley 2006, §7.2: coloured measurement noise.
  • F. R. Hampel, J. Amer. Statist. Assoc. 69, 1974: MAD scale estimator.
  • H. W. Kuhn, Naval Res. Logist. Q. 2, 1955; D. F. Crouse, IEEE TAES 52(4), 2016: assignment.

docs.title: ROS 2 node graph — JetOwl_FlightControl · JetOwl_Vision · Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL
docs.text:
Source

This page is rendered from Docs/flowcharts/ros2_nodes_flowchart.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in Docs/flowcharts/.

A single diagram of every ROS 2 node in the three repositories, connected through topics, services and transport links (UDP, TCP, HTTP).

  • Two micro-ROS nodes on MCUs: jetowl_fc (STM32N657) and jetowl_vision (STM32N655). The control chain inside the firmware is drawn as well, so that every closed loop is visible.
  • 71 nodes in Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL: 61 in Source/, 3 in MATLAB/ and 7 in Examples/.
  • 9 external node blocks started by the repository's launch files, e.g. micro_ros_agent, ros_gz_bridge, the Isaac ROS DNN encoder/TensorRT.
How to view Notes The mermaid block below Rendered directly by GitHub. The flowcharts/ directory is in exclude_docs; on the MkDocs site the System Node Graph page renders this file through the hook Scripts/mkdocs_hooks/source_pages.py. The diagram has 304 edges, below Mermaid's default limit of 500 images/ros2_nodes_flowchart.svg Pre-rendered with Mermaid 12 (dagre), plain SVG labels, white background. Open this file to zoom in https://mermaid.live Paste the mermaid block to edit it and export a PNG

The data was checked against the source code on branch ccr-b2081e2f-1udgah, including the fixes of section 4. Base commits at the time of drawing:

Repository Commit JetOwl_FlightControl b1b56ef JetOwl_Vision 872fe84 Isaac_ROS-Jetbot_NanoOWL dabd1ad

Topic names are the names after the remappings of each package's main launch file, listed in section 3. Relative names (without a leading /) live in the root namespace unless the subgraph states a namespace.

  subgraph FCREPO["JetOwl_FlightControl — STM32N657 · 192.168.10.2"]
    direction TB

    FC_MIXR["Mixer · saturation priority<br/>arm latch"]:::fw
    FC_ROT["Rotor speed loop 1 kHz/rotor<br/>2-DOF: inverse-model FF + PI (SIMC)"]:::fw

    FC_ESC -.->|"RPM — rotor loop feedback"| FC_ROT

  end

docs.title: 2. Closed loops in the diagram
docs.text:
Under the project's control convention (.claude/rules/control-systems.md), every path from a sensor to an actuator must pass through filtering, estimation and control, and be closed by measured feedback. The diagram contains the following loops:

# Loop Path in the diagram Status 1 Rotor speed, 1 kHz per rotor (FC) FC_ROT → DShot → ESC → RPM telemetry → FC_ROT Closed in firmware 2 Angular rate 1 kHz and attitude 250 Hz (FC) IMU → imu_frontend → imu_fusion → attitude loop → rate loop → mixer → ESC → body motion → IMU Closed in firmware 3 Position / trajectory, 50 Hz (Jetson ↔ FC) /imu/data → uav_state_estimator (ESKF) → /odometry/filtered → uav_trajectory_controller (MPC) → /control/attitude_setpoint + /control/thrust → jetowl_fc → loop 2 → IMU → /imu/data Closed, over micro-ROS/UDP 4 Flight commands flight_controller_node → flight/setpoint + flight/active → MPC → … → ESKF → /odometry/filtered → flight_controller_node Closed. odom_topic defaults to /odometry/filtered 5 Camera AE/AWB (Vision) ISP → cam_isp_ctrl → exposure/gain → IMX335 sensor Closed in firmware 6 Thermal imaging thermal_camera → filter + CA-CFAR → Kalman/GNN Estimation chain only, no actuator. ros2_dashboard_node (Vision → Thermal tab) only displays it 6b Stereo depth 2× IMX219 → rectification → SGM → spatial filter → per-pixel Kalman → Z, σ_Z Estimation chain only. The Stereo tab of ros2_dashboard_node displays it, calls services and writes parameters; every action is confirmed by the node's response and a read-back 7 Target following isaac_ros_target_follower_node → /cmd_vel (heading frame) → flight_controller_node (MANUAL mode, manual.source: cmd_vel, v_w = R_z(ψ̂) v_h) → loop 4 Closed on the UAV when the follower reads odom_topic:=/odometry/filtered. On the Jetbot, the base driver (subscribes /cmd_vel, publishes /odom) is outside the three repositories 8 RF defence spectrum_analyzer_cuda → rf_threat_alert → failsafe_controller → flight/nav_command (JAMMING → RTH, SPOOFING → LAND) → flight_controller_node Closed through the FCN. Commands are latched, escalate-only, cleared with ~/reset 9 Relative altitude BMP280 → jetowl_fc → /baro/pressure (σ² = 1.44 Pa²) → ESKF → loop 3 Closed. Previously there was no barometer source

docs.title: 4. Unconnected topics and fixed mismatches
docs.text:
In the diagram, topics with a dashed red border have no publisher in the three repositories. All of them are inputs from hardware or external drivers, which is expected:

  • /points: 3-D LiDAR.
  • /camera/color/image_raw: camera driver.
  • joy: joy_node.
  • rf_monitor/raw_iq: SDR.
  • /odom: wheel odometry from the Jetbot base driver. Only the target follower (on the Jetbot) and lidar_slam_node (with use_odom) read this topic.

Drawing the diagram exposed the following mismatches, all of which have been fixed:

# Mismatch Fix 1 The launch file remapped gnss/velocity → /gps/velocity, while the bridge publishes /gps/vel_cov control_system.launch.py and the SIL now use /gps/vel_cov 2 No node published /baro/pressure The FC firmware reads the BMP280 (already on the SEN0253 module) and jetowl_fc publishes FluidPressure. Settings from datasheet BST-BMP280-DS001: ×4/IIR 2, 25 Hz, σ² = 1.44 Pa², timestamp minus 18 ms (airframe_config.h section 6.4). The ESKF's baro_sigma is now sourced from the BMP280 3 flight_controller_node read /odom by default, and /odom has no publisher odom_topic defaults to /odometry/filtered 4 telemetry_logger_node read flight/state, a topic without a publisher It reads odometry/filtered (remapped through odom_topic) 5 The MPC expected /perception/obstacles, a topic without a publisher Remap obstacles → /tracked/markers. The node now accepts CUBE markers with the tight bounding sphere ½‖s‖, and the CYLINDER bounding sphere is corrected to ½√(d² + h²) (the old formula did not enclose the shape). Markers are transformed to odom through tf2, or through the ESKF pose when the frame is base_link, and expire with their lifetime (test test_obstacle_geometry) 6 /cmd_vel carried two different meanings and had no subscriber The FCN publishes its world-frame command on flight/cmd_vel and subscribes to /cmd_vel (heading frame) in MANUAL mode. Added the nav commands MANUAL/MANUAL_RELEASE; the mode was previously unreachable. Two further bugs fixed: the joystick was not rotated by ψ̂, and signal loss was only detected when the next message arrived 7 /jetowl/motor_rpm had no subscriber The bridge's fc link monitors rate, per-rotor rpm, valid ratio and malformed messages (jetowl_bridge/fc: rotors) 8 /imu/data has two sources (FC and sensor_link) Kept by design: the two sources are never enabled together, and the bridge warns when both are 9 MATLAB read /ld19_scan and /lpb40b_scan, ran SLAM on a single-point range sensor, and used a ROS 1 connection It reads /scan (lidarSLAM, rays filtered to 0.3–12 m) and /range (limit checks only), and uses ros2node with ROS_DOMAIN_ID 10 The RF package had wrong executable names and remaps, entry points to missing modules, two empty launch files, no setup.cfg and no find_packages (no node could run), and a failsafe_controller that was only a TODO All fixed. failsafe_controller uses failsafe_policy.py (tested) and publishes flight/nav_command 11 pipeline_params.yaml and full_pipeline.launch.py set different topics Kept: the launch parameters win, and the diagram follows the launch file 12 thermal_detector put the centre of the Detection2D bbox at the hot blob's centroid, so the box was offset from the object (vision_msgs defines bbox as the object's bounding box) bbox is the blob's true bounding box (centre u_min + (w − 1)/2); the centroid and its 2×2 covariance are in results[0].pose. read_detection and ros2_qt read the position from the same covariance-carrying field; producers without a covariance (NanoOWL) still use the bbox centre 13 The diagram showed /stereo/left/camera_info as a topic without a publisher stereo_node publishes left/image_rect + left/camera_info through an image_transport camera publisher: stereo_node → topic is now connected. The Stereo tab uses this topic as its heartbeat and takes the P matrix from it

docs.title: 6. Updating and re-rendering the image
docs.text:
When adding or changing a node, update together:

  1. The mermaid block of section 1. Declare each topic once, in the subgraph of its main publisher.
  2. The table of section 3, and section 4 if a topic has no publisher or no subscriber.
  3. The SVG image, re-rendered with the bundled script. The script runs Mermaid 12 (dagre) in headless Chromium, converts labels to plain SVG, adds a white background and rounds the coordinates:
npm i --no-save mermaid@12 playwright-core            # at the repository root
CHROMIUM=/path/to/chromium node Docs/flowcharts/render_flowchart.mjs \
    Docs/flowcharts/ros2_nodes_flowchart.md Docs/flowcharts/images/ros2_nodes_flowchart.svg

Keep "layout": "dagre" in the %%{init}%% line. Without it, Mermaid 12 (including mmdc) lays this graph out about twice as wide (~17 000 px instead of ~8 400 px) with many detours.

The diagram must stay below Mermaid's default limits (500 edges, 50 000 characters) so that GitHub can still render the mermaid block.

docs.title: isaac_ros_objectdetection
docs.text:
Source

This page is rendered from Source/Isaac_ROS-Object_Detection/README.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in Source/Isaac_ROS-Object_Detection/.

Object detection nodes for NVIDIA Isaac ROS on Jetson Orin Nano Super: YOLOv5 and SSD-MobileNet decoders for the TensorRT/Triton pipelines, a NanoOWL open-vocabulary detector, a model-agnostic visualizer, and a shared post-processing library with a Kalman state estimator.

docs.title: Signal chain
docs.text:
┌──────────────── feedback (predicted prior) ──────────────┐
                     ▼                                                          │
camera ──▶ dnn_image_encoder ──▶ TensorRT / Triton ──▶ decoder ──▶ [Kalman filter] ──▶ /object_detections
                                                          │                              │
                                                          └──────────────────────────────┴──▶ visualizer ──▶ annotated image

The decoders publish per-frame detections. With enable_tracking: true those detections are treated as a noisy sensor and passed through a recursive estimator before publication: association is gated on the filter's own prediction, closing the loop.

docs.title: Nodes
docs.text: Executable Purpose Input Output yolov5_decoder_node Decode the YOLOv5 head tensor_sub (TensorList) object_detections ssd_mobilenet_decoder_node Decode the SSD-MobileNet head tensor_sub (TensorList) object_detections nano_owl_decoder_node Decode the NanoOWL head tensor_sub (TensorList) object_detections ssd_mobilenet_detector_node Standalone jetson_inference detection camera_topic (Image) object_detections, tensor_pub, detection_visualization nano_owl_detector_node Standalone open-vocabulary detection input_image (Image), input_query (String) output_detections, output_image yolov5_visualizer_node Draw any Detection2DArray on its frame detections + image annotated Image

docs.title: Launch
docs.text:
# YOLOv5 through TensorRT
ros2 launch isaac_ros_objectdetection isaac_ros_yolov5_tensor_rt.launch.py \
    model_file_path:=/workspaces/isaac_ros-dev/models/yolov5s.onnx \
    engine_file_path:=/workspaces/isaac_ros-dev/models/yolov5s.plan \
    source_image_width:=1280 source_image_height:=720

# SSD-MobileNet through Triton
ros2 launch isaac_ros_objectdetection ssd_mobilenet_triton.launch.py \
    model_repository_paths:='["/workspaces/isaac_ros-dev/models"]'

# NanoOWL, open vocabulary, no inference container
ros2 launch isaac_ros_objectdetection nano_owl_detector.launch.py \
    image_encoder_engine:=/workspaces/isaac_ros-dev/data/owl_image_encoder_patch32.engine

ros2 topic pub --once /input_query std_msgs/String "{data: 'a person, a mug'}"

Every launch file resolves its parameter file from the package share directory and accepts a *_config argument to override it.

docs.title: Geometry that must match
docs.text:
The decoders map boxes from the network frame back to the camera frame, so two pairs of parameters have to agree with the pipeline:

  • network_image_width/height — the resolution dnn_image_encoder resizes to.
  • source_image_width/height (img_width/img_height for SSD and NanoOWL) — the camera resolution.

The YOLOv5 launch files pass both to the encoder and the decoder from the same launch arguments, so the two cannot drift apart. letterbox: true inverts an aspect-preserving resize-and-pad; set it to false if the encoder stretches the image instead.

docs.title: Post-processing library (common/)
docs.text:
Module Contents tensor_utils NITROS TensorList ↔ NumPy, with the NITROS element-type table box_ops xywh/xyxy conversion, IoU, greedy and class-aware NMS, letterbox-inverse rescaling detection_head The shared (boxes, scores, classes, count) decoder tracking Constant-velocity Kalman filter bank with χ²-gated association detection_utils vision_msgs message assembly visualization Label lookup and rendering, ROS-free ros_utils QoS profiles, parameter declaration, share-path resolution

Everything except ros_utils and detection_utils is pure NumPy, so the whole decode chain is unit-testable on CPU without ROS, CUDA or PyTorch.

docs.title: State estimation
docs.text:
common/tracking.py implements a nearly-constant-velocity Kalman filter over the state x = [cx, cy, w, h, ẋ, ẏ]ᵀ:

  • Transition F advances the centre by the velocity over the sampling interval T; extents follow a random walk.
  • Process noise uses the continuous white-noise-acceleration discretisation, Q_pv = q_a · [[T³/3, T²/2], [T²/2, T]] per position/velocity pair — positive semi-definite for every T > 0.
  • Update uses the Joseph form, P = (I − KH)P⁻(I − KH)ᵀ + KRKᵀ, which stays symmetric positive semi-definite under round-off where the short form does not.
  • Association rejects any pair whose normalised innovation squared d² = νᵀS⁻¹ν exceeds the 99 % χ² quantile for 4 degrees of freedom (13.277) before IoU is considered, then maximises total IoU with scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment when SciPy is available and a greedy descending-IoU pass otherwise.

dt is taken from the message stamps, not wall time, so a bag replayed at anything other than 1× still yields the correct velocities.

Tracking is off by default: the decoders publish raw per-frame detections unless enable_tracking is set. With it on, Detection2D.id carries the track identifier.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
colcon test --packages-select isaac_ros_objectdetection
colcon test-result --verbose

The suite needs only NumPy, pytest and OpenCV; tests touching ROS message types stub them, and the OpenCV tests skip when cv2 is absent.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Kalman, R. E. (1960). A New Approach to Linear Filtering and Prediction Problems. Journal of Basic Engineering 82(1), 35–45.
  • Bar-Shalom, Y., Li, X.-R., Kirubarajan, T. (2001). Estimation with Applications to Tracking and Navigation, §6.2.2 (CWNA process noise) and §5.4 (χ² gating).
  • Jocher, G. et al. YOLOv5 — detection head output contract.
  • Minderer, M. et al. (2022). Simple Open-Vocabulary Object Detection with Vision Transformers (OWL-ViT).

docs.title: ros2_qt — Qt operator dashboard
docs.text:
Source

This page is rendered from Source/ROS2_Qt/README.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in Source/ROS2_Qt/.

Operator dashboard for the JetOwl flight stack. One ROS 2 node, ros2_dashboard_node, reads the stack's topics with the same names and QoS as their publishers, supervises them (rate, jitter, staleness, publisher presence), and sends flight commands on flight/nav_command only. Every command is confirmed against the measured flight/status, never assumed. For the stereo camera it also calls ros2_stereo's services and writes its parameters, each confirmed by the node's response and a read-back.

Any widget can be added to any tab with Add widget; Serial Interface, System Monitor and Web Viewer are local tools without ROS traffic.

docs.title: Look
docs.text:
• Dark theme by default (less glare in the field), light theme with the header's sun / moon button or Ctrl+T. One QSS template (src/resource/styles/theme.qss) with two palettes (MainWindow::loadThemes): slate surfaces, one blue accent, 8 / 10 / 12 px radii.
  • Status colours keep their meaning in both themes (green OK, amber attention, red fault, blue info, grey unknown) and switch shade with the theme: every one has ≥ 4.5:1 contrast on its surface (WCAG AA); body text is 15:1 (dark) and 18:1 (light).
  • State badges (command result, E-STOP, RF failsafe) are tinted, not filled, so they never look like buttons; E-STOP is the only filled red control.
  • Icons are Lucide SVGs (ISC, src/resource/icons/), tinted to the theme at run time through Qt's SVG image plugin (libqt5svg5); without the plugin the text labels remain. Image, map and 3-D views share one dark canvas tone in both themes.
  • Fonts: Inter, else Segoe UI / Ubuntu / Noto Sans / DejaVu Sans (whichever is installed).

docs.title: Role in the control system
docs.text:
The project rule (control-systems.md) requires every sensor-to-actuator path to be filtered, estimated, controlled and closed by feedback. The dashboard is not on any such path:

  • It subscribes only. The loops close elsewhere: rotor/attitude in jetowl_fc, position in uav_state_estimator (ESKF) → uav_trajectory_controller (MPC) → jetowl_fc, flight logic in flight_controller_node (flowchart §2).
  • It never publishes /cmd_vel, flight/cmd_vel, control/*, flight/setpoint or calls /jetowl/arm. Arming reaches the FC only through the stateflow (ARM → PRE_ARM_CHECK → flight/status → ros2_jetowl_bridge → /jetowl/arm) with its pre-arm checks.
  • Its one flight output, flight/nav_command, is a discrete event for the stateflow, and the operator loop is closed on the measured state (below).
  • Its other outputs act on ros2_stereo, a perception node that drives no actuator: set_processing, ~/capture_calibration_pair, ~/reset_temporal_filter and parameter writes. Each is closed the same way: the node's response (its own validation) is shown, a written parameter is read back, and the processing state is read from the node's diagnostics, not assumed from the button.
flowchart LR

    DB -->|"CONFIRMED / NOT CONFIRMED<br/>within command.ack_timeout_s"| OP

docs.title: Interface contract
docs.text:
Source of truth: include/ros2_qt/core/topic_contract.hpp (unit-tested). Names are spelled exactly as the publisher spells them — relative names stay relative — so a namespace or --ros-args -r remap moves the dashboard together with the stack.

QoS: a best-effort subscription matches reliable and best-effort publishers, so periodic streams use SensorDataQoS. Reliable is used where the publisher is reliable and a lost sample matters (status strings, flags). Transient local is requested only from latched publishers, so their last sample arrives on connect.

Without that package installed the fields show n/a and only the topic's rate and presence are supervised.
