docs.title: Publication
docs.text:
Topic Type QoS Content flight/nav_command std_msgs/String reliable, depth 10 ARM DISARM TAKEOFF LAND HOVER RTH START ORBIT PATH_START EMERGENCY_STOP EMERGENCY_CLEAR

Nothing is published when the topic has no subscriber (the operator is told that flight_controller_node is not running in this domain). MANUAL / MANUAL_RELEASE are left out: they hand the vehicle to a joystick or /cmd_vel source the dashboard does not provide.

docs.title: Service clients
docs.text:
std_srvs/Trigger: mission/start · mission/abort · mission/reset · mission/reload (mission_planner_node) · lidar_slam_node/save_map · stereo/stereo_node/capture_calibration_pair · stereo/stereo_node/reset_temporal_filter. std_srvs/SetBool: stereo/set_processing. Parameter services (list / get / describe / set_parameters) of stereo/stereo_node, stereo/depth_stereo_node, stereo/stereo_3d_node. An unavailable service is reported, not waited for.

stereo_node converts and sends a layer only while it has subscribers, so the contract holds only its small left CameraInfo (health, and P for the probe); the stereo panel subscribes the two layers on screen plus depth and σ_Z, and unsubscribes them when they are no longer shown.

docs.title: Mathematics
docs.text: All formulas live in the ROS/Qt-free headers of include/ros2_qt/core/ and are unit-tested in tests/test_core.cpp.

docs.title: Topic rate, jitter and staleness — topic_rate_estimator.hpp
docs.text:
For the receive times t₁ < … < tₙ in a sliding window of health.rate_window_s = W seconds:

mean period   T̄ = (1/(n−1)) Σᵢ (tᵢ − tᵢ₋₁) = (tₙ − t₁)/(n − 1)        (telescoping sum)
rate          f̂ = 1/T̄
jitter        σ_T = √( Σᵢ (Δtᵢ − T̄)² / (n − 2) )                      (unbiased, n ≥ 3)

This is the estimator of ros2 topic hz (ros2cli ros2topic/verb/hz.py), so the table and the CLI agree. The standard error of T̄ is σ_T/√(n−1). health.max_samples = 1000 ≥ W·f_max = 5 s · 200 Hz keeps the whole window for /imu/data.

A topic with nominal period T (from its publisher's configuration) is STALE when its age exceeds k·T, health.stale_periods k = 3. With independent message loss probability p and jitter below T, that needs k consecutive losses, so a false alarm has probability pᵏ per period (1.25·10⁻⁴ for p = 5 %). k = 3 is also the ros2_jetowl_bridge link timeout (vision_mcu.link_timeout_s = 3 status periods). Event-driven topics have no period and are never called stale; the measured T̄ is never used as the threshold, because a stream that slows down would move its own limit.

docs.title: Command acknowledgement — flight_status.hpp, ros_bridge.cpp
docs.text: A command is confirmed when a flight/status message received after the send reports a mode in its expected set (e.g. TAKEOFF → {TAKEOFF, HOVER}; ARM → armed flag or {PRE_ARM_CHECK, ARMED_IDLE}), not confirmed after command.ack_timeout_s = 1 s. The bound: the slowest honest path is T_ui (50 ms) + T_status (20 ms at 50 Hz) + DDS latency (O(10 ms)) ≈ 80 ms, so 1 s leaves a > 10× margin, including the stateflow's own pre-arm transition. If the vehicle is already in the expected state, the dashboard says so instead of reporting a confirmation of a transition that did not happen.

docs.title: Attitude — conversions.hpp
docs.text:
Unit quaternion → intrinsic Z-Y-X (roll φ, pitch θ, yaw ψ), after normalisation:

φ = atan2(2(wx + yz), 1 − 2(x² + y²))
θ = asin(clamp(2(wy − zx), −1, 1))
ψ = atan2(2(wz + xy), 1 − 2(y² + z²))

J. Diebel, Representing Attitude: Euler Angles, Unit Quaternions, and Rotation Vectors, Stanford University, 2006. Frames follow REP-103 / REP-105 (ENU world, FLU body).

docs.title: Uncertainty display
docs.text: ESKF position 1σ = √diag(P) from pose.covariance (6×6 row-major). GNSS horizontal 1σ = √((σ²_E + σ²_N)/2), SLAM pose 1σ = √((σ²_x + σ²_y)/2) (RMS of the two axes). Barometer ± √variance (1.2 Pa for the BMP280 σ² = 1.44 Pa², Bosch BST-BMP280-DS001).

docs.title: Occupancy grid — conversions.hpp
docs.text: Cell (i, j) centre in the map frame: p = o + R(ψ_o)·((i + ½)r, (j + ½)r); inverse i = ⌊x_g/r⌋, j = ⌊y_g/r⌋ with (x_g, y_g) = R(ψ_o)ᵀ(p − o); image row = H − 1 − j. Grey levels follow nav2_map_server: unknown → 205, otherwise g = 255·(1 − p/100). Since g(19) = 207 and g(20) = 204, the value 205 identifies unknown cells exactly (used by the colour schemes).

docs.title: Flight data tiles — conversions.hpp
docs.text: REP-105 odometry carries the twist in the child frame (odom_twist_in_child_frame: true in uav_control.yaml), so the body velocity is rotated into the world frame first: v_w = q ⊗ v_b ⊗ q*, computed as v_w = v_b + 2w(u × v_b) + 2u × (u × v_b) with u = (x, y, z) (J. B. Kuipers, Quaternions and Rotation Sequences, 1999, §5.14). Ground speed = √(v_w,x² + v_w,y²), vertical speed = v_w,z. Compass heading h = (90° − ψ_ENU) mod 360° (ENU yaw is counter-clockwise from east, REP-103). Position 1σ = √((σ_x² + σ_y²)/2).

docs.title: Subsystem status and command availability — system_health.hpp, flight_status.hpp
docs.text:
Each of the 7 contract groups is reduced to one state from its periodic topics (an event topic's silence is normal): no publisher at all → NOT RUNNING (a FAULT for flight controller, estimation and flight manager); a present topic STALE → FAULT; never delivered or partly missing → DEGRADED; else OK. Diagnostics are STALE after k·T = 3 × 1 s.

A command button is enabled only in the modes where flight_controller_node's stateflow has a transition for its event (stateflow.cpp table plus the airborne failsafes added by add_if_missing); E-STOP is never disabled. Battery colour bands are the flight manager's own battery_warning_pct 30 % / battery_critical_pct 15 % (flight_params.yaml).

docs.title: SLAM 3D — slam3d_mapper.hpp, voxel_map.hpp
docs.text:
The sensors. The LD19 is a 360° scanner that measures one plane (450 rays, 10 Hz, 0.3–12 m used); the LPB40B measures one point along +x (0.05–40 m, 2.2° beam). Neither is a 3-D sensor. The third dimension comes from the vehicle: each revolution is placed with the full pose, so slices taken at different altitudes and attitudes stack into a 3-D map (on a ground robot it is the single slice at the sensor height).

Pose of a scan. x, y, ψ from slam/pose, matched by time stamp (the SLAM stamps its pose with the scan time); z, φ, θ from the ESKF odometry/filtered, the nearest sample within 30 ms, decided once a sample at or after the scan time has arrived. The 2-D SLAM's map → odom is planar, so z and the gravity-referenced roll/pitch are the same in both frames. Without ESKF data the scan is placed planar (z = φ = θ = 0, the 2-D SLAM's own assumption) and the view says so. p_map = R_z(ψ) R_y(θ) R_x(φ) (R_m p_s + t_m) + t, mounts (R_m, t_m) from /tf_static.

Motion during a revolution. Ray i is taken at tᵢ = stamp + i·time_increment; a constant-velocity de-skew from the last two SLAM poses moves it to (x + vₓΔtᵢ, y + v_yΔtᵢ, ψ + ωΔtᵢ). Without it the error is v·T_rev (0.1 m at 1 m/s).

Occupancy. Binary Bayes filter in log-odds (Thrun et al., Probabilistic Robotics, §9.2) with the same inverse sensor model as the 2-D grid (occupancy_grid.cpp): l_hit = logit(P_D/(P_D + P_FA)) = 2.48, l_pass = logit((1−P_D)/((1−P_D)+(1−P_FA))) = −0.865, clamped to ±4 (as OctoMap, Hornung et al. 2013), shown when p > 0.5. Rays are traversed with the 3-D DDA of Amanatides & Woo (1987). The LPB40B follows the SLAM's wide-beam rule: its end voxel is marked only while r·FOV ≤ 2 voxels (r ≤ 2.6 m), else only free space to r − 3σ. Voxels are created by their first hit, so memory follows the surface (37 k voxels for a 9 × 6.5 × 3 m room, against 1.4 M for its volume); free evidence still clears existing voxels.

docs.title: Thermal view — thermal_view.hpp
docs.text:
The view only displays; the thermal chain ends at its tracker and closes no loop here.

  • Position. A covariance belongs to one estimate, so position and covariance are read from the same field: results[0].pose when its 2×2 block P = [a b; b c] is positive definite (a > 0, c > 0, ac − b² > 0), otherwise the bbox centre (producers without uncertainty, such as NanoOWL; no ellipse is drawn then). This is read_detection() of the publishing package.
  • 95 % ellipse (Bar-Shalom, Li, Kirubarajan 2001, §1.4.17, §3.7.1). For e ~ N(0, P), d² = eᵀP⁻¹e is χ²₂ with the closed-form CDF 1 − e^(−γ/2), so the region holding probability p is d² ≤ γ_p = −2 ln(1 − p) (5.991 for 95 %). Eigenvalues λ₁,₂ = (a + c)/2 ± √(((a − c)/2)² + b²), major-axis angle θ = ½·atan2(2b, a − c), semi-axes √(γ_p λᵢ). The table's 1σ is √λ₁, the error in the worst direction. A Monte-Carlo test (2·10⁵ samples) checks the 95 % coverage.
  • Time alignment. Overlays are drawn on the frame with the same header.stamp (the detector copies the image header, the tracker the detection header). On the latest frame instead, a target moving at the 32.7 px/s the detector's low-pass still passes would be off by v·Δt = 1.3 px per 40 ms frame (10 screen px at 8× zoom). An overlay that arrives before its frame waits for it (16-frame history); if that frame was lost (image is best effort) or the stamps come from another clock, the nearest frame is used and the offset Δt is printed. With no detections or tracks for thermal.overlay_timeout_s = k·T = 3 × 40 ms, the raw frame is shown alone.
  • Colour scale. [T_lo, T_hi] = the 1 % and 99.5 % quantiles of the finite pixels (as the detector's debug image), linear interpolation between order statistics (Hyndman & Fan 1996, type 7), widened to ≥ 1 K so a uniform scene does not stretch sensor noise over the palette. Index i = round(255·clamp((T − T_lo)/(T_hi − T_lo))). Inferno is matplotlib's 256-entry table (van der Walt & Smith 2015, CC0) at 8 bit, lightness increasing with temperature; white hot is grey. Non-finite pixels are cyan. Hold scale freezes [T_lo, T_hi].
  • Pixels. Nearest-neighbour magnification with an integer zoom: each sensor pixel is one square, no interpolated temperature is shown. Pixel centres are on integers, so pixel (u, v) covers [u − ½, u + ½) and a box (centre c, size w) holds the pixels ⌈c − w/2⌉ … ⌊c + w/2⌋; T max is the hottest raw pixel among them.
  • Decoding = thermal_detector's: 32FC1/64FC1 are °C; 16UC1/mono16/mono8 map T = counts_scale·counts + counts_offset.

docs.title: Stereo view — stereo_view.hpp
docs.text:
Display only: ros2_stereo is the sensor → filter → estimator part of the depth consumers' loops.

  • Pixel grid. Disparity, depth, σ_Z, confidence and the left rectified image share the left rectified pixel grid at the working resolution, so one cursor probes all of them; the right image is another camera and does not probe.
  • Depth. The node's depth is used; without it Z = f·T/d from the DisparityImage (stereo_msgs definition, zero-disparity rectification, Hartley & Zisserman §9.3). depth/image_mm is millimetres with 0 = no return (REP-118).
  • 3-D point. The ray of pixel (u, v) is m = ((u − c_x)/f_x, (v − c_y)/f_y, 1) with f, c from the rectified projection P of left/camera_info; p = Z·m, i.e. X = (u − c_x)Z/f_x, Y = (v − c_y)Z/f_y, the node's own back-projection. For a fixed pixel p is linear in Z, so the range r = ‖m‖Z has σ_r = ‖m‖σ_Z exactly to the first order in which σ_Z = Z²σ_d/(fB) is itself propagated by the node.
  • Same frame. depth, σ_Z, disparity and confidence of one pair carry one stamp; the probe reads each layer at the stamp of its Z (4-frame history ≥ ⌈30 Hz · 50 ms⌉ + 1) and leaves a value out rather than take it from another frame.
  • Region. valid fraction, nearest Z = min over valid pixels with σ_Z at that pixel (what an obstacle check needs), median Z (type-7 quantile).
  • Colours (inferno): depth over the node's depth window [min_depth, max_depth], read from its parameters, near = bright; disparity over [min_disparity, max_disparity] of the message, large d = bright (the same near = bright); σ_Z over [0, 99.5 % quantile]; confidence over [0, 1]. Non-finite (invalid) pixels are cyan. Scalar layers are drawn nearest-neighbour.
  • Rates of the shown layers come from their header stamps, so they are the node's output rate, not the GUI poll rate.

docs.title: Images and clouds
docs.text: Depth encodings (16UC1/mono16, 32FC1) are stretched linearly over the finite, non-zero values of each frame (0 = no return, REP-118). Point clouds are decimated with a fixed stride s = ⌈n / N_max⌉ (viewer.max_cloud_points), NaN returns dropped; all numeric PointField types and either byte order are decoded.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
src/core/main.cpp            argv → RosBridge; SIGINT/SIGTERM → self-pipe → QApplication::quit
src/ros/ros_bridge.cpp       rclcpp::Context per connection (InitOptions::set_domain_id),
                             SingleThreadedExecutor in a std::thread, Qt signals, command ack
src/ros/dashboard_node.cpp   subscriptions / publisher / clients, copies into plain types
src/ros/introspected_message.cpp  decode a message by type name via its run-time type support
include/ros2_qt/core/        contract, rate estimator, status protocol, conversions (no ROS/Qt)
include/ros2_qt/widgets/     status strip, flight data, commands, alerts, topic health, diagnostics,
                             camera, thermal, stereo, remote parameters; + map and point-cloud
                             viewers (built in code, no .ui forms)
src/resource/styles/theme.qss  one theme template; MainWindow fills the dark / light palette
  • Domain switching works. ROS_DOMAIN_ID is read once by rclcpp::init; the previous build set the variable afterwards, which had no effect. Each connect now creates a new context with the domain from the GUI and passes it the process's --ros-args, so launch remaps and parameter files still apply.
  • The GUI never blocks on ROS. Callbacks copy into a snapshot under one mutex; image decoding, grid conversion and cloud decimation happen in the executor thread. The GUI polls the snapshot at ui.refresh_rate_hz (20 Hz) and the health table at 2 Hz.
  • Clean shutdown. Disconnect / close / SIGINT cancel the executor, join its thread, then release node and context.

docs.text: Parameter Default Meaning ui.refresh_rate_hz 20.0 GUI poll rate of the snapshot health.rate_window_s 5.0 W of the rate estimator [s] health.max_samples 1000 N_max ≥ W·f_max health.stale_periods 3.0 k of the staleness test command.ack_timeout_s 1.0 confirmation deadline of a nav command [s] viewer.image_topic jetowl_vision/image initial image topic viewer.cloud_topic /stereo/points initial point-cloud topic viewer.max_cloud_points 200000 decimation bound N_max slam3d.* see config/ros2_qt.yaml voxel size, inverse sensor model and clamps (= slam_params.yaml), mount fallbacks (= launch defaults), voxel budget thermal.history 16 frames kept for stamp matching (0.64 s at 25 Hz) thermal.overlay_timeout_s 0.12 k·T = 3 × 40 ms: overlay stream considered stopped thermal.counts_scale, thermal.counts_offset 1.0, 0.0 °C mapping of integer encodings (= thermal_detector) stereo.namespace stereo namespace of ros2_stereo (layers, services, parameters) stereo.node_name stereo_node its node name (private services, diagnostics) stereo.history 4 frames per layer for stamp matching ≥ ⌈30 Hz · 50 ms⌉ + 1

docs.title: Build and run
docs.text:
# System packages (Ubuntu 22.04 / Humble)
sudo apt install qtbase5-dev libqt5serialport5-dev qtwebengine5-dev libqt5opengl5-dev \
                 libcurl4-openssl-dev libjsoncpp-dev pkg-config

colcon build --packages-select ros2_qt         # builds ros2_qt alone (no workspace dependency)
source install/setup.bash

ros2 launch ros2_qt ros2_qt.launch.py                       # domain from ROS_DOMAIN_ID
ros2 launch ros2_qt ros2_qt.launch.py domain_id:=42 image_topic:=yolov5_processed_image

Launch arguments: params_file, domain_id, image_topic, cloud_topic, thermal_namespace (default thermal), stereo_namespace (default stereo; sets stereo.namespace and remaps the contract's stereo/left/camera_info). The domain can also be changed in the GUI (Disconnect → domain → Connect).

Thermal view with the software-in-the-loop scene:

ros2 launch ros2_night_vision_owl night_vision_owl_pipeline.launch.py    # synthetic MI48 scene
ros2 launch ros2_qt ros2_qt.launch.py                                    # Vision tab → Thermal

Stereo tab with a rosbag or Gazebo pair (stereo/left|right/image_raw), or on the Jetbot:

ros2 launch ros2_stereo stereo.launch.py sim:=true          # or jetbot_stereo.launch.py
ros2 launch ros2_qt ros2_qt.launch.py                        # Stereo tab

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
colcon test --packages-select ros2_qt && colcon test-result --verbose
Test Covers test_ros2_qt_core rate/jitter/staleness, status parsers, command whitelist, confirmation and availability per mode, attitude, body → world velocity, compass heading, subsystem reduction, grid geometry, image encodings, contract consistency; 3-D: inverse sensor model = 2-D grid, DDA traversal, clamp/clearing, memory bound, scan at ESKF altitude, roll tilt, de-skew, out-of-order arrival, LPB40B wide beam, rotation helpers; thermal: χ²₂ quantile, ellipse axes/angle and Monte-Carlo 95 % coverage, position-with-covariance rule, box ↔ pixel convention, type-7 quantiles, inferno table anchors and monotonic lightness, radiometric decoding (byte order, padding, counts), stamp alignment (overlay before frame, lost frame, foreign clock, timeout, clock jump); stereo: layer table = stereo_node outputs, camera from P (else K), probe Z/σ_Z at the same stamp and X = (u − c_x)Z/f_x with σ_r = ‖m‖σ_Z, Z = fT/d without a depth layer, history and clock jump, region nearest/median/valid, REP-118 millimetres, physical colour ranges, type-7 quantile test_ros2_qt_dashboard_node the node against real publishers with production QoS: best-effort IMU, latched /map, health counts, nav command refused without subscriber and delivered with one, diagnostics fan-in, image and cloud decoding, mission/status (when ros2_mission_planner is installed), 3-D voxel at the ESKF altitude from /tf_static + /scan + slam/pose, thermal frame + detections + tracks with the pipeline's QoS drawn on the same stamp; stereo layers + left/camera_info with stereo_node's QoS → probe (and a layer forgotten once unsubscribed); parameters of a stand-in stereo/stereo_node listed with read-only flags, a write rejected by the node with its reason and one accepted, set_processing test_ros2_qt_introspected_message run-time decoding by type name: scalars, strings, nested fields, reuse of the instance, rejected fields (missing, message, sequence), type not installed, foreign buffer test_firebase_client_config Firebase REST client configuration

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text: Shortcut Action Ctrl+N New dashboard tab Ctrl+T Toggle dark / light theme Ctrl+B Side panel (node name, widget list, log) Ctrl+Shift+T Screenshot of the current tab F1 Package documentation Ctrl+Q Quit

docs.title: Firebase (optional)
docs.text: FirebaseClient (libcurl + jsoncpp, REST API) is enabled at run time when FIREBASE_URL and FIREBASE_API_KEY are set (configure_firebase.sh, .env.example). It is independent of ROS.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Saving / opening dashboard layouts (*.dash) and the preferences dialog are not implemented; their menu entries are hidden and the default tab is rebuilt on start-up.
  • One image topic and one point-cloud topic are subscribed at a time (shared by all viewers).
  • Poses and paths are drawn only when their frame equals the map frame (no TF lookup).
  • battery/state has no publisher in the three repositories yet; the overview says so.
  • The stereo panel makes stereo_node publish the layers it shows (that is how the node saves work); set the image pane to None when the Jetbot's CPU or the link is tight (depth and σ_Z stay subscribed for the probe).
  • The thermal view shows the raw frame (image_temperature), not the low-passed frame the detector thresholds; T max is therefore the hottest raw pixel in the box, not the detector's filtered peak (which Detection2D has no field for).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Check Everything NO PUBLISHER ROS_DOMAIN_ID in the GUI matches the stack; ros2 node list from a shell in that domain Command NOT SENT flight_controller_node not running: nothing subscribes flight/nav_command Command NOT CONFIRMED the stateflow rejected it from the current mode (see flight_controller_node log), or flight/status is stale mission/status fields n/a ros2_mission_planner not installed in the sourced environment (no rebuild of ros2_qt needed), or its MissionStatus fields changed (warning at start-up) Black 3-D view OpenGL 2.1 needed; on WSL2/headless use LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 Thermal: "Waiting for thermal/image_temperature" pipeline not started, or started in another namespace: thermal_namespace:= must equal the pipeline's namespace:= Stereo panes "Waiting for stereo/…" stereo_node not running, or in another namespace (stereo_namespace:=); confidence exists only with the VPI matcher, right/image_rect only with output.right_rectified: true, depth/image_mm only from depth_stereo_node Stereo parameters "not available" the node's parameter services are not discovered yet (press Refresh), or the node name differs (stereo.node_name, or type it in the selector) Thermal: "overlay Δt = … ms" the overlay's own frame was not received (best-effort image under load), or the producer stamps with another clock; the offset is the stamp difference to the frame drawn

docs.title: ROS2_RF_Spectrum — RF spectrum monitor, jamming/spoofing detection and RF failsafe
docs.text:
Source

This page is rendered from Source/ROS2_RF_Spectrum/README.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in Source/ROS2_RF_Spectrum/.

ros2_rf_spectrum 0.2.0 watches the 2.4–2.5 GHz command/telemetry band from an SDR, flags jamming and spoofing, and turns a detected threat into a supervisory flight-mode command for ros2_flight_controller. It contains no control law: the flight controller flies the commanded mode (RTH / LAND) with its own closed position loop.

Executable (node name) Role spectrum_analyzer_cuda (spectrum_analyzer_cuda) IQ → windowed FFT (CuPy on the GPU, NumPy fallback) → power spectrum [dBm] → anomaly test (mean + 3σ) and threshold classification → alerts jamming_detector (jamming_detector_ml_cuda) spectrum → baseline + features → LSTM (TensorRT/GPU) and random forest → jamming flag and confidence failsafe_controller (failsafe_controller) rf_threat_alert → escalate-only, latched flight/nav_command (failsafe_policy.py) 
ros2 launch ros2_rf_spectrum rf_monitor_lite.launch.py   # analyser + failsafe
ros2 launch ros2_rf_spectrum rf_monitor_full.launch.py   # + ML jamming detector
ros2 service call /failsafe_controller/reset std_srvs/srv/Trigger   # operator reset

Parameters: config/sdr_config.yaml, config/frequency_bands.yaml, config/alert_thresholds.yaml, config/threat_signatures.yaml; failsafe actions jamming_action (RTH), spoofing_action (LAND), unknown_action (LAND).

docs.title: Node graph
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    SDR["SDR driver<br/>(external)"] --> RAW[/"rf_monitor/raw_iq<br/>Float32MultiArray, interleaved I/Q"/]
    RAW --> SA["spectrum_analyzer_cuda"]
    SA --> SPEC[/"rf_monitor/spectrum_data"/]
    SA --> AST[/"rf_monitor/analyzer_stats"/]
    SA --> ALERT[/"rf_threat_alert<br/>std_msgs/String"/]
    SPEC --> JD["jamming_detector_ml_cuda<br/>(rf_monitor_full only)"]
    JD --> JDET[/"rf_monitor/jamming_detected<br/>std_msgs/Bool"/]
    JD --> JCONF[/"rf_monitor/jamming_confidence"/]
    JD --> JST[/"rf_monitor/detector_status"/]
    ALERT --> FS["failsafe_controller"]
    RESET{{"~/reset<br/>std_srvs/Trigger"}} --> FS
    FS --> NAV[/"flight/nav_command<br/>HOVER, RTH, LAND, EMERGENCY_STOP"/]
    FS --> ACT[/"rf_failsafe/active<br/>Bool, transient local"/]
    NAV --> FC["flight_controller_node<br/>(closed position loop)"]

docs.title: Processing flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A(["spectrum_analyzer_cuda: on raw_iq"]) --> A1["interleaved floats → complex IQ<br/>(odd length rejected)"]
    A1 --> A2["pad / truncate / batch to fft_size"]
    A2 --> A3{"CUDA available?"}
    A3 -- yes --> A4["GPU: window × IQ, batched FFT, fftshift,<br/>power kernel → dBm, mean over batch"]
    A3 -- no --> A5["CPU: same steps with NumPy"]
    A4 --> A6["anomaly test: bins above mean + 3σ"]
    A5 --> A6
    A6 --> A6b["classify: mean > −50 dBm → jamming;<br/>max > −30 dBm and σ < 5 dB → spoofing;<br/>anomalies > 30 % of bins → interference"]
    A6b --> A7["publish rf_monitor/spectrum_data"]
    A7 --> A8{"jamming / spoofing?"}
    A8 -- yes --> A9["publish rf_threat_alert<br/>'JAMMING DETECTED (…)' / 'SPOOFING DETECTED (…)'"]

    J(["jamming_detector: on spectrum_data"]) --> J1["buffer spectra, learn baseline"]
    J2(["timer 0.1 s: process_detection"]) --> J3{"window full and<br/>baseline learned?"}
    J3 -- no --> J4["wait"]
    J3 -- yes --> J5["features → LSTM (GPU) + random forest"]
    J5 --> J6["combined confidence vs threshold,<br/>alert cooldown"]
    J6 --> J7["publish jamming_detected (on change),<br/>jamming_confidence"]

    F(["failsafe_controller: on rf_threat_alert"]) --> F1["classify text: jamming / spoofing / unknown"]
    F1 --> F2["action = jamming_action / spoofing_action / unknown_action"]
    F2 --> F3{"more severe than the active one?<br/>HOVER < RTH < LAND < EMERGENCY_STOP"}
    F3 -- no --> F4["ignore (escalate-only, latched)"]
    F3 -- yes --> F5["publish flight/nav_command,<br/>rf_failsafe/active = true"]
    R(["~/reset"]) --> R1["clear latched action,<br/>rf_failsafe/active = false"]

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• rf_monitor/raw_iq must be published by an external SDR driver; none is part of this package.
  • The jamming_detector outputs (rf_monitor/jamming_*) are informational: only rf_threat_alert from spectrum_analyzer_cuda drives failsafe_controller.
  • The analyser's mean + 3σ test assumes Gaussian band power, and its classification thresholds (−50 dBm mean, −30 dBm peak, 5 dB spread, 30 % of bins) are fixed constants in spectrum_analyzer_cuda.py without a recorded derivation; their false-alarm and detection probabilities on real clutter have not been measured.

docs.title: Sensor Fusion & Estimation
docs.text:
There is no separate sensor-fusion package any more: the former ros2_sensor_fusion EKF was merged into uav_state_estimator of ros2_control_system, which is the stack's only full-state estimator. Every other estimator below has a narrower job (one sensor, one object class, one clock) and feeds either that ESKF or a consumer of its own.

The chain each of them belongs to is the one the repository requires for every path that moves hardware or estimates physical state (control design standard):

flowchart LR
    S["Sensor<br/>y = h(x) + v"] --> F["Filter<br/>guard · LPF · outliers"]
    F --> E["Estimator<br/>KF / EKF / ESKF / observer"]
    E --> C["Controller"]
    C --> A["Actuator<br/>saturation · rate limit"]
    A --> P(("Plant"))
    P -. "measured state" .-> S

docs.title: Where each estimator lives
docs.text:
Estimator State Fuses Gating / consistency Page Error-state Kalman filter (uav_state_estimator) 15 states [δp δv δθ δb_a δb_g] IMU 200 Hz, GNSS position and velocity 10 Hz, barometer 50 Hz, AHRS heading χ² gates (99.9 %), Joseph update, NIS inside its 95 % bounds Control System CWNA Kalman filter (flight_controller_node) per-axis position and velocity nav_msgs/Odometry from the ESKF or any source χ²₂ gate Flight Controller Clock and encoder estimation (jetowl_bridge, sensor link) host−MCU offset and drift; rotor angle MCU timestamps, AS5047P encoders covariances published from sensor models JetOwl Bridge EKF + PL-ICP + pose graph (lidar_slam_node) 2-D pose LD19 scan matching, IMU, wheel odometry loop closure on the pose graph LiDAR SLAM Per-pixel Kalman filter on disparity (stereo_node) disparity per pixel VPI semi-global matching metric depth published with its 1σ Stereo Vision Constant-velocity Kalman filter + GNN (thermal_tracker) target position and velocity CA-CFAR detections from the MI48 χ² gates, run-time consistency monitor Night Vision Nearly-constant-velocity Kalman filter (common/tracking.py) box centre, size and velocity YOLOv5 / SSD / NanoOWL detections Joseph form, NIS gate at the 99 % χ²₄ quantile Object Detection Range/bearing Kalman filter (isaac_ros_target_follower_node) target range and bearing fused 2-D/3-D detections control barrier safety filter downstream LiDAR AI Perception

On the microcontrollers and in simulation:

Estimator Where Page Mahony filter on SO(3), dual-IMU quaternion averaging, extended state observer JetOwl flight-control firmware (STM32N657) JetOwl Flight Control Log-domain Kalman filter for auto-exposure / white balance JetOwl Vision firmware (STM32N655) JetOwl Vision Mahony attitude filter, Kalman [z, v_z, b_a], Luenberger speed/load observer per ESC coaxial X12 hexacopter core Hexacopter Control EKF chain sensor → median → low-pass → noise identification → EKF JetbotNanoOWL Android console Mobile App

docs.text:
The ESKF reads the topics below. On the vehicle they come from the MCUs through ros2_jetowl_bridge; in Gazebo the virtual MCU sends the same UDP frames to the same driver, so the estimator cannot tell simulation from the vehicle.

docs.title: ros2_lidar_slam — 2-D LiDAR SLAM for the Jetbot (LD19 + LPB40B + IMU)
docs.text:
Source

This page is rendered from Source/ROS2_Lidar_SLAM/README.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in Source/ROS2_Lidar_SLAM/.

Drivers for the two range sensors on the robot and a complete 2-D SLAM pipeline, written from their datasheets and protocol documents and verified in software-in-the-loop.

Part Language Content lidar_slam_core C++17, Eigen, no ROS sensor protocols, filters, de-skew, PL-ICP, EKF, pose graph, occupancy grid ld19_node C++17, rclcpp LDROBOT LD19 360° DToF scanner → sensor_msgs/LaserScan lpb40b_node C++17, rclcpp DFRobot LPB40B single-point DToF range finder → sensor_msgs/Range lidar_slam_node C++17, rclcpp SLAM → map, slam/pose, slam/path, TF map → odom, /diagnostics 
 LD19 ──UART 230400──▶ ld19_node ── /scan ─────┐
   CRC-8 0x4D, sensor clock → host time          │     lidar_slam_node (SlamCore)
   gate · mixed-pixel filter                      ├──▶ gate · Hampel · project(Σ) · de-skew(gyro)
 LPB40B ─UART 115200─▶ lpb40b_node ─ /range ──────┤       │
   CRC-8 0x31, status → REP-117, Hampel           │       ▼

                                                          └──────────────────────────────┘
                                keyframe ─▶ pose graph ─▶ loop closure (correlative + ICP) ─▶ Gauss–Newton
                                         └▶ log-odds occupancy grid (LD19 rays + LPB40B wide beam) ─▶ /map

docs.title: 1. The sensors — what they are and how they are used
LDROBOT LD19 (360° scanning DToF)
docs.text:
Source: LD19 Development Manual V2.3, LD19 Datasheet V1.0 (LDROBOT).

Item Value Used for Interface UART 230400 8N1, one-way, streams on power-up baudrate (the old driver used 115200) Packet 47 B: 0x54 0x2C, speed, start angle, 12 × {mm, intensity}, end angle, timestamp, CRC-8 ld19_protocol.cpp CRC table-driven CRC-8, polynomial 0x4D checked on every packet Sampling / rotation 4500 Hz / 10 ± 0.1 Hz (in-device closed loop) 450 rays, Δθ = 0.8° Range 0.02–12 m; accuracy ±45 mm for 0.3–12 m, none below 0.3 m gate; SLAM uses 0.3–12 m Angle convention 0° = sensor front, clockwise (left-handed) mirrored to REP-103: θ_ros = −θ_ld19 Timestamp u16 ms, wraps at 30 000 mapped to host time (below)

Time. USB-serial bridges deliver in 1–16 ms bursts, far more than the 0.22 ms point spacing. Arrival t_rx = s + o + d with d ≥ 0, so the lower envelope of t_rx − s tracks the offset: ô_k = min(ô_{k−1} + ε·Δs, t_rx,k − s_k). In the unit test raw jitter is 5.7 ms RMS and the mapped stamp 0.3 ms RMS.

LaserScan convention. angle_min = −π, increasing angle; since the sensor turns clockwise, time_increment < 0 and header.stamp is the time of ray 0 (the last one taken). The seam of a revolution is placed at 180° (behind the sensor, cable side).

docs.title: DFRobot LPB40B (single-point DToF) — not a scanning LiDAR
docs.text:
Source: DFRobot SEN0586 product page; LP series communication protocol (DFRobot).

Item Value Used for Measurement one distance along a fixed beam sensor_msgs/Range (the old driver published its raw bytes as a LaserScan) Range / accuracy / resolution 0.05–40 m (90 % refl.), 0.05–12 m (10 %) / ±5 cm / 1.5 cm σ = 0.05/√3 = 0.029 m Beam receive FOV 2.2°, emitter 0.17°, 905 nm wide-beam map model Rate 1–2000 Hz, default 100 Hz configured on start-up Frame 0x55 key value[4] CRC-8(0x31) 0xAA; data MSB first lpb40b_protocol.cpp Status 0 ok · 1 weak · 2 strong · 3 out of range · 4 system error REP-117: ok → r, 3 → +inf, else NaN

It extends the map forward beyond the LD19's 12 m and gives a second, independent range along the direction of travel. In the grid it is a wide beam: its end cell is marked occupied only while the 2.2° arc is ≤ 2 cells wide (r ≤ 2.6 m); farther away only the free space up to r − 3σ is used, because the echo cannot be localised inside the arc.

docs.title: IMU and wheel odometry
docs.text: The yaw rate comes from /imu/data (BMI088 through Source/ROS2_JetOwl_Bridge sensor_link, already in base_link), used as a process input of the EKF. Wheel odometry is optional (use_odom); do not enable it if that odometry already fused the same IMU.

docs.title: Bugs of the previous implementation fixed here
docs.text: Where Defect Effect serial.cpp cfsetospeed(&tty, 115200) — integer instead of B115200 undefined baud rate serial.cpp port not in raw mode 0x0D→0x0A, 0x11/0x13 swallowed: binary protocol corrupted LD19 driver 115200 baud, no framing/CRC, bytes read as 16-bit words no valid range ever LPB40B driver single-point sensor published as a scan physically meaningless CUDA path curvature kernel overwrote the ranges; voxel kernel sorted ranges angle ↔ range association destroyed dual_lidar_slam.cpp did not compile (missing constructor, fragments) no SLAM node existed launch files LaunchConfiguration == 'x' (always false), src/... relative paths back ends never started

docs.title: 2. Quick start
docs.text:
colcon build --packages-select ros2_lidar_slam && source install/setup.bash
ros2 launch ros2_lidar_slam dual_lidar_slam.launch.py ld19_port:=/dev/ld19 lpb40b_port:=/dev/lpb40b
ros2 launch ros2_lidar_slam dual_lidar_slam.launch.py odom_frame:="''"   # no odom → base_link TF
ros2 launch ros2_lidar_slam dual_lidar_slam.launch.py backend:=slam_toolbox
ros2 launch ros2_lidar_slam lidar_visualization.launch.py                 # RViz on a laptop
ros2 service call /lidar_slam_node/save_map std_srvs/srv/Trigger         # ~/maps/slam_<time>.{pgm,yaml,g2o}

Without ROS: cmake -S . -B build -DBUILD_TESTING=ON && cmake --build build -j && (cd build && ctest).

Stable device names (/etc/udev/rules.d/99-lidar.rules; check udevadm info -a /dev/ttyUSBx for the vendor/product/serial of your adapters):

SUBSYSTEM=="tty", ATTRS{idVendor}=="10c4", ATTRS{idProduct}=="ea60", ATTRS{serial}=="<ld19>",   SYMLINK+="ld19"
SUBSYSTEM=="tty", ATTRS{idVendor}=="1a86", ATTRS{idProduct}=="7523", ATTRS{serial}=="<lpb40b>", SYMLINK+="lpb40b"

The sensor mounts are static transforms from launch arguments ld19_{x,y,z,yaw} and lpb40b_{x,y,z,yaw} (set publish_mounts:=false if the URDF provides them).

docs.title: 3. Interfaces
docs.text:
Node Topic / service Type Notes ld19_node scan LaserScan 450 rays, NaN = no echo; gate + mixed-pixel filter lpb40b_node range Range +inf = nothing within 40 m, NaN = invalid lidar_slam_node map OccupancyGrid transient local, published when changed slam/pose PoseWithCovarianceStamped EKF posterior (x, y, yaw blocks) slam/path Path optimised keyframes slam/debug Float64MultiArray every estimator signal, below TF map → odom post-dated by transform_tolerance; map → base_link if odom_frame:='' ~/save_map std_srvs/Trigger PGM + YAML (map_server) + g2o pose graph all /diagnostics DiagnosticArray rates, CRC errors, rotation, status codes, NIS, loop closures, processing time

slam/debug layout (one message per scan, record with ros2 bag record /slam/debug): [t, prior x y θ, ICP x y θ, ν x y θ, S_xx S_yy S_θθ, NIS, icp_accepted, ekf_updated, inlier_ratio, iterations, correspondences, λ1 λ2 λ3, degenerate, χ²_ν, d_max, v, ω, b_g, processing_ms].

All parameters and their provenance ([D] datasheet, [C] computed, [A] assumption) are in config/slam_params.yaml.

docs.title: 3.1 Node flowcharts
docs.text:
Node graph of dual_lidar_slam.launch.py (built-in back end):

flowchart LR
    LD19HW["LD19 (UART 230400)"] -->|serial| LD["ld19_node"]
    LPBHW["LPB40B (UART)"] -->|serial| LP["lpb40b_node"]
    LD --> SCAN[/"scan<br/>LaserScan, 10 Hz"/]
    LP --> RANGE[/"range<br/>Range, 100 Hz"/]
    IMU[/"/imu/data<br/>(use_imu)"/] --> SLAM
    ODOM[/"/odom<br/>(use_odom)"/] --> SLAM
    SCAN --> SLAM["lidar_slam_node"]
    RANGE --> SLAM
    MOUNT[("static TF base_link → ld19 / lpb40b")] -.-> SLAM
    SLAM --> MAP[/"map<br/>OccupancyGrid, transient local"/]
    SLAM --> POSE[/"slam/pose"/]
    SLAM --> PATH[/"slam/path"/]
    SLAM --> DBG[/"slam/debug"/]
    SLAM --> TF[("TF map → odom")]
    SLAM -->|"~/save_map"| FILES[("PGM + YAML + g2o")]
    LD -.-> DIAG[/"/diagnostics"/]
    LP -.-> DIAG
    SLAM -.-> DIAG

ld19_node (and, with its own frame parser, lpb40b_node):

flowchart TD
    R(["readLoop thread"]) --> O{"port open?"}
    O -- no --> O1["open; on failure retry after 1 s"] --> R
    O -- yes --> RD["read bytes"]
    RD --> N{"bytes received?"}
    N -- no --> W{"silent longer than<br/>watchdog_timeout?"}
    W -- yes --> W1["close port, reconnects++"] --> R
    W -- no --> R
    N -- yes --> P["parser: header, CRC-8 → packet"]
    P --> TS["map sensor timestamp → ROS time"]
    TS --> AS{"revolution complete?"}
    AS -- no --> R
    AS -- yes --> G["resample to a fixed angular grid<br/>gate range_min / range_max / min_intensity"]
    G --> SH["mixed-pixel (shadow) filter"]
    SH --> PUB["publish scan"] --> R
    D(["timer 1 s"]) --> D1["/diagnostics: rate, CRC errors, rotation speed"]

lidar_slam_node — one scan through the estimation loop (SlamCore::processScan):

flowchart TD
    S(["onScan"]) --> X{"extrinsic base ← scan frame<br/>from TF?"}
    X -- no --> X1["scans_skipped++"]
    X -- yes --> F["filter stage: Hampel (registration only), voxel 0.05 m"]
    F --> PR["EKF predict to the scan time<br/>(gyro as input, odometry update)"]
    PR --> DS["de-skew: gyro integral over the revolution,<br/>else constant EKF twist"]
    DS --> V{"enough valid points?"}
    V -- no --> V1["skip: too few valid points"]
    V -- yes --> I{"initialised?"}
    I -- no --> I1["initialise map and EKF"]
    I -- yes --> ICP["point-to-line ICP against the submap<br/>gate from predicted covariance"]
    ICP --> C{"converged and<br/>χ² gate passed?"}
    C -- no --> C1["prediction only"]
    C -- yes --> U["EKF update with the ICP pose<br/>(Joseph form; degenerate direction held)"]
    U --> K{"keyframe distance / angle exceeded?"}
    C1 --> K
    K -- yes --> KG["add keyframe and odometry edge to the pose graph<br/>loop-closure search → verify → optimise"]
    K -- no --> M
    KG --> M["log-odds grid update"]
    M --> P["publish slam/pose, slam/debug; update map → odom"]
    P -. "estimate feeds the next de-skew,<br/>gate and ICP initial guess" .-> PR

    IM(["onImu"]) --> IM1["ω_z in base frame → addGyro"]
    OD(["onOdom"]) --> OD1["v, ω with covariance → addOdometry"]
    RG(["onRange"]) --> RG1["LPB40B range → addRange"]
    T1(["map timer"]) --> T1a["publish map when changed"]
    T2(["tf timer"]) --> T2a["publish map → odom, post-dated"]

docs.title: 4. Signal chain and design
docs.text:
No actuator is commanded by this package: it is the sensor, filter and estimator part of the chain of control-systems.md. Its output (pose, map) feeds the planners and controllers. The loop inside it is an estimation loop: the fused pose and velocity feed back into the next scan's de-skew, correspondence gate and ICP initial guess, and the map built from the estimates is the next reference.

CONTROL DESIGN (estimation loop)
  Sensor       : LD19 f_s = 4500 Hz / 10 Hz rev, σ_r = 0.028 m; LPB40B 100 Hz, σ = 0.029 m;
                 BMI088 gyro N_g = 2.443e-4 rad/s/√Hz at 1 kHz
  Filter       : gate (datasheet ranges) · mixed-pixel β < 10° · Hampel K = 2, 3σ (registration
                 only) · voxel 0.05 m · gyro-integrated de-skew
  Estimator    : EKF [x y θ v ω b_g], gyro as input, ICP pose measurement, χ²(0.99) gate,
                 Joseph update; observability rank 5 (ω algebraic), b_g observable
  Measurement  : point-to-line ICP, Gauss–Newton + Huber, Σ = H⁻¹·max(1, χ²_ν), degeneracy
                 via eigenvalues of the scaled information vs. normal-noise floor
  Back end     : keyframe pose graph, Huber, sparse LDLᵀ; loop closure: rasterised correlative
                 search + ICP + geometric verification
  Map          : log-odds grid 0.05 m, P_D = 0.6, P_FA = 0.05, clamp ±4
  Loop         : closed: estimate → de-skew / gate / guess → measurement → estimate
  Verification : 36 unit tests + SIL (tests/test_slam_simulation.cpp), ROS end-to-end with an
                 emulated LD19 on a pseudo-terminal
  References   : Censi ICRA 2008/2007; Zhang, Kaess, Singh ICRA 2016; Olson ICRA 2009;
                 Grisetti et al. 2010; Thrun, Burgard, Fox 2005; Bar-Shalom, Li, Kirubarajan 2001

docs.title: 4.1 Sensor models (every default is derived)
docs.text: Quantity Value Derivation LD19 range σ_r 0.028 m √(σ_bias² + σ_rand²): σ_bias = 0.045/√3 (±45 mm bound as uniform, [D]), σ_rand = 0.01 m [A] LD19 angle σ_φ 0.23° ray spacing Δ/√12 (uniform quantisation of the resampled scan) point covariance Σ_p = J diag(σ_r², σ_φ²) Jᵀ J = ∂(r cos φ, r sin φ)/∂(r, φ); checked against 200 000-sample Monte Carlo LPB40B σ 0.029 m 0.05/√3 gyro sample variance N_g²·f_s = 5.97e-5 (rad/s)² IEEE Std 952 Annex C gyro mean over T N_g²/T variance of the mean of white noise

docs.title: 4.2 Filters
docs.text:
• Gate: LD19 0.02–12 m (driver), 0.3–12 m for SLAM (no accuracy below 0.3 m).
  • Mixed pixels: for rays i, j at angular distance Δ, tan β = r_j sin Δ / (r_i − r_j cos Δ); the farther point is removed if β < 10° or β > 170°. At 0.8° spacing this rejects range steps ≥ 0.08·r per ray (≥ 2.8 σ_r already at 1 m).
  • Hampel (registration only): reject if |x − med| > 3·max(1.4826·MAD, σ_r) over 5 rays. Not applied to the published /scan, because it would also delete objects ≤ 2 rays wide (a table leg at 2 m).
  • De-skew: within a 0.1 s revolution the robot moves (0.5 m error at 5 m for ω = 1 rad/s). Each ray is moved to the pose at the scan end with the gyro-integrated motion φ(t) = −∫ₜ^{t_ref}(g − b_g), p(t) = −∫ₜ^{t_ref} v[cos φ, sin φ]. A constant-twist model fails when the yaw rate changes inside the revolution (entering a turn: 5–10σ heading innovations in SIL); the gyro integral removes them (unit test: residual < 5 mm vs. > 5 cm).

docs.title: 4.3 Scan matching (measurement)
docs.text:
Point-to-line ICP (Censi 2008), e = nᵀ(R p + t − q), weights 1/σ² with σ² = nᵀRΣ_pRᵀn + σ_line², Huber k = 1.345, Gauss–Newton with re-association. The reference line passes through the PCA centroid of its neighbourhood (standard error λ_min/(n−2)).

  • Covariance Σ = H⁻¹·max(1, χ²_ν). Monte Carlo NEES over 60 runs: 2.90, inside the 95 % bounds [2.41, 3.65] of the expected 3 → consistent, not optimistic.
  • Degeneracy (Zhang, Kaess, Singh 2016): eigenvalues of H' = S H S, S = diag(1, 1, 1/L). The PCA normal error σ_δ² = λ_min/(n λ_max) gives a spurious information λ_noise = Σ w σ_δ²/σ² even along an unobservable axis (≈ 2000 m⁻² in a 3 m corridor, which would pass a bare 1/σ_max² = 400 test and claim σ = 2 cm). The threshold is therefore λ_thr = 1/σ_max² + λ_noise(1 + 3√(2/N)); the update is projected on the constrained subspace and the degenerate direction gets σ = 10 m (finite, so it cannot leak into the constrained axes). Corridor test: along-corridor held at the prior, σ_x = 10 m, σ_y = 1.3 mm.

docs.title: 4.4 Estimator (EKF)
docs.text:
State [x, y, θ, v, ω, b_g]. Process: unicycle with midpoint integration, continuous white-noise acceleration discretised exactly, q̃ = a_max²·T_s (Bar-Shalom §6.2.2): q̃_v = 0.1 m²/s³ (a_max = 1 m/s²). With an IMU the mean gyro rate is the input: θ⁺ = θ + (ḡ − b_g)T, input noise N_g²/T. As a measurement of a random-walk ω, the process noise on θ (≈ 1° per scan) would hide the bias (0.03° per scan); as an input the bias converges (SIL: 0.0050 estimated for 0.0050 true).

  • Observability (rank of [H; HF; …; HF⁵], unit-tested): scans + gyro: ⅚ — everything but ω, which is then the algebraic output ḡ − b_g; scans only: ⅚ (b_g not in the model); gyro + wheels only: 3/6 (pose unobservable, dead reckoning).
  • Gating: pose NIS vs χ²₃(0.99) = 11.34. A 1 m jump is rejected (test). Gyro/odometry are only gated against 5σ faults.
  • Lock-out recovery: 3 consecutive rejections of a healthy registration (converged, ≥ 60 % inliers, non-degenerate) re-initialise the pose from ICP; false-alarm probability 0.01³. Found in SIL: a robot already moving when the node starts (v = 0 prior) diverged. The prior is now σ_v = v_max/√3.
  • Initial uncertainty: v uniform on ±0.5 m/s → σ = 0.29 m/s; ω on ±1 rad/s → 0.58 rad/s; b_g: BMI088 zero-rate offset ±1°/s → 0.02 rad/s.

docs.title: 4.5 Pose graph and loop closure
docs.text:
Keyframes every 0.2 m or 30°. Edge covariance J(Σ_i + Σ_j)Jᵀ (two independent registrations). Error and Jacobians from Grisetti et al. 2010 (verified against finite differences), Huber k² = χ²₃(0.95), node 0 fixed, sparse LDLᵀ.

Loop candidates: nearest keyframe ≥ 30 keyframes older within 3 m. Verification: rasterised correlative search ±1 m, ±10° (0.1 m, 1° steps; Olson 2009), then ICP; accepted only if converged, not degenerate and ≥ 60 % inliers. After optimisation the EKF is moved rigidly with the current keyframe and the grid and submap are rebuilt.

Robustness limit (measured, not assumed): Huber limits a moderately confident wrong loop (σ = 0.3 m wrong edge between nodes 4.4 m apart: least squares pulls them to 2.2 m, Huber keeps 3.5 m) but cannot neutralise a very confident one. The geometric verification is the primary defence.

docs.title: 4.6 Occupancy grid
docs.text: Log-odds (Thrun et al. §9.2). Inverse sensor model from detection probabilities with a 0.5 prior: P(occ|hit) = P_D/(P_D + P_FA), P(occ|pass) = (1−P_D)/((1−P_D) + (1−P_FA)); with P_D = 0.6, P_FA = 0.05: l_hit = +2.48, l_pass = −0.87. Clamp ±4 (OctoMap) keeps the map able to change. Resolution 0.05 m ≥ 2σ_r and equal to the beam spacing at 3.6 m.

docs.title: 5. Verification evidence
docs.text:
colcon test: 0 failures — 37 gtest cases (36 unit + 1 SIL) in 8 executables plus test_serial_utils (colcon reports these as 46 results: cases + CTest entries). All also run without ROS.

Test Checks test_ld19_protocol CRC table = manual; manual example packet; all 376 single-bit errors rejected; resync in noise; timestamp mapper (5.7 ms → 0.3 ms RMS); revolution assembly and ray timing (< 0.3 ms) test_lpb40b_protocol all 9 quick-reference frames of the protocol document; measurement example (1453 mm); 8/44-byte frames in a noisy stream test_scan_filters gate; Hampel removes spikes, keeps step edges, < 1 % false rejections; mixed pixel; Σ_p vs Monte Carlo; de-skew exact; gyro de-skew with a yaw-rate step test_scan_matcher convergence from 20 cm/3°; NEES consistency; corridor degeneracy; correlative search from 0.9 m/7° test_pose_ekf F vs finite differences; observability ranks; bias estimation, NIS consistency; gate test_pose_graph Jacobians vs finite differences; loop closure removes drift; Huber limit; g2o test_occupancy_grid inverse-model numbers; free/occupied/unknown; growth; wide-beam rule; PGM/YAML test_slam_simulation complete pipeline, below test_serial_utils baud mapping, errors on missing devices

SIL (test_slam_simulation): 52 m corridor loop at 0.4 m/s, simulated LD19 with per-ray timing (real motion distortion), σ_r = 0.02 m, BMI088 gyro with 0.005 rad/s bias, LPB40B:

Metric Result ICP accepted / EKF updates 99.9 % / 99.4 % of 1307 scans Keyframe ATE (after 8 loop closures) 0.030 m Final pose error 0.015 m / 0.18° Gyro bias 0.0050 estimated (0.0050 true) Map precision 99.5 % of occupied cells within 2 cells of a real wall NIS per axis (expect 1) across 1.13, yaw 0.56, along 0.16 Processing (x86 Xeon 2.8 GHz, 1 core) mean 1.4 ms/scan, keyframe 4 ms, loop-closure worst 66 ms

NIS, stated plainly. The mean NIS is 1.87 against a 95 % band of [2.87, 3.13] for the mean, so the filter is conservative, never optimistic. Across-track and yaw are consistent. The along-track component (0.16) is low because q̃_v is sized for a_max = 1 m/s² while the SIL robot drives at constant speed. On the vehicle, check nis_mean in /diagnostics: above the upper bound means inconsistent, far below means q̃ can be reduced for that robot's actual accelerations.

ROS end-to-end (Jazzy, pseudo-terminal emulating an LD19): /scan published at the emulator rate with the correct CW→CCW mirroring (an object at sensor 100–102° appears at ROS −101°), 2 % injected CRC errors detected (0.020) and reported as WARN, /map, /slam/pose, /slam/path, TF and slam/debug published, and a rotationally symmetric room was correctly flagged as degenerate in yaw.

Still required before driving (verification order of control-systems.md §4): HIL with the real sensors and a recorded bag (NIS inside bounds, bench σ_r), then the vehicle.

docs.title: 6. Calibration on the bench
docs.text:
1. σ_rand of the LD19: park facing a matte wall at 1, 3 and 6 m, record 100 scans (ros2 bag record /scan), take the standard deviation of the ray normal to the wall; sensor.sigma_range = √((0.045/√3)² + σ_rand²).
  2. LD19 yaw mount: place a single post in front of the robot on its x axis; the post must appear at 0° in /scan viewed in base_link; correct ld19_yaw.
  3. LPB40B: compare range with a tape measure at 1, 5, 10 m; the mean error must be within ±5 cm, else set latency_s/mount.
  4. Consistency: record /slam/debug on a representative run; the mean NIS must lie within nis_bound_low … nis_bound_high of /diagnostics.

docs.title: 7. Why no CUDA
docs.text: A revolution has 450 rays. Measured on one x86 core (-O2): the driver's filter chain (gate + mixed-pixel) takes 22 µs per revolution, the SLAM chain (gate, Hampel, projection with covariance, de-skew, voxel) 113 µs, ICP ≈ 1 ms. A kernel launch plus synchronisation alone costs tens of µs (typical figure, not measured on the Orin), so the GPU cannot win at this size; it stays free for NanoOWL. The old kernels also corrupted the data (§1). Their sources remain in cuda/ but are no longer built.

docs.title: 8. Known limitations
docs.text:
• 2-D only: roll/pitch of the base are assumed small (flat floor). Tilted sensors see the floor.
  • The ICP covariance ignores map-registration correlation; edges use Σ_i + Σ_j.
  • Loop closure, correlative search and grid rebuild run in the scan callback. Worst case 66 ms on x86; on the Orin's Cortex-A78AE expect roughly 2–3× more [A]. Watch processing_ms in /diagnostics; moving loop closure to a worker thread is the next step if it approaches 100 ms.
  • Localisation-only mode on a saved map is not implemented (use backend:=slam_toolbox or Nav2 AMCL with the saved PGM/YAML).

docs.title: 9. Legacy files
docs.text: Kept in the tree but not built (their functions are replaced or unrelated to SLAM): cuda/, src/human_pose.cpp, src/lidar_visualizer.cpp, include/ros2_lidar_slam-configs.hpp, include/ros2_lidar_slam/obstacle_detection.hpp, include/ros2_lidar_slam/speech_command.hpp, tests/test_obstacle_detection.cpp, config/lidar_visualization.rviz. They can be deleted.

docs.title: 10. References
docs.text:
• LDROBOT, LD19 Development Manual V2.3; LD19 Datasheet V1.0.
  • DFRobot, LPB40B (SEN0586) product page; LP series laser ranging communication protocol.
  • A. Censi, "An ICP variant using a point-to-line metric", ICRA 2008; "An accurate closed-form estimate of ICP's covariance", ICRA 2007.
  • J. Zhang, M. Kaess, S. Singh, "On degeneracy of optimization-based state estimation problems", ICRA 2016.
  • E. Olson, "Real-time correlative scan matching", ICRA 2009.
  • G. Grisetti, R. Kümmerle, C. Stachniss, W. Burgard, "A tutorial on graph-based SLAM", IEEE ITS Magazine 2(4), 2010.
  • S. Thrun, W. Burgard, D. Fox, Probabilistic Robotics, MIT Press 2005.
  • Y. Bar-Shalom, X.-R. Li, T. Kirubarajan, Estimation with Applications to Tracking and Navigation, Wiley 2001.
  • A. Hornung et al., "OctoMap", Autonomous Robots 34(3), 2013.
  • J. Tuley, N. Vandapel, M. Hebert, "Analysis and removal of artifacts in 3-D LADAR data", ICRA 2005.
