  • IEEE Std 952-1997, Annex C (Allan variance).

docs.title: ros2_stereo — stereo depth for the Jetbot
docs.text:
Source

This page is rendered from Source/ROS2_Stereo/README.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in Source/ROS2_Stereo/.

Two IMX219 cameras (60 mm baseline) → calibrated, rectified stereo pair → semi-global matching on the GPU (NVIDIA VPI) → filtered disparity → per-pixel Kalman estimate → metric depth with its 1σ uncertainty, point cloud, rectified images for NanoOWL.

 ┌──────────┐  ┌───────────────────┐  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐  ┌────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐
 │ 2×IMX219 │─▶│ resize (INTER_AREA)│─▶│ SGM      │─▶│ spatial filter   │─▶│ Kalman / pixel │─▶│ Z = fB/(d−d_off) │─▶ depth, σ_Z, points
 │ CSI 30 Hz│  │ + rectify (Bouguet)│  │ VPI|SGBM │  │ conf·range·      │  │ on disparity,  │  │ σ_Z = Z²σ_d/(fB) │─▶ disparity, image_rect
 └──────────┘  └───────────────────┘  └──────────┘  │ speckle·median   │  │ χ² gate, NIS   │  └──────────────────┘─▶ /diagnostics
   sensor           filter (geometric)   measurement └──────────────────┘  └────────────────┘      output model
Part Language / deps Runs on ros2_stereo_core — calibration, rectification, matchers, filters, Kalman, depth C++17, OpenCV (+ VPI on Jetson) Jetson, any x86 (tests, SIL) stereo_calibrate — chessboard calibration tool C++17, OpenCV bench / laptop stereo_node — CSI or topic input → all outputs rclcpp Jetson, Gazebo SIL depth_stereo_node, stereo_3d_node — external DisparityImage → depth / cloud rclcpp anywhere

This package drives no actuator. It is the sensor → filter → estimator part of the loops that consume depth (navigation, obstacle stop, NanoOWL 3-D localisation); those loops close on it. Its failsafe is therefore on the data: invalid depth is NaN (never 0 or a stale value), every pixel carries σ_Z, and /diagnostics goes to ERROR when no depth has been produced for 1 s. Consumers must treat NaN as unknown, never as free space.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
colcon build --packages-select ros2_stereo && source install/setup.bash

# 1. Calibrate (once per rig, and after any change of lens, mount or flip_method)
ros2 launch ros2_stereo jetbot_stereo.launch.py          # uncalibrated bring-up, see WARN
ros2 service call /stereo/stereo_node/capture_calibration_pair std_srvs/srv/Trigger   # ×25–40 poses
ros2 run ros2_stereo stereo_calibrate --images /tmp/stereo_calibration \
    --board 9x6 --square 0.025 --output ~/stereo_calibration.yaml

# 2. Run
ros2 launch ros2_stereo jetbot_stereo.launch.py calibration_file:=$HOME/stereo_calibration.yaml
ros2 run rqt_image_view rqt_image_view /stereo/disparity/color
ros2 topic echo /diagnostics --field status[0].values     # rate, latency, NIS …

# Simulation / rosbag (left/image_raw + right/image_raw in /stereo)
ros2 launch ros2_stereo stereo.launch.py sim:=true

Without ROS: cmake -S . -B build -DBUILD_TESTING=ON && cmake --build build -j && ctest --test-dir build.

docs.title: Interfaces (stereo_node, namespace stereo in the launch files)
docs.text:
Topic Type Content left/image_raw, right/image_raw (sub, topics mode) sensor_msgs/Image bgr8 or mono8, approximate-time synchronised left/image_rect + left/camera_info Image + CameraInfo rectified left at the working resolution, K D R P right/image_rect + right/camera_info idem P with T_x = −f·B (output.right_rectified) disparity stereo_msgs/DisparityImage 32FC1 px, NaN invalid; f, T, band, Δ = delta_d depth Image 32FC1 Z [m], NaN invalid (REP 118) depth/uncertainty Image 32FC1 σ_Z [m] per pixel confidence Image 32FC1 matcher confidence ∈ [0, 1] (VPI only) points PointCloud2 x y z (+ rgb) [m], left optical frame (REP 103), dense disparity/color Image bgr8 visualisation only /diagnostics DiagnosticArray rate, latency, timing, valid %, NIS test

Services: set_processing (SetBool), topic enable_processing (Bool), ~/capture_calibration_pair and ~/reset_temporal_filter (Trigger). Every parameter is documented in config/stereo_params.yaml with its unit and origin; filter, estimator, matcher-penalty and depth-window parameters can be changed at run time (ros2 param set) and are validated before they are applied.

depth_stereo_node (disparity → depth, depth/uncertainty, depth/image_mm 16UC1) and stereo_3d_node (disparity + left/camera_info → points) serve disparity from other sources (Isaac ROS ESS, stereo_image_proc): stereo_postprocess.launch.py.

docs.title: Node flowcharts
docs.text:
Node graph (namespace stereo):

flowchart LR
    CSI["2× IMX219 (CSI, nvarguscamerasrc)<br/>input_mode: csi"] -->|"capture thread"| SN
    LR[/"left/image_raw + right/image_raw<br/>input_mode: topics (sim / rosbag)"/] -->|"ApproximateTime sync"| SN
    EN[/"enable_processing (Bool)"/] --> SN
    SRV{{"set_processing (SetBool),<br/>~/capture_calibration_pair,<br/>~/reset_temporal_filter (Trigger)"}} --> SN
    SN["stereo_node"]
    SN --> RECT[/"left|right/image_rect + camera_info"/]
    SN --> DISP[/"disparity<br/>DisparityImage"/]
    SN --> DEP[/"depth, depth/uncertainty<br/>32FC1, NaN invalid"/]
    SN --> CONF[/"confidence, disparity/color"/]
    SN --> PTS[/"points<br/>PointCloud2"/]
    SN -.-> DIAG[/"/diagnostics"/]
    RECT --> OWL["NanoOWL / consumers"]
    DEP --> NAV["navigation, obstacle stop"]
    RECT & DISP & DEP & CONF -.-> QT["ros2_qt Stereo tab (display, probe;<br/>services and parameters below)"]
    QT -.-> SRV

    EXT["Isaac ROS ESS /<br/>stereo_image_proc"] --> D2[/"disparity"/]
    D2 --> DSN["depth_stereo_node"]
    DSN --> DOUT[/"depth, depth/uncertainty,<br/>depth/image_mm 16UC1"/]
    D2 --> S3D["stereo_3d_node"]
    CI[/"left/camera_info"/] --> S3D
    S3D --> P3D[/"points"/]

stereo_node — one stereo pair:

flowchart TD
    A(["capture_loop (CSI) or on_images (topics)"]) --> B["handle_pair(left, right, stamp)"]
    B --> C{"calibration pair requested?"}
    C -- yes --> C1["write raw pair to calibration_capture_dir"]
    C -- no --> D
    C1 --> D{"processing enabled?"}
    D -- no --> Z(["return"])
    D -- yes --> E["INTER_AREA resize (anti-alias) + Bouguet rectification"]
    E --> F["SGM disparity: VPI on the GPU, OpenCV SGBM fallback"]
    F --> G["spatial filter: confidence, depth window,<br/>speckle, 3×3 median"]
    G --> H["per-pixel Kalman filter on d<br/>χ²₁ gate, reset after 3 rejections"]
    H -. "estimate is the prior of the next frame" .-> H
    H --> I["Z = fB/(d − d_off), σ_Z = Z²σ_d/(fB),<br/>X, Y from K"]
    I --> J["publish only topics with subscribers:<br/>image_rect, disparity, depth, σ_Z, confidence, colour, points"]
    J --> K["update stats: rate, latency, valid %, NIS"]
    T(["diagnostic updater"]) --> T1{"no depth for 1 s?"}
    T1 -- yes --> T2["ERROR"]
    T1 -- no --> T3["OK / WARN with NIS test"]

docs.title: Design record
docs.text:
CONTROL DESIGN (perception stages; no actuator)
    Sensor        : 2× Sony IMX219, 1640×1232 (2×2 binned, full FOV) @ f_s = 30 Hz, free-running,
                    grab() back-to-back → inter-camera skew ≤ 1/f_s. Measurement y = I(u, v).
    Filter        : INTER_AREA resize to 480×360 (box pre-filter, anti-aliasing) + rectification
                    (Bouguet, from a Zhang calibration); disparity gates: confidence, depth window,
                    speckle (A = 100 px, δ = 1 px), 3×3 majority median.
    Measurement   : SGM disparity d [px], Q10.5 (VPI, Δ = 1/32) or Q12.4 (SGBM, Δ = 1/16).
                    Noise σ_d = 0.3 px (bound of 0.278 px measured on the synthetic scene; re-measure).
    Estimator     : scalar Kalman filter per pixel on d, random walk with
                    Q = (x̂²σ_vΔt/(fB))² + q₀, R = σ_d² + Δ²/12, χ²₁ gate γ = 6.635, reset after 3.
    Output model  : Z = fB/(d − d_off), σ_Z = Z²σ_d/(fB);  X = (u − c_x)Z/f_x, Y = (v − c_y)Z/f_y.
    Timing        : T_s = 33 ms; latency = grab → publish, reported in /diagnostics.
    Failsafe      : NaN for invalid; diagnostics ERROR when no output for 1 s; node refuses to
                    start without calibration or explicit fallback geometry.
    Verification  : unit tests + in-process ROS SIL on a ray-traced scene (below); bench/HIL pending.
    References    : Hartley & Zisserman; Zhang 2000; Hirschmüller 2008; Simon 2006; Bar-Shalom 2001.

docs.title: 1. Resolution change and rectification
docs.text:
A resize by s about pixel centres (the cv::resize convention, pixel centres at integer coordinates) maps u' = s(u + ½) − ½. Composing with u = f·x + c for the normalised coordinate x gives

f' = s·f,    c' = s·(c + ½) − ½,    distortion coefficients unchanged (they act on x)

so the calibration done at the capture size is exact at the working size (scale_intrinsics, checked by ScaleIntrinsicsFollowsPixelCentreConvention). Shrinking uses INTER_AREA, whose box kernel is the pre-filter that bounds aliasing; plain bilinear decimation by 3.4 would alias. Rectification (cv::stereoRectify, CALIB_ZERO_DISPARITY) rotates both cameras by R1, R2 so epipolar lines are image rows and c_x = c_x' (d_off = 0); the baseline is recovered as B = −P2(0,3)/P2(0,0) = ‖T‖.

docs.title: 2. Disparity → depth and its uncertainty
docs.text:
For a rectified pair (Hartley & Zisserman §9.3, §12.1):

x_l = f·X/Z + c_x,   x_r = f·(X − B)/Z + c_x'   ⇒   d = x_l − x_r = f·B/Z + d_off
Z = f·B/(d − d_off)
∂Z/∂d = −f·B/(d − d_off)² = −Z²/(f·B)   ⇒   σ_Z = Z²·σ_d/(f·B)            (first order)
E[Ẑ] − Z ≈ Z·(σ_d/(d − d_off))²                                           (second order)

The first-order σ_Z is checked against Monte Carlo (DepthSigmaMatchesMonteCarlo, within 2 %), and the reprojection against cv::reprojectImageTo3D with the same Q matrix. For the Jetbot (f = 339.7 px at 480 px, B = 0.06 m, fB = 20.38 px·m, σ_d = 0.3 px, Δ = 1/32 px):

Z [m] d [px] σ_Z, one frame depth step of Δ σ_Z, Kalman steady state at σ_v = 0.5 m/s time constant 0.3 67.9 1.3 mm 0.14 mm 1.3 mm 7 ms 0.5 40.8 3.7 mm 0.38 mm 3.6 mm 11 ms 1.0 20.4 14.7 mm 1.5 mm 12.0 mm 31 ms 2.0 10.2 58.9 mm 6.1 mm 29.2 mm 118 ms 3.0 6.8 132 mm 13.8 mm 45.5 mm 265 ms 5.0 4.1 368 mm 38.3 mm 77.4 mm 736 ms

max_depth = 5 m is where one frame gives σ_Z/Z = 7.4 %; beyond it the band d < fB/max_depth is rejected. min_depth = 0.2 m needs d = 102 px < max_disparity = 128.

docs.title: 3. Spatial filter (disparity_filter.hpp)
docs.text: Order: matcher invalid codes → confidence gate → depth-window band [fB/Z_max + d_off, min(fB/Z_min + d_off, D_max − 1)] → speckle removal (connected regions of < A px with steps ≤ δ are mismatches) → majority median: a k×k median is applied only where ≥ (k² + 1)/2 of the window is valid. Invalid pixels are stored as 0, the minimum of the window, so with fewer than half of them the ((k² + 1)/2)-th order statistic is a valid sample — the median can never write an invalid value into a valid pixel, and it never fills holes (randomised property test MajorityMedianPropertyRandomised).

docs.title: 4. Estimator: per-pixel Kalman filter on disparity (temporal_disparity_filter.hpp)
docs.text:
Disparity, not depth, is filtered because the matching error is homoscedastic in d (σ_d does not depend on range) while σ_Z ∝ Z²; a constant R is only correct in disparity space.

x[k] = x[k−1] + w,   w ~ N(0, Q),   Q = (x̂²·σ_v·Δt/(fB))² + q₀     (ḋ = −(d²/(fB))·Ż, Ż ~ N(0, σ_v²))
z[k] = x[k] + v,     v ~ N(0, R),   R = σ_d² + Δ²/12                (matching + uniform quantisation)
P⁻ = P + Q;  ν = z − x̂;  S = P⁻ + R;  NIS = ν²/S
NIS ≤ γ:  K = P⁻/S,  x̂ ← x̂ + Kν,  P ← (1 − K)P⁻          (scalar: identical to the Joseph form)
NIS > γ:  keep x̂, P ← P⁻; after 3 consecutive rejections re-initialise on z (the scene changed)
no z:     P ← P⁻ (coast); output withheld once P > P_max = 1 px²

Stability. 0 < K < 1, so the error recursion e[k] = (1 − K)e[k−1] + … is exponentially stable. With constant Q the Riccati recursion converges to P⁻∞ = (Q + √(Q² + 4QR))/2, K∞ = P⁻∞/(P⁻∞ + R) — an exponential smoother with α = K∞ and time constant −Δt/ln(1 − K∞) (table above); with Q = 0 it is the recursive mean P_n = R/n. Both are unit tests (ConvergesToRiccatiSteadyState, RecursiveMeanWithoutProcessNoise).

Consistency. When the model holds, NIS ~ χ²₁: the gate rejects α = 1 − F₁(γ) = 1 % and the accepted NIS averages F₃(γ)/F₁(γ) = 0.925 (from x·f₁(x) = f₃(x)). NisConsistencyOnStaticScene checks both on 1.1 M simulated updates; on the robot /diagnostics reports the measured and expected values and goes to WARN when the mean deviates by more than 25 % over ≥ 10 000 updates (sampling σ of the mean ≈ √(2/N) ≤ 1.4 %, so 25 % is a real model mismatch).

Assumptions. A pixel is the same scene point from frame to frame, i.e. image motion is small over τ. Rotation of the robot violates this at depth discontinuities; the gate and the 3-frame reset bound the damage, and q₀ is the one tunable term for it — set it only from a recording, checked with the NIS values. temporal.enable: false gives the raw per-frame estimate with σ_Z computed from σ_d.

docs.title: 5. Matchers
docs.text:
Both implement semi-global matching (Hirschmüller 2008): pixel-wise matching cost aggregated along 1-D paths with penalties P1 (|Δd| = 1) and P2 (|Δd| > 1).

  • vpi — VPIStereoDisparityEstimator, CUDA backend: census cost, Q10.5 output and a confidence map (used by the confidence gate). BGR8 → Y16_ER conversion on the GPU.
  • sgbm — OpenCV StereoSGBM (3-way), Q12.4 output, left-right consistency check with disp12MaxDiff = 1 px, P1 = 8w², P2 = 32w². CPU; used on x86 for SIL and CI.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
1. ros2 launch ros2_stereo jetbot_stereo.launch.py, show a flat chessboard (9×6 inner corners, printed square measured with a calliper) and call ~/capture_calibration_pair for 25–40 poses: tilt ±25°, 0.4–1 m, and centres spread over the whole image including the corners. With boards only near the centre the distortion is extrapolated at the edges: the synthetic rig then shows 0.35 px row error at the image edge instead of 0.04 px.
  2. stereo_calibrate --images DIR --board 9x6 --square <m> --output stereo_calibration.yaml runs a mono calibration of each camera (Zhang 2000) and then a joint refinement of both intrinsics and the extrinsics (bundle adjustment). With 0.1 px corner noise on the synthetic rig, fixed intrinsics gave rectified row errors up to 0.65 px (6 draws), the joint refinement at most 0.09 px over 40 draws with OpenCV 4.6 (0.30 px worst with 4.11).
  3. Accept when: the stereo RMS is close to the corner-noise floor √2·σ_c (σ_c, the corner-detector noise, is typically 0.1–0.2 px), the rectified row error is ≤ 0.5 px (SGM degrades beyond it — Hirschmüller & Gehrig 2009; the tool exits with code 3 above it), and no view is listed as an outlier (> 2× median error).
  4. Calibrate at the capture size with the same flip_method; the node rescales to the working size.

docs.title: Characterising σ_d (required before trusting σ_Z)
docs.text: Place a textured plane fronto-parallel at 1.0 m and record disparity for 10 s with temporal.enable: false. Fit a plane d = a·u + b·v + c over the valid pixels; the robust σ_d is 1.4826·MAD of the residual (the same estimator as IdealRigRecoversDepth, which measured 0.278 px for SGBM on synthetic texture). Set disparity_sigma to that value (VPI and SGBM differ), then run a static recording with the Kalman filter enabled and check temporal NIS mean ≈ 0.925 and temporal gated ≈ 1 % in /diagnostics.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Rule order: model → SIL → HIL → bench → vehicle.

Level Evidence Status Unit (core, no ROS) test_stereo_geometry, test_stereo_calibration, test_disparity_filter, test_temporal_filter, test_csi_stereo_camera pass (OpenCV 4.6 and 4.11) Pipeline test_stereo_pipeline: ray-traced plane (1.2 m) + box (0.7 m) through a distorted, toed-in rig; depth within 1–1.5 %, σ_d measured, temporal jitter reduction pass SIL (ROS) test_stereo_node: nodes in-process on synthetic images: depth, disparity, CameraInfo, clouds, chained nodes, parameter validation pass (ROS 2 Humble) HIL / bench VPI matcher on the Jetson, σ_d on a plane, NIS on a static recording, latency pending — the VPI path has not been compiled or run yet

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The VPI matcher (src/vpi_stereo_matcher.cpp) is compiled only on JetPack; it follows the API calls of the previous implementation but has not been built in CI.
  • The two IMX219 are free-running: fast rotation adds a disparity error u̇·Δt_skew.
  • SGBM sub-pixel errors are not Gaussian (pixel locking); the χ² gate absorbs the tails, and σ_d is a robust (MAD) estimate.
  • stereo_msgs/DisparityImage has no d_off field; the external-disparity nodes assume zero-disparity rectification.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• R. Hartley, A. Zisserman, Multiple View Geometry in Computer Vision, 2nd ed., CUP 2004.
  • Z. Zhang, "A Flexible New Technique for Camera Calibration", IEEE TPAMI 22(11), 2000.
  • J.-Y. Bouguet, Camera Calibration Toolbox for MATLAB (rectification algorithm).
  • H. Hirschmüller, "Stereo Processing by Semiglobal Matching and Mutual Information", IEEE TPAMI 30(2), 2008.
  • H. Hirschmüller, S. Gehrig, "Stereo Matching in the Presence of Sub-Pixel Calibration Errors", CVPR 2009.
  • D. Gallup, J.-M. Frahm, P. Mordohai, M. Pollefeys, "Variable Baseline/Resolution Stereo", CVPR 2008.
  • D. Simon, Optimal State Estimation: Kalman, H∞, and Nonlinear Approaches, Wiley 2006.
  • Y. Bar-Shalom, X.-R. Li, T. Kirubarajan, Estimation with Applications to Tracking and Navigation, Wiley 2001.
  • R. Szeliski, Computer Vision: Algorithms and Applications, 2nd ed., Springer 2022.
  • REP 103 (units, optical frames), REP 118 (depth images).

docs.title: ROS2 Lidar AI Solution
docs.text:
Source

This page is rendered from Source/ROS2_Lidar_AI_Solution/README.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in Source/ROS2_Lidar_AI_Solution/.

ROS2 package providing CUDA-accelerated lidar perception nodes for CenterPoint and PointPillars, with optional BEVFusion multi-sensor fusion and cuPCL utilities. The NVIDIA inference libraries come from the upstream repositories as git submodules (see NVIDIA libraries).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This package wraps high-performance CUDA/TensorRT lidar AI components into ROS2 nodes:

  • centerpoint_node for 3D object detection on PointCloud2.
  • pointpillars_node for PointPillars inference on PointCloud2.
  • bevfusion_node for camera + lidar fusion (optional).
  • cuPCL utilities for filtering, segmentation, clustering, ICP, NDT, and octree search (optional).
  • An Isaac ROS integration layer that fuses NanoOWL open-vocabulary 2D detections with the lidar tracks, publishes the result on vision_msgs, and closes a control loop onto the drive base.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• ROS2 nodes with configurable topics, thresholds, and model paths.
  • Optional BEVFusion fusion pipeline with calibration tensor loading.
  • Optional cuPCL GPU utilities as ROS2 nodes.
  • Launch files for CenterPoint and PointPillars.
  • Model assets installed into the package share folder.
  • Isaac ROS integration: camera/lidar semantic fusion, a vision_msgs bridge, and a closed-loop target follower with a control barrier safety filter.

docs.title: Package Layout
docs.text:
ROS2_Lidar_AI_Solution/
├── CMakeLists.txt
├── package.xml
├── launch/
├── src/
│   ├── centerpoint/
│   ├── pointpillars/
│   ├── bevfusion/
│   ├── cupcl/
│   └── isaac_ros/
├── CUDA-Utilities/        own CUDA kernels shared by the nodes (cuda_utilities)
├── CUDA-LidarAI/          CMake project that builds NVIDIA's libraries (lidar_ai::*)
└── Lidar_AI_Solution/     git submodule NVIDIA-AI-IOT/Lidar_AI_Solution (MIT), never modified:
                           CenterPoint, BEVFusion, 3DSparseConvolution, cuOSD, and the nested
                           submodules cuPCL and CUDA-PointPillars (Apache-2.0)

docs.title: NVIDIA libraries
docs.text:
The NVIDIA code is not copied into this repository. It is consumed as the git submodule Lidar_AI_Solution/, pinned to an upstream commit, and compiled by CUDA-LidarAI/ into shared libraries with exported CMake targets. The ROS 2 nodes in src/ link those targets only.

PointPillars is the one exception to the pin: Lidar_AI_Solution pins its nested CUDA-PointPillars at an old revision (092affc, PointPillar::doinfer API), while pointpillars_node uses the current API (pointpillar::lidar::create_core). The nested submodule is therefore moved to its upstream tip with submodule update --remote (below); CMake checks the layout and skips PointPillars with that command if it finds the old one. The submodule is marked ignore = dirty, so this does not show up in git status.

Target Upstream source Used by lidar_ai::centerpoint Lidar_AI_Solution/CUDA-CenterPoint centerpoint_node lidar_ai::bevfusion, lidar_ai::custom_layernorm Lidar_AI_Solution/CUDA-BEVFusion + libraries/3DSparseConvolution bevfusion_node lidar_ai::pointpillars Lidar_AI_Solution/CUDA-PointPillars (upstream tip) pointpillars_node lidar_ai::cuosd Lidar_AI_Solution/libraries/cuOSD isaac_ros_semantic_overlay_node lidar_ai::cupcl_<module> Lidar_AI_Solution/libraries/cuPCL (prebuilt, aarch64) cupcl_*_node, ground_plane_node

What the upstream sources support (checked at configure time, a component that cannot work is skipped with the reason instead of failing at run time):

Component TensorRT CUDA Notes BEVFusion 8 / 10 11–13 libspconv per CUDA major; aarch64 12.8/13.0 are in git, the x86_64 and CUDA 11.4 builds need git lfs pull CenterPoint 8 only 11 bundled libspconv needs libcudart.so.11 and libprotobuf.so.17 PointPillars 8 only any TensorRT 8 binding API cuOSD – any cuPCL – any prebuilt for aarch64 only

JetPack 6.x (TensorRT 10, CUDA 12) therefore builds bevfusion_node, the cuPCL nodes and the cuOSD overlay; centerpoint_node and pointpillars_node need JetPack 5.x (TensorRT 8.5, CUDA 11.4) until upstream supports TensorRT 10.

docs.title: Fetching the sources
docs.text:
git submodule update --init Source/ROS2_Lidar_AI_Solution/Lidar_AI_Solution
cd Source/ROS2_Lidar_AI_Solution/Lidar_AI_Solution
git submodule update --init libraries/cuPCL
git submodule update --init --remote CUDA-PointPillars   # current API, see above
# x86_64 or CUDA 11 only: the libspconv builds kept in Git LFS
git lfs pull

--recursive would also fetch mit-han-lab/bevfusion, OpenPCDet, pybind11 and dlpack, which the build does not need, and would leave CUDA-PointPillars at the old pinned revision.

docs.title: Building the libraries separately
docs.text:
CUDA-LidarAI is an ordinary CMake project; build and install it once, then build the ROS 2 package against the installed result:

cmake -S Source/ROS2_Lidar_AI_Solution/CUDA-LidarAI -B build/lidar_ai \
      -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=87 -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/opt/lidar_ai
cmake --build build/lidar_ai -j"$(nproc)" && cmake --install build/lidar_ai

colcon build --packages-select ros2_lidar_ai_solution --cmake-args \
    -DUSE_INSTALLED_LIDAR_AI_CORE=ON \
    -Dlidar_ai_core_DIR=/opt/lidar_ai/lib/cmake/lidar_ai_core

Without USE_INSTALLED_LIDAR_AI_CORE the package builds CUDA-LidarAI as a subdirectory in the same colcon build and installs the libraries into its own prefix (lib/liblidar_ai_*.so, private libspconv builds under lib/lidar_ai/).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• ROS 2 Humble or Jazzy
  • CMake 3.18+, C++17 compiler
  • CUDA Toolkit (nvcc available)
  • TensorRT (libnvinfer and libnvinfer_plugin), see the support table above
  • Protobuf and protoc (BEVFusion; its ONNX protobuf sources are regenerated with the installed protoc at build time)
  • Eigen3 (cuPCL nodes)
  • The Lidar_AI_Solution/ submodule (see Fetching the sources)

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
Build options:

  • BUILD_CENTERPOINT (default ON)
  • BUILD_POINTPILLARS (default ON)
  • BUILD_BEVFUSION (default OFF)
  • BUILD_CUPCL (default OFF)
  • BUILD_ISAAC_ROS (default ON, needs vision_msgs)
  • BUILD_CUOSD_OVERLAY (default ON, needs CUDA — builds the GPU overlay node)
  • USE_INSTALLED_LIDAR_AI_CORE (default OFF — link against a separately installed lidar_ai_core, with -Dlidar_ai_core_DIR=...)
  • AUTO_CLONE_SUBMODULES (default OFF — clones missing Lidar_AI_Solution/ sources at configure time, at the upstream tip rather than the pinned commit; prefer git submodule update)
  • CUDA-LidarAI options: LIDAR_AI_BUILD_{CENTERPOINT,BEVFUSION,POINTPILLARS,CUOSD,CUPCL}, LIDAR_AI_SPCONV_CUDA_VERSION, LIDAR_AI_{CENTERPOINT,BEVFUSION}_SPCONV_LIBRARY
  • CUDA-V2XFusion (training/export tooling, Python only) is available in Lidar_AI_Solution/CUDA-V2XFusion; there is no node for it.

Example build: 

export CUDACXX=/usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc
export TENSORRT_ROOT=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu

colcon build --packages-select ros2_lidar_ai_solution \
  --symlink-install --event-handlers console_direct+ \
  --cmake-args \
    -DBUILD_CENTERPOINT=ON \
    -DBUILD_POINTPILLARS=ON \
    -DBUILD_BEVFUSION=OFF \
    -DBUILD_CUPCL=OFF \
    -DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER=$CUDACXX \
    -DTENSORRT_ROOT=$TENSORRT_ROOT

If CUDA or TensorRT are missing, the CUDA-based nodes will be skipped and no executables will be installed.

docs.title: Models and Calibration
docs.text:
CenterPoint and PointPillars require TensorRT engine plan files.

  • CenterPoint default: share/ros2_lidar_ai_solution/models/centerpoint/model/rpn_centerhead_sim.plan
  • PointPillars default: share/ros2_lidar_ai_solution/models/pointpillars/model/pointpillar.plan

BEVFusion expects a model root and calibration tensors: 

<model_root>/<model_name>/
  build/
    camera.backbone.plan
    camera.vtransform.plan
    fuser.plan
    head.bbox.plan
  lidar.backbone.xyz.onnx

<calibration_root>/
  camera2lidar.tensor
  camera_intrinsics.tensor
  lidar2image.tensor
  img_aug_matrix.tensor

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
Source the workspace: 

source install/setup.bash

CenterPoint: 

ros2 launch ros2_lidar_ai_solution centerpoint.launch.py

PointPillars: 

ros2 launch ros2_lidar_ai_solution pointpillars.launch.py

BEVFusion (example): 

ros2 run ros2_lidar_ai_solution bevfusion_node --ros-args \
  -p input_topic:=/points \
  -p model_root:=/path/to/models/bevfusion \
  -p model_name:=resnet50int8 \
  -p calibration_root:=/path/to/calibration

Isaac ROS integration (after the lidar pipeline and the Isaac ROS detector are up): 

ros2 launch ros2_lidar_ai_solution isaac_ros_perception.launch.py

# with closed-loop following
ros2 launch ros2_lidar_ai_solution isaac_ros_perception.launch.py \
  enable_follower:=true target_label:="a person"

docs.title: CenterPoint Node
docs.text:
• Executable: centerpoint_node
  • Subscribes: sensor_msgs/msg/PointCloud2 (default /points)
  • Publishes: visualization_msgs/msg/MarkerArray (default /centerpoint/markers)

Key parameters:

  • model_file (string)
  • score_threshold (double)
  • max_points (int)
  • output_frame (string)
  • verbose (bool)

docs.title: PointPillars Node
docs.text:
• Executable: pointpillars_node
  • Subscribes: sensor_msgs/msg/PointCloud2 (default /points)
  • Publishes: visualization_msgs/msg/MarkerArray (default /pointpillars/markers)

Key parameters:

  • model_file (string)
  • score_threshold (double)
  • max_points (int)
  • output_frame (string)
  • enable_timing (bool)

docs.title: BEVFusion Node (Optional)
docs.text:
• Executable: bevfusion_node
  • Subscribes: sensor_msgs/msg/PointCloud2 and multiple sensor_msgs/msg/Image
  • Publishes: visualization_msgs/msg/MarkerArray

Key parameters:

  • model_root, model_name, precision
  • calibration_root
  • score_threshold, max_points
  • num_cameras, camera_topics
  • sync_tolerance_ms

Images must be rgb8, bgr8, rgba8, or bgra8.

docs.title: cuPCL Nodes (Optional)
docs.text:
Executables:

  • cupcl_filter_node
  • cupcl_segmentation_node
  • cupcl_cluster_node
  • cupcl_icp_node
  • cupcl_ndt_node
  • cupcl_octree_node

These nodes require the cuPCL submodule (Lidar_AI_Solution/libraries/cuPCL, prebuilt aarch64 libraries); they are skipped on x86_64.

docs.title: Isaac ROS Integration Nodes
docs.text: Require vision_msgs; see docs/isaac_ros_integration.md for the models, the derivations and the tuning order.

docs.title: isaac_ros_semantic_fusion_node
docs.text:
Projects lidar 3D tracks into the camera, associates them with the Isaac ROS 2D detections, and maintains a recursive Bayesian posterior over the prompt vocabulary for each track.

  • Subscribes: ros2_lidar_ai_msgs/msg/TrackedObjectArray (/tracked/objects), vision_msgs/msg/Detection2DArray (/object_detections), sensor_msgs/msg/CameraInfo (/camera_info), tf2
  • Publishes: ros2_lidar_ai_msgs/msg/SemanticObjectArray (/isaac_ros/semantic_objects), vision_msgs/msg/Detection3DArray, visualization_msgs/msg/MarkerArray

Key parameters:

  • vocabulary (string[]) — must match the NanoOWL prompt, in the same order
  • association_metric (iom or iou), min_association_score
  • sync_tolerance_ms, forgetting_factor, max_log_odds
  • use_tf, camera_frame, static_camera_translation, static_camera_rotation_rpy

docs.title: isaac_ros_detection_bridge_node
docs.text:
Converts between the internal messages and vision_msgs, in either or both directions, so Isaac ROS and nav2 consumers see standard interfaces.

  • Subscribes: TrackedObjectArray, SemanticObjectArray, DetectionResult, vision_msgs/msg/Detection3DArray
  • Publishes: vision_msgs/msg/Detection3DArray (/isaac_ros/detections_3d), vision_msgs/msg/VisionInfo (latched), ros2_lidar_ai_msgs/msg/DetectionResult

Key parameters:

  • direction (lidar_to_vision | vision_to_lidar | bidirectional)
  • class_labels, max_hypotheses, min_score, publish_vision_info

docs.title: isaac_ros_semantic_overlay_node
docs.text:
Draws the fusion result onto the camera image on the GPU with cuOSD (lidar_ai::cuosd). It consumes SemanticObject.projected_bbox, which the fusion node already computes, so it needs no camera model of its own.

  • Subscribes: sensor_msgs/msg/Image (rgb8, bgr8, rgba8 or bgra8), ros2_lidar_ai_msgs/msg/SemanticObjectArray
  • Publishes: sensor_msgs/msg/Image (/isaac_ros/semantic_overlay)

Key parameters:

  • font_path — leave empty to auto-detect a system TrueType font
  • font_size, box_thickness, label_background_alpha
  • draw_labels, draw_unmatched, min_probability
  • sync_tolerance_ms

Unsupported encodings are republished unchanged rather than mangled. The drawing runs on the GPU; the image transport is still a host round-trip, which only NITROS removes.

docs.title: isaac_ros_target_follower_node
docs.text:
Closed-loop follower: Kalman range/bearing estimation, PD heading with line-of-sight feedforward, PI range control gated by heading, a control barrier safety filter and actuator slew limits, with wheel odometry closing the loop.

  • Subscribes: SemanticObjectArray (/isaac_ros/semantic_objects), nav_msgs/msg/Odometry (/odom), std_msgs/msg/Bool (/safety/emergency_stop)
  • Publishes: geometry_msgs/msg/Twist (/cmd_vel), diagnostic_msgs/msg/DiagnosticArray, visualization_msgs/msg/MarkerArray

Key parameters:

  • target_label, min_label_probability, desired_distance, safe_distance
  • linear_kp/ki/kd, angular_kp/ki/kd, derivative_tau
  • cbf_alpha, max_linear_velocity, max_linear_acceleration
  • range_process_psd, range_measurement_variance, nis_gate
  • target_timeout_s — past this the node ramps to a stop open loop

Topic names as set by the launch file; every stage can be switched off with its enable_* argument.

flowchart LR

    PRE --> PP[/"/preprocessed/points"/] --> GP["ground_plane_node<br/>cuPCL RANSAC plane"]

    FIL --> FP[/"/filtered_points"/]

docs.title: isaac_ros_target_follower_node — control cycle
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    T(["OnControlCycle, fixed rate"]) --> DT["dt = measured period<br/>(reject jumps > 5·T)"]
    DT --> E{"/safety/emergency_stop?"}
    E -- yes --> STOP1["EmitStop(hard): ramp to 0,<br/>reset estimators and integrators"]
    E -- no --> SEL["select target: target_label,<br/>min_label_probability, hysteresis"]
    SEL --> H{"target found?"}
    H -- no --> H1{"silent longer than<br/>target_timeout_s?"}
    H1 -- yes --> STOP2["EmitStop(hard) — open-loop ramp<br/>(no measurement to close the loop)"]
    H1 -- no --> STOP3["EmitStop(soft): keep estimator state"]
    H -- yes --> NEW{"new track id?"}
    NEW -- yes --> RST["restart range / bearing filters"] --> MEAS
    NEW -- no --> MEAS["range d and bearing ψ in the body frame"]
    MEAS --> KF["2-state Kalman filters (range, bearing)<br/>NIS gate"]
    KF --> EGO["remove ego-motion with wheel odometry"]
    EGO --> ERR["e_d = d − d_des, e_ψ with deadbands"]
    ERR --> ANG["ω = LOS-rate feed-forward + Kp·ψ + Kd·ψ̇"]
    ERR --> LIN["v = (Kp·e_d + Ki·∫e_d)·max(cos ψ, 0)"]
    ANG --> CBF["control barrier filter: d ≥ safe_distance"]
    LIN --> CBF
    CBF --> AW["unwind integrator by the clipped amount"]
    AW --> SL["slew limits (max_linear_acceleration, …)"]
    SL --> PUB["publish /cmd_vel, /diagnostics, markers"]

docs.title: object_tracker_node and safety_zone_node
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    D(["OnDetections: /fused/markers"]) --> P["predict every track (Kalman CV, dt)"]
    P --> C["cost matrix = distance(prediction, detection)"]
    C --> A["assignment within max_association_distance"]
    A --> M["matched: Kalman update, hits++,<br/>confirm after confirmation_hits"]
    A --> U["unmatched track: missed++,<br/>drop after max_missed_frames"]
    A --> N["unmatched detection: new tentative track"]
    M --> PUB["publish /tracked/objects, /tracked/markers"]
    U --> PUB
    N --> PUB

    S(["safety_zone timer"]) --> S1["for each tracked object: distance to robot"]
    S1 --> S2["zone levels CAUTION / WARNING / CRITICAL<br/>by caution / warning / critical radius"]
    S2 --> S3{"use_velocity_prediction?"}
    S3 -- yes --> S4["closing speed → time to collision,<br/>predicted position inside critical radius → CRITICAL"]
    S3 -- no --> S5
    S4 --> S5["overall level = max of zones<br/>emergency_stop = level ≥ CRITICAL"]
    S5 --> S6["publish /safety/status, /safety/emergency_stop,<br/>/safety/markers, /diagnostics"]

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• libexec directory does not exist: CUDA/TensorRT not found, nodes were skipped.
  • CUDA available: FALSE: nvcc not detected. Ensure /usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc is present.
  • lidar_ai_core: TensorRT not found: libnvinfer.so not found. Set TENSORRT_ROOT.
  • lidar_ai_core: <component> skipped, ... is empty: the Lidar_AI_Solution/ submodule was never populated; see Fetching the sources. The configure log lists every submodule and whether it is populated.
  • lidar_ai_core: <component> skipped, ... is a Git LFS pointer: run git -C Lidar_AI_Solution lfs pull (x86_64 and CUDA 11 libspconv builds).
  • lidar_ai_core: PointPillars skipped, ... the revision pinned by Lidar_AI_Solution: run git -C Lidar_AI_Solution submodule update --init --remote CUDA-PointPillars.
  • lidar_ai_core: CenterPoint/PointPillars skipped, ... TensorRT 8 binding API: expected on JetPack 6; see the support table in NVIDIA libraries.
  • Missing plan files: generate TensorRT engines before running nodes.
  • Overlay draws boxes but no text: no usable TrueType font was found. Install one (apt install fonts-dejavu-core) or set font_path.
  • Isaac ROS nodes missing after a build: vision_msgs was not found. Install it with sudo apt install ros-$ROS_DISTRO-vision-msgs and rebuild.
  • matched_count stuck at 0 in /isaac_ros/semantic_objects: the camera-lidar extrinsics or the frame convention are wrong. See docs/isaac_ros_integration.md section 8.

docs.title: Isaac ROS Integration
docs.text:
Source

This page is rendered from Source/ROS2_Lidar_AI_Solution/docs/isaac_ros_integration.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in Source/ROS2_Lidar_AI_Solution/docs/.

How the lidar perception stack in this package joins the Isaac ROS detectors (NanoOWL, YOLOv5, SSD-MobileNet) in Source/Isaac_ROS-Object_Detection, and how the result closes a control loop on the Jetbot.

Every block below is derived rather than tuned by feel; each section states the model, the equation that is implemented, and the reference it comes from. The unit tests in tests/isaac_ros/ check those properties numerically.

docs.title: 1. Why the layer exists
docs.text:
knows where knows what CenterPoint / PointPillars / BEVFusion metric 3D boxes, velocities a fixed 5-class nuScenes head NanoOWL (Isaac ROS) 2D pixels only any prompt you write

Neither is sufficient on its own. The integration layer projects the lidar geometry into the camera, associates it with the open-vocabulary detections, and maintains a calibrated posterior over the prompt vocabulary for each track.

 /points ─▶ preprocessor ─▶ ground_plane ─▶ detectors ─▶ detection_fusion ─▶ object_tracker
                                                                                   │
                                                                          /tracked/objects
                                                                                   │
 camera ─▶ isaac_ros_tensor_rt ─▶ nano_owl_decoder ─▶ /object_detections ─┐        │
 /camera_info ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤        │
                                                                          ▼        ▼
                                                      ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
                                                      │ isaac_ros_semantic_fusion_node   │
                                                      │  projection · association · Bayes│
                                                      └──────────────┬───────────────────┘
                                                                     │
                                                    /isaac_ros/semantic_objects
                                                        │                    │
                        ┌───────────────────────────────┘                    └──────────────┐
                        ▼                                                                   ▼
        ┌────────────────────────────────┐                        ┌──────────────────────────────┐
        │ isaac_ros_detection_bridge_node│                        │ isaac_ros_target_follower_node│
        │  vision_msgs for Isaac ROS/nav2│                        │  KF · PD+PI · CBF · limiter  │
        └────────────────────────────────┘                        └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                        │                                                        │ /cmd_vel
          /isaac_ros/detections_3d                                               ▼
                                                                              drive base
                                                                                 │ /odom
                                                                                 └──────▶ back to the controller

docs.title: 2. Projection: lidar box into the camera
docs.text:
File: src/isaac_ros/camera_projection.hpp

Camera model: pinhole with Brown-Conrady distortion, exactly what sensor_msgs/CameraInfo describes and OpenCV implements.

p_C   = R p_L + t                              rigid transform, SE(3)
x_n   = X_C / Z_C ,  y_n = Y_C / Z_C           normalized coordinates
r²    = x_n² + y_n²
f_r   = 1 + k₁r² + k₂r⁴ + k₃r⁶                 radial
x_d   = x_n f_r + 2p₁x_n y_n + p₂(r² + 2x_n²)
y_d   = y_n f_r + p₁(r² + 2y_n²) + 2p₂x_n y_n  tangential
u     = f_x x_d + c_x ,  v = f_y y_d + c_y

Three things the implementation gets right that a naive projection does not:

  1. Depth test. The perspective division is singular at Z_C = 0 and mirrors points behind the camera. Points with Z_C < min_depth are rejected, not projected.
  2. Partial visibility. An oriented box is projected corner by corner; min_visible_corners (default 4 of 8) rejects boxes straddling the image plane, whose 2D hull would be numerically valid but geometrically meaningless.
  3. Frame convention. A REP-103 lidar frame is x-forward / y-left / z-up; a ROS optical frame is x-right / y-down / z-forward. The rotation between them
R_opt←body = [ 0 −1  0 ]
             [ 0  0 −1 ]
             [ 1  0  0 ]

is applied automatically when static_extrinsic_is_optical is false. Getting this wrong is the single most common cause of "the projection lands nowhere near the object".

With use_tf: true the extrinsics come from tf2 at the detection timestamp, so a moving sensor head is handled correctly; the static parameters are only the fallback.

CameraInfo handling: the projection matrix P describes the rectified image an Isaac ROS pipeline actually publishes, K describes the raw image. P is used when populated (and distortion is then correctly skipped, because rectification already removed it); otherwise K plus d is used.

References: Hartley & Zisserman, Multiple View Geometry, 2nd ed., ch. 6; Brown, Close-Range Camera Calibration, Photogrammetric Engineering 37(8), 1971.

docs.title: 3. Association
docs.text:
The projected hull of a 3D box is systematically larger than a tight 2D detection: the hull is the bounding box of eight corners, several of which are on the far face. Plain IoU therefore under-reports good matches. The default metric is intersection-over-minimum,

IoM(A,B) = |A ∩ B| / min(|A|, |B|)

which is 1 when one box contains the other. association_metric: iou selects the Jaccard index instead, appropriate for a tightly calibrated setup.

Matching is greedy over the gated score matrix: candidates are visited in decreasing score and accepted when neither element is taken. This is a ½-approximation of the optimal weighted matching (Preis, STACS'99) at O(nm log nm) rather than the O(n³) of the Hungarian algorithm — tight enough here because the score gate leaves few candidates per track.

Temporal alignment. The 2D and 3D pipelines run at different rates with different latencies, so the newest 2D frame is rarely the right one. Detections are buffered and the frame closest in time within sync_tolerance_ms is used; sync_error_ms in the output message reports the residual.

docs.title: 4. Recursive Bayesian label estimation
docs.text:
File: src/isaac_ros/bayesian_label_estimator.hpp

State: the posterior p_k(c) = p(c | z_1:k) over the vocabulary C, |C| = N, held in the log domain.

Observation model. A detector reports label z_k with confidence s_k. Treating s_k as the probability the report is correct and spreading the rest uniformly gives the standard discrete sensor model

p(z_k | c) = s_k                  if c = z_k
           = (1 − s_k) / (N − 1)  otherwise

which is a proper conditional pmf: Σ_{z_k} p(z_k | c) = 1 for every c.

Update. Detections are conditionally independent given the class, so

log p_k(c) = log p_{k−1}(c) + log p(z_k | c) − log η_k

The normalizer uses log-sum-exp, log Σ exp(a_c) = a* + log Σ exp(a_c − a*), which is exact and does not underflow.

Fading memory. Objects are not stationary — a misclassified track must be able to recover, and the prompt may change. The prediction step contracts the belief towards the uniform prior u = 1/N:

log p(c) ← λ log p_{k−1}(c) + (1 − λ) log u ,  λ ∈ (0,1]

In log-odds coordinates ℓ(c) = log p(c) − log u this is just ℓ ← λℓ, so an observation's influence decays as λ^k and the effective memory is 1/(1 − λ) steps: λ = 0.95 at 20 Hz is about one second.

Clamping. log p(c) is floored at −max_log_odds before renormalizing, the bound used for occupancy grids in Thrun/Burgard/Fox §9.2. Without it a long run of agreeing detections drives one label so close to 1 that no finite amount of contradicting evidence can move it. The test suite checks exactly this: after 50 confident observations of label 0, 20 of label 1 must flip the MAP.

Reported confidence. Alongside the MAP label the node publishes the full posterior and its Shannon entropy H(p) = −Σ p ln p in nats: 0 for a certain posterior, ln N for the prior. Entropy, not the MAP probability, is the honest measure of how much the camera has actually resolved.

References: Thrun, Burgard & Fox, Probabilistic Robotics, MIT Press 2005, ch. 4 and §9.2; Bar-Shalom, Li & Kirubarajan, Estimation with Applications to Tracking and Navigation, Wiley 2001, ch. 11.

docs.title: 5. Closed-loop follower
docs.text:
File: src/isaac_ros/follower_control.hpp, isaac_ros_target_follower_node.cpp

semantic track ─▶ LPF ─▶ 2-state Kalman ─▶ ego-motion removal ─▶ PD / PI
                                                                    │
                                          rate limiter ◀── CBF safety filter
                                                │
                                            /cmd_vel ─▶ plant ─▶ /odom ─┐
                                                ▲                        │
                                                └────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 5.1 Plant and error kinematics
docs.text:
The Jetbot is a differential drive, i.e. a unicycle

ẋ = v cos θ ,  ẏ = v sin θ ,  θ̇ = ω

Writing the target in the body frame in polar form (d, ψ) and denoting the target's own velocity along and across the line of sight by (v_r, v_t):

ḋ = v_r − v cos ψ                       (1)
ψ̇ = (v_t + v sin ψ) / d − ω             (2)

docs.title: 5.2 Filtering and estimation
docs.text:
(d, ψ) are measured, their rates are not — and (1), (2) need both. A two-state Kalman filter per channel under the continuous white-noise acceleration model supplies them:

F = [1 dt; 0 1]
Q = q · [dt³/3  dt²/2 ;
         dt²/2  dt   ]                   Bar-Shalom §6.2.2
H = [1 0] ,  R = σ²

q is the PSD of the acceleration noise in (m/s²)²/Hz, so it is set from how hard the target can actually accelerate rather than tuned blindly.

Outlier gate. When the model holds, the normalized innovation squared NIS = ν²/S is χ²-distributed with one degree of freedom, so nis_gate: 9.0 rejects at roughly the 0.3 % level (Bar-Shalom §5.4). A rejected measurement leaves the state on its prediction instead of yanking it — this is what keeps a single bad association from producing a lurch in cmd_vel.

The bearing filter wraps its innovation modulo 2π, so it stays well behaved across the ±π discontinuity.

docs.title: 5.3 Ego-motion removal — what odometry is actually for
docs.text:
The estimator observes relative motion, which mixes the target's motion with the robot's own. Inverting (1) and (2) with the measured v, ω from /odom:

v_r = ḋ + v cos ψ
v_t = d (ψ̇ + ω) − v sin ψ

v_r is what the safety filter needs (a target walking towards the robot must tighten the bound). Without wheel odometry these two quantities are simply not observable, which is why /odom is a required input and not decoration.

docs.title: 5.4 Angular channel: feedforward plus PD
docs.text:
ω = (v_t + v sin ψ)/d + K_p ψ + K_d ψ̇          (3)

The feedforward term cancels the target-motion term in (2), leaving ψ̇ = −(K_p ψ + K_d ψ̇). With V = ½ψ²,

V̇ = ψψ̇ = −K_p ψ² / (1 + K_d) ≤ 0

so the bearing error is asymptotically stable for any K_p > 0, K_d > −1 (Khalil, Nonlinear Systems, Thm. 4.1). Substituting v_t back in collapses the feedforward to ψ̇ + ω, the line-of-sight rate in the inertial frame, which is how the node computes it — avoiding a division by the range that is ill-conditioned close to the target.

docs.title: 5.5 Linear channel: PI gated by heading
docs.text:
v = (K_p e_d + K_i ∫e_d) · max(cos ψ, 0) ,   e_d = d − d_des      (4)

The gate is what makes the proof work. Substituting the proportional part of (4) into (1) for a stationary target gives ḋ = −K_p e_d cos²ψ, so with W = ½e_d²

Ẇ = −K_p e_d² cos²ψ ≤ 0

Clipping the gate at zero also stops the robot driving forward while the target is behind it, where cos ψ < 0 would flip the sign of the feedback.

Anti-windup. The PI integrator uses back-calculation (Åström & Hägglund, Advanced PID Control, §3.5):

İ = K_i e + K_t (sat(u) − u)

which bounds the wind-up at u_max + K_i e / K_t instead of letting it grow without limit. The node additionally calls ApplyOutputCorrection with what the downstream stages actually applied, so the integrator also unwinds when the heading gate or the safety filter overrides the controller — not only when the actuator saturates.

The derivative acts on a low-pass filtered error. This is mandatory: the raw difference of a noisy error amplifies noise by K_d/dt, a factor of 20 at 20 Hz.

docs.title: 5.6 Safety: control barrier function
docs.text:
Safe set C = {x : h(x) ≥ 0} with h = d − d_safe. Along (1), ḣ = v_r − v cos ψ, so the exponential CBF condition ḣ ≥ −αh is affine in v:

v cos ψ ≤ α(d − d_safe) + v_r
⟺  v ≤ v_max_safe = (αh + v_r) / cos ψ        for cos ψ > ε        (5)

The minimum-intervention QP min (v − v_des)² subject to (5) has the closed-form solution v* = min(v_des, v_max_safe), so no solver is needed. By Ames et al. (ECC 2019, Thm. 2) any locally Lipschitz controller satisfying (5) renders C forward invariant: if h(x₀) ≥ 0 then h(x_t) ≥ 0 for all t ≥ 0.

The test suite verifies this numerically by running 400 cycles of a controller that always demands full speed and asserting the clearance never goes negative.

Two cases sit outside (5) and are handled explicitly:

  • cos ψ ≤ ε — the target is abeam or behind, forward motion does not close the range, and the constraint is vacuous.
  • h < 0 — already inside the clearance. The bound turns negative and commands a reverse that drives h back to 0 exponentially. This is the intended recovery and requires allow_reverse: true; otherwise the robot is held at 0.

α has a direct physical reading: the range may decay no faster than exp(−αt) towards d_safe.

docs.title: 5.7 Actuator limits and fail-safe
docs.text:
Slew limiters enforce |v̇| ≤ a_max and |ω̇| ≤ α_max. Commanding a step the motors cannot follow makes the measured velocity lag the command, which the feedback then reads as a disturbance; limiting the command keeps the plant inside the region where the linear design holds.

The one open-loop path. When no target has been seen for target_timeout_s there is no feedback signal, so the loop cannot be closed. The node ramps the command to zero through the slew limiters and resets the estimators and integrators. This is the only open-loop path in the node and exists solely to bring the robot to a controlled stop. /safety/emergency_stop from safety_zone_node short-circuits everything and commands zero directly.

docs.title: 5.8 Tuning order
docs.text:
1. safe_distance and max_linear_velocity from the physical envelope.
  2. range_measurement_variance ≈ the tracker's position noise, in m²; range_process_psd ≈ the target's peak acceleration squared.
  3. angular_kp, then angular_kd — the heading loop settles first.
  4. linear_kp, then linear_ki just large enough to remove the steady-state offset.
  5. cbf_alpha last: raise it for a more assertive approach, lower it to stop further out.

safe_distance must stay below desired_distance; the node clamps it to 0.8 · desired_distance and warns otherwise, because a barrier that opposes the set point produces a permanent standoff.

docs.title: 6. vision_msgs bridge
docs.text:
File: src/isaac_ros/isaac_ros_detection_bridge_node.cpp

TrackedObjectArray  ─┐
SemanticObjectArray ─┼─▶ vision_msgs/Detection3DArray  (+ VisionInfo, latched)
DetectionResult     ─┘
vision_msgs/Detection3DArray ─▶ DetectionResult   (feeds detection_fusion_node)

A SemanticObject carries a full posterior, which maps exactly onto the ObjectHypothesisWithPose[] array of vision_msgs: the top-k labels are published in decreasing probability, so a consumer can reason about the runner-up instead of only the MAP label.

VisionInfo is published on a transient-local (latched) topic, so a consumer that starts later still receives the label database.

Known limitation: vision_msgs/Detection3D has no velocity field. Consumers that need the tracked kinematics must subscribe to TrackedObjectArray or SemanticObjectArray directly.

docs.title: 6b. GPU overlay
docs.text:
File: src/isaac_ros/isaac_ros_semantic_overlay_node.cpp

The fusion node already publishes each track's pixel box in SemanticObject.projected_bbox, so the overlay is a pure rendering stage: box plus label, drawn with cuOSD, NVIDIA's GPU on-screen display library.

Rasterising text is the expensive half of an overlay — a glyph atlas blended per pixel — and that is what moves to the GPU. Box outlines are nearly free either way.

What this does not buy you. sensor_msgs/Image lives in host memory, so each frame still pays one host-to-device and one device-to-host copy. The drawing is on the GPU; the transport is not. Those copies disappear only when the whole image pipeline is negotiated through NITROS. On a Jetson's unified memory the copies are cheap enough that text rasterisation still dominates, but the honest summary is: this replaces CPU glyph rendering, not the round-trip.

Implementation notes worth knowing:

  • Labels are coloured by an FNV-1a hash of the label string, so a prompt keeps the same colour across frames and across runs — which matters when reviewing a recording. std::hash is not used because it may differ between standard library versions.
  • bgr8/bgra8 are supported by swapping the red and blue components of the drawing colours, which is exact and free. Unsupported encodings are republished unchanged rather than mangled.
  • Stride comes from Image::step, not width * channels, because ROS images may pad rows.
  • A font is accepted only if it exists and is non-empty: the .ttf files in the vendored sample trees are zero-byte placeholders, and stb_truetype on an empty buffer yields garbage metrics instead of failing cleanly.

docs.title: 6c. GPU point extraction
docs.text:
cuda_utils::ExtractXYZFromPointCloud2 de-interleaves a PointCloud2 on the device, replacing the per-point PointCloud2ConstIterator loop in centerpoint_node and pointcloud_preprocessor_node.

Why the transfer does not get bigger. The staged copy is the raw message buffer — point_step bytes per point — instead of the packed feature array, feature_num floats per point. For a 16-byte point_step that is 16N bytes against 20N: strictly less. A wider point_step trades a larger copy for dropping the scalar CPU loop entirely, which on unified memory is the cheaper side of the trade.

The guard. The kernel reinterprets raw bytes as floats, which PointCloud2 does not guarantee. src/common/pointcloud_layout.hpp checks, before every frame:

  1. x, y, z are FLOAT32 with count == 1;
  2. the cloud is little-endian;
  3. every field read lies fully inside point_step, and the points read are fully backed by data;
  4. intensity is FLOAT32 — otherwise it is dropped, not reinterpreted.

Violating any of these is silent corruption, not a crash, because every byte pattern is a legal float. A cloud that fails is routed to the CPU loop and the reason is logged once. The header carries no ROS, CUDA or Eigen dependency precisely so this reasoning is unit tested on machines that cannot compile the kernel it guards (tests/pointcloud/).

centerpoint_node reports which path each frame took as point_extraction: gpu|cpu in /diagnostics, so a silent fallback shows up as more than a lower frame rate.

Not done: PointPillars. PointPillar::forward() takes a host pointer and copies internally, and its header lives in the CUDA-PointPillars submodule. Feeding it a device buffer would mean patching upstream vendored code, which breaks the ability to track upstream. It keeps the CPU loop.

docs.title: 7. Bring-up
docs.text:
# 1. Messages first (two-stage build)
colcon build --packages-select ros2_lidar_ai_msgs

# 2. The package
colcon build --packages-select ros2_lidar_ai_solution --symlink-install \
  --cmake-args -DBUILD_ISAAC_ROS=ON

source install/setup.bash

# 3. Lidar perception
ros2 launch ros2_lidar_ai_solution full_pipeline.launch.py

# 4. Isaac ROS NanoOWL (separate package)
ros2 launch isaac_ros_objectdetection nano_owl_tensor_rt.launch.py

# 5. Integration layer
ros2 launch ros2_lidar_ai_solution isaac_ros_perception.launch.py

# 6. Closed-loop following (commands the drive base)
ros2 launch ros2_lidar_ai_solution isaac_ros_perception.launch.py \
    enable_follower:=true target_label:="a person"

# 7. GPU overlay on the camera stream
ros2 launch ros2_lidar_ai_solution isaac_ros_perception.launch.py \
    enable_overlay:=true image_topic:=/image_raw

The vocabulary parameter must list the NanoOWL prompts in the same order they were given to the encoder: the decoder publishes the prompt index as Detection2D.class_id. A mismatch shows up as a throttled warning naming the unrecognized class_id.

docs.title: Inspecting the loop
docs.text:
ros2 topic echo /isaac_ros/semantic_objects --field objects[0].label
ros2 topic echo /isaac_ros/semantic_objects --field sync_error_ms
ros2 topic echo /diagnostics                       # follower internals, 20 Hz
ros2 run rqt_plot rqt_plot                         # plot /cmd_vel against /odom

The follower's diagnostics expose range_m, bearing_rad, range_rate_mps, target_range_rate_mps, clearance_m, barrier_bound_mps, linear_integral and gate_rejections — enough to tell a tuning problem from a perception one without a debugger.

docs.title: 8. Failure modes
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix matched_count always 0 wrong extrinsics or frame convention check static_extrinsic_is_optical, verify ros2 run tf2_tools view_frames sync_error_ms near the tolerance camera and lidar pipelines far apart in latency raise sync_tolerance_ms, or detection_buffer_size labels flicker forgetting_factor too low raise towards 0.98 labels stick after the object changes max_log_odds too high lower towards 4.0 warning about an unrecognized class_id vocabulary does not match the NanoOWL prompt align order and spelling follower oscillates around the set point linear_ki too high, or derivative_tau too small halve linear_ki, raise derivative_tau follower stops short and never closes safe_distance too close to desired_distance, or cbf_alpha too low widen the gap, raise cbf_alpha cmd_vel stutters tracker dropouts; check gate_rejections in /diagnostics raise nis_gate, or measurement_tau above 0 nodes missing after a build vision_msgs not installed sudo apt install ros-$ROS_DISTRO-vision-msgs overlay draws boxes but no text no usable TrueType font apt install fonts-dejavu-core, or set font_path overlay republishes the image unchanged encoding unsupported, or no semantic array within sync_tolerance_ms convert to rgb8, or raise the tolerance point_extraction: cpu in /diagnostics the cloud failed the GPU layout guard read the one-off warning; usually a non-FLOAT32 or big-endian publisher

C/C++ simulation for the ROS 2 nodes in Source/. On the vehicle the IMU, GNSS and encoders are read by the MCU and sent to the Jetson over Ethernet; in Gazebo a virtual MCU sends the same UDP frames to the same Jetson driver, so every node downstream runs unchanged in simulation and on the vehicle.

 Vehicle:  sensors ─▶ MCU (STM32N6, protocol.c) ────Ethernet/UDP─┐
 Gazebo:   ground truth ─▶ error models ─▶ virtual MCU (protocol.c) ─UDP─┤
                                                                 ▼
                     ros2_jetowl_bridge/jetowl_bridge (Jetson, sensor_link) ─▶ /imu/data, /gps/fix, /gps/vel,
                                                            /encoders/joint_states, /diagnostics
                                                                 ▼
                     ROS2_Control_System (ESKF), ROS2_Flight_Controller, ROS2_Mission_Planner …
Package Language Content Guide ROS2_Mcu_Emulator C++17 virtual MCU: IMU/GNSS/encoder error models, WGS-84, generic McuEmulatorSystem gz plugin. The wire protocol (CRC-32) and the Jetson driver (clock-sync Kalman filter, encoder speed estimator, covariances, diagnostics) live in Source/ROS2_JetOwl_Bridge README ROS2_Hexacopter_Description xacro/YAML coaxial X12 hexacopter physical parameters (single source of truth), URDF README ROS2_Hexacopter_Control C++17 BLDC/FOC ESC, allocation, estimators, cascaded control, gain synthesis + margin proofs README ROS2_Hexacopter_Gazebo C++17 Gazebo Harmonic (gz-sim 8) plugin, lock-step 1 kHz, motors at 20 kHz, MCU link, SIL tests README

C++ style for this directory: .clang-format (Google, 100 columns). Python: black -S -l 99, flake8 --max-line-length 99.

# Hexacopter: build, prove, fly — sensor topics for Source/ come through the MCU link
colcon build --packages-up-to ros2_hexacopter_gazebo && source install/setup.bash
ros2 run ros2_hexacopter_control hexa_design_report
ros2 launch ros2_hexacopter_gazebo hexacopter_sim.launch.py sensor_fusion:=true

# Vehicle: the same node against the real MCU (192.168.1.103)
ros2 launch ros2_jetowl_bridge jetowl_bridge.launch.py fc:=false sensor_link:=true
ros2 run ros2_jetowl_bridge mcu_link_dump --mcu 192.168.1.103:9871   # bench check, no ROS

docs.title: ros2_hexacopter_control
docs.text:
Source

This page is rendered from Gazebo/ROS2_Hexacopter_Control/README.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in Gazebo/ROS2_Hexacopter_Control/.

ROS- and Gazebo-independent C++17 flight-control core for the coaxial X12 hexacopter (6 arms × 2 BLDC rotors with encoders). Builds with colcon or plain CMake (Eigen, yaml-cpp). The Gazebo plugin in ros2_hexacopter_gazebo is a thin adapter around it; overview, evidence and limits are in that package's README.

Header Content parameters.hpp plant (hexacopter_physical.yaml) + design specs (config/flight_control.yaml) airframe.hpp rotor geometry, k_T/k_Q, effectiveness matrix, voltage-circle ω_max, T/W bldc_esc.hpp BLDC dq model (RK4, 20 kHz), FOC ESC: IMC current PI, Luenberger speed/load observer on the encoder, speed PI + exact FF, fault detection allocation.hpp minimum-norm allocation, priority roll/pitch > yaw > thrust, rotor-failure aware sensors.hpp BMI088 / MS5611 noise and bias models estimators.hpp Mahony attitude filter; Kalman [z, v_z, b_a] flight_controller.hpp calibration, altitude→climb→thrust, attitude→rate→torque, allocation → ω_ref design.hpp gain synthesis and frequency-domain margins of every loop, ±20 % corners vehicle_model.hpp, simulator.hpp rotor wrench (thrust, reaction, gyroscopic, drag) and 6-DOF SIL 
ros2 run ros2_hexacopter_control hexa_design_report      # exit code 0 = PASS
colcon test --packages-select ros2_hexacopter_control     # 6 gtest suites
# or: cmake -S . -B build && cmake --build build -j && (cd build && ctest)

Every gain is computed at start-up from the two YAML files. config/flight_control.yaml contains specifications (bandwidths, damping ratios, separations, limits), never gains. Change a physical parameter and the controller is re-designed; the tests then re-prove the margins.

This page is rendered from Gazebo/ROS2_Hexacopter_Description/README.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in Gazebo/ROS2_Hexacopter_Description/.

Physical parameters and URDF/xacro of the coaxial X12 hexacopter.

  • config/hexacopter_physical.yaml is the single source of truth for mass, inertia, arm geometry, propeller, BLDC motor, encoder, IMU and barometer. It is read by the xacro, by the C++ controller design and by the Gazebo plugin. Values are tagged [G] geometry, [D] datasheet, [R] from the repository's MATLAB config or [A] assumption.
  • urdf/hexacopter.urdf.xacro is one rigid body (CoM at the base_link origin) with visual-only arms, motors and 12 rotor discs, 4 landing-gear contacts, and the HexacopterSystem plugin block.
  • test/test_hexacopter_urdf.py checks the URDF mass/inertia against the YAML, and every rotor visual against the rotor positions the allocator uses.
ros2 launch ros2_hexacopter_description display.launch.py

docs.title: Coaxial X12 hexacopter — Gazebo C++ simulation
docs.text:
Source

This page is rendered from Gazebo/ROS2_Hexacopter_Gazebo/README.md, the authoritative description kept next to the code in Gazebo/ROS2_Hexacopter_Gazebo/.

A hexacopter with 6 arms × 2 counter-rotating BLDC motors (12 rotors), each with an encoder, simulated in Gazebo Harmonic (gz-sim 8) by a native C++ system plugin. The motor physics, the ESC firmware and the flight controller all run inside the physics step (lock-step, deterministic). Three colcon packages make up the stack:

Package Content ros2_hexacopter_description hexacopter_physical.yaml (single source of truth), URDF/xacro, RViz display ros2_hexacopter_control ROS/Gazebo-independent C++17 core: BLDC + FOC ESC + encoder observer, allocation, estimators, cascaded control, gain synthesis + margin proofs, 6-DOF simulator, gtest suite, hexa_design_report ros2_hexacopter_gazebo (this) HexacopterSystem gz-sim plugin, world, ros_gz bridge, launch, headless Gazebo SIL tests ros2_mcu_emulator virtual MCU: GNSS/IMU/encoder error models + the MCU side of the Ethernet link ros2_jetowl_bridge Jetson side of the MCU Ethernet link (jetowl_bridge, sensor_link) — same node on the vehicle

docs.title: Why a C++ system plugin
docs.text:
• Lock-step, zero-latency loop. Sensors, estimator, controller, 12 ESCs and the wrench on the body are computed inside PreUpdate of the same physics step, so there is no transport hop, no thread scheduling jitter and runs are bit-reproducible for a given seed.
  • Electrical time scale. The FOC current loop and the motor's L/R = 1.4 ms need sub-millisecond integration: each rotor runs 20 × 50 µs RK4 sub-steps per 1 ms physics step (240 motor integrations per step). Measured: 20 s of flight simulated in 5.0 s wall-clock (4× real time, 4 cores, incl. start-up), headless.
  • One code base for SIL and the vehicle. The plugin is a thin adapter around ros2_hexacopter_control; the same classes run in the stand-alone simulator used by the unit tests and can run on the Jetson or be ported to the ESC/flight firmware.
  • Gazebo's MulticopterMotorModel models the rotor speed as a first-order lag. It has no dq electrical model, no FOC and no encoder, so it cannot represent "12 BLDC with encoders".

Gazebo version. The plugin targets Harmonic (LTS until 2028). Gazebo Fortress reached end-of-life in September 2026. With ROS 2 Humble, install the OSRF ros-humble-ros-gzharmonic packages.

docs.title: MCU link: sensor topics for the nodes in Source/
docs.text:
On the vehicle the IMU, GNSS and the 12 encoders are read by the flight MCU, which sends them to the Jetson over Ethernet. The plugin is the flight MCU, so with <mcu_link> it also sends those frames over UDP — same protocol, same C encoder — to the Jetson node jetowl_bridge (its sensor_link), which publishes the topics the Source/ nodes subscribe to:

HexacopterSystem (flight MCU)                          jetowl_bridge (Jetson)          Source/
 BMI088 sample used by the FC ─┐                        CRC/seq ─▶ stamp ─▶ covariance ─▶ /imu/data, /imu/data_raw ─▶ ROS2_Control_System,
 12 rotor angles (AS5047P)  ───┼─▶ sensor link ─UDP─▶ encoder Kalman (α-β)           ─▶ /encoders/joint_states      ROS2_Flight_Controller,
 u-blox GNSS model          ───┤   frames (9870)        GNSS gate                     ─▶ /gps/fix, /gps/vel(_cov)    ROS2_Mission_Planner …
 Mahony attitude + variance ───┘                                                      ─▶ /diagnostics
Stream Rate Content (details: ros2_jetowl_bridge) IMU 1 kHz the very sample the flight controller used (one noise realisation for both) IMU description 1 Hz BMI088 noise densities and full scales from hexacopter_physical.yaml encoders 1 kHz 12 × 14-bit counters of the true rotor angle, θ += ½(ω_{k−1} + ω_k)·dt attitude 100 Hz Mahony estimate; tilt σ = 0.020 rad (accelerometer bias / g), yaw unobservable (π²) GNSS 10 Hz NEO-M9N model at the CoM, geodetic origin from gnss_latitude/longitude/height heartbeat 1 Hz 1 ready, 2 armed, 3 degraded (a rotor failed)

hexacopter_sim.launch.py starts jetowl_bridge with sensor_link_sim.yaml (mcu_link:=true, default; fc and vision links off) with clock.mode: passthrough — the virtual MCU stamps with simulation time — and with sensor_fusion:=true also the stack's ESKF (ros2_control_system/uav_state_estimator) on those topics, with the MCU attitude as heading source → /odometry/filtered.
